## highly blessed late Mr. J. W. U. <note>J. W. U. refers to Johann Wilhelm Überfeld (1659–1731), a prominent German mystic and follower of Jacob Böhme.</note>

->To C. U. on April 7, 1685.<-

1. How one should keep the mind <term>Gemüth</term> <note>In this context, the Gemüth refers to the inner soul, disposition, or the seat of the emotions and will</note> free from earthly things, and how one should constantly penetrate through their <term>Turba</term> <note>original: "Turba"; a term used in Böhmean mysticism to describe spiritual turmoil, disturbance, or the "wrath" of the fallen world</note> into God’s heart and will. 2. The author’s own example in this matter.

<image-desc>Decorative initial box containing an ornate script letter, likely 'M', surrounded by floral vines.</image-desc>
My dear brother, I know very well how powerfully earthly things disturb <note>original: "turbiren"; meaning to throw into disorder or confusion</note> one’s mind. At times I have been as if dead; however, I have not ceased to immerse myself back into God with all my might. Under the powerful burden, I have groaned continually and leaned toward divine freedom, which has always supported my weakness so that I did not remain lying prostrate.

<summary>This page introduces a series of extracts from the spiritual letters of Johann Wilhelm Überfeld, beginning with advice on how to maintain inner peace and focus on God despite the heavy burdens and disturbances of the physical world.</summary>

<keywords>Johann Wilhelm Überfeld, Gemüth, Turba, spiritual letters, divine freedom, earthly burdens, immersion in God</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the letter to C. U. dated April 7, 1685, which began on the previous page. The text continues the author's personal advice on spiritual discipline and recounts his own mystical experiences.</meta>

<header>Extracts of the Letters</header>
<meta>catchword: To</meta>

You can do no better than to approach God untiringly with your inner will and desire in every matter, sighing that He might strengthen your heart and give you the power to penetrate into His holy will, so that you may recognize what separates us from our God. And do not let the spirit of this world beguile you, ensuring it does not fill your mind <term>Gemüth</term> <note>In the context of German Pietism and mysticism, "Gemüth" refers to the depth of the soul, encompassing the will, emotions, and inner disposition.</note> with earthly things, which destroys the noble image of God <note>original: "edle Bildniß GOttes"; a reference to the *Imago Dei*, the belief that humans are created in God's image, which mystics believed was obscured by worldly attachments.</note>. God is faithful; He will help you out of every evil, if only you desire Him without ceasing.

2. When I remember the gracious drawing <note>original: "Zugs"; this refers to the "divine draw" or attraction, a common mystical concept where God pulls the soul toward Himself.</note> of God in my soul—how He has drawn me from the very beginning—I stand in great wonder. There was always such an earnest hunger and desire for God in my soul that I could not express my longing in words; instead, I pressed toward God with earnest desire and will, until finally the gates of darkness and death in the soul were burst asunder, and the entrance to God's heart was opened to me. It is impossible to say what joy was then in the soul; I experienced there that God Himself was present in that earnest, anxious desire and will, and thus drew me through that very desire. One must simply not allow oneself to be deterred, but must look the wrath of God right in the eye and wrestle like Jacob <note>A reference to Genesis 32:24–32, where the biblical patriarch Jacob wrestles with an angel and refuses to let go until he is blessed.</note> for as long as it takes to be perceptibly heard: Lord! I will not let you go, unless you bless me <note>original: "HErr! ich lasse dich nicht, du segnest mich dann."</note>.

### To C. U. on September 20, 1686.

1. Through earnest prayer, and faithfulness in the struggle, we can now easily overcome all obstacles of Satan and the spirit of the world within us. 2. How the prayer of a proven warrior comes to our aid therein.

I do not doubt that you will take the kingdom of GOD by force <note>original: "Gewalt anthun"; a reference to Matthew 11:12, "the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force," implying a spiritual intensity required to reach God.</note>, and draw the same to you through earnest prayer. It is indeed true that Satan seeks to constantly lull the mind <term>Gemüth</term> <note>A central term in German mysticism referring to the depth of the soul, encompassing the will, emotions, and spiritual disposition.</note> to sleep, and instills many a doubt regarding the impossibility of breaking through, in order to frighten the soul: but Satan is a liar, and can do nothing other than lie and lead people away from GOD; that is his trade. Therefore, the person who wishes to reach God must by no means hold conversation with the devil, nor give ear to his whisperings, but must oppose him with all earnestness and fight against him; then he must retreat in shame. For he is a powerless spirit, and has absolutely no power over man, unless it be that man voluntarily submits to him. This, however, one must not do; instead, one must overcome him through earnest prayer, so he must be our servant and prisoner, and lie eternally under our feet. I write this knowing it well, and you also—if you will earnestly continue to fight—shall experience it in practice <term>Praxi</term> <note>The lived experience or practical application of spiritual principles.</note>. For the Hero in the struggle and the Breaker of death <note>A common mystical title for Christ, depicting Him as a warrior who shatters the gates of hell and death.</note> has paved the path for us—He who has overcome sin, death, devil, hell, and the world, so that they, praise GOD, can no longer hold us: and He has opened Paradise again in our souls, so that we now again have free access to our heavenly...

<summary>Ueberfeld encourages his correspondent to persevere in spiritual combat, asserting that Satan is a powerless liar who can be defeated through earnest prayer. He emphasizes that Christ has already overcome the world, reopening the "Paradise" within the human soul.</summary>
<keywords>spiritual warfare, Satan, prayer, Gemüth, Christ the Hero, inner Paradise, Johann Wilhelm Ueberfeld, Pietism</keywords>

It is said: *Seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you;* likewise: *Whatever two or three of them ask in my name, it shall be done for them by my Father in heaven, Amen!*

### of the late Mr. J. W. U.
A 4

[... ne]vermore over me; when I cry out, do not hear me. In short, I cannot express with the pen what kind of vows the soul made to her bride <note>In this mystical tradition, the soul is often personified as a bridegroom seeking reunion with "Sophia" (Divine Wisdom), his heavenly bride.</note>, the likes of which a vile beggar or a swineherd should not even be able to make to a queen. See, in such a way the soul was sanctified, and thus went from one level or stair of humility to another; until the **Process of Christ** <term>Proceß Christi</term> <note>A central concept in Böhmean mysticism where the believer must internally mirror the life, suffering, death, and resurrection of Jesus.</note> was completed in her, and her **Great Mystery** <term>Mysterium magnum</term> <note>A term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the divine chaotic origin or "mother" of all beings; the potentiality from which all things are manifested.</note> was graciously entrusted to her, and put on like a wedding priestly robe. For there is a very great danger with the soul, because in her root she leads to the abyss of hell, and can just as easily turn herself into a devil as into an angel: therefore I recognized **GOD’S** process, and willingly gave myself over into his chastisement, so that the soul might afterwards be safe from the devil. As has also happened to me out of **GOD’S** inexpressible grace in his light, putting the devil to shame—however much he stormed against the poor creature—where so many a brave spirit has been overcome by him.

2. Thus you see how the **Process of Rebirth** <term>Wiedergeburt</term> is fulfilled in us. Then **GOD** led us to the "Well of the Living One who sees me" <note>A reference to Genesis 25:11 and the well Beer-lahai-roi, symbolizing divine providence and spiritual vision.</note>, and opened the eyes of our spirit, so that we came into the gift and acquaintance of dear Brother **Gichtel** <note>Johann Georg Gichtel (1638–1710), a mystic who spread the teachings of Jacob Böhme and led a community of "Angelic Brethren."</note> through **GOD’S** providence, and were thus grafted as a little branch into the **Tree of Life** <term>Lebens-Baum</term>, Christ: therein our soul has then come to rest, and become free from the anxious taskmaster, and all this time has heartily refreshed herself therein, as in the Tree of Life, Christ, and has no further seeking outside of herself, because she rests quite securely in the eternal Whole and All; although under very great

### To R. S., July 10, 1694.

### The Earnest Process of Rebirth and the Great Bliss Following It.

If mankind knew what is prepared for them by **GOD**, they would surrender themselves with all the powers of the soul to their **Re-creator** <note>German: *Wiederschöpfer*. A term for Christ, emphasizing his role in "re-making" the fallen human soul.</note> of the new birth, **JEsus**, as is required of a disciple of **CHrist**. One must surrender their will to the very ground of **GOD** and firmly shut the earthly eye of their reason: let **GOD** give, or **GOD** take; let **GOD** lead into heaven or hell, through love or sorrow, through fortune or misfortune: everything must be equal and level to them. This is because **GOD** leads the poor soul through many a sharp fire, so that it may be rid of the harmful poison inherited through **Adam’s Fall** <note>The original sin that, in Böhmean thought, corrupted the "divine image" of man into a "wrathful" or "dark" nature.</note>, and turn from an incarnate devil back into an angel.

This process is often very sharp and difficult, and it would be impossible for any natural powers (even if the strength of all humanity were melted into one) to endure it for a single moment. But to the sanctified will, surrendered to the ground in **GOD**, it is a very light burden and a lovely yoke, because **GOD** is essentially present in that same will, and can carry **mountains of leaden weights** <term>Centner-Berge</term> <note>Literally "mountains of hundredweights," implying an immense, crushing burden.</note> (even if the sins of all humanity lay upon this soul) as light as a feather. Who can truly express these depths with natural words, or recount the temptations of nature and the creaturely self! Until finally, the soul has received its proper **schooling** <term>Schulrecht</term> <note>The formal "right of the school" or "legal standing in school," used here metaphorically to mean the soul has finally learned the lessons of the divine discipline.</note> in the **divine fire**...

<vocab>Wiedergeburt (Rebirth), Wiederschöpfer (Re-creator), Seele (Soul), Adams Fall (Adam's Fall), göttliches Feuer (Divine Fire), Schulrecht (Schooling/Discipline), JEsus (Jesus), CHristus (Christ), Centner-Berge (Mountains of weights)</vocab>

<summary>This letter describes the "Process of Rebirth," a painful but necessary spiritual purification where the soul must surrender its will entirely to God to be transformed from a fallen state back into an angelic one. The author emphasizes that while this "divine fire" is too intense for human strength, God's presence within a surrendered heart makes the burden light.</summary>
<keywords>rebirth, surrender of will, divine fire, purification, Adam's Fall, mystical struggle, Christ as Re-creator, internal alchemy</keywords>

### To C. U. on March 29, 1695.

1. New rebirth, how it initially occurs, and in what manner the newborn child, entirely without its own will, allows itself to be led only by the heavenly mother <note>In this mystical tradition, the "heavenly mother" is Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, who guides the soul back to God.</note>.
2. Its great danger in a false peace, and especially in the ensuing trial by fire <term>Fire-Trial: A spiritual crisis or "testing" where the soul's faith is purified by the "fire" of divine justice or deep internal struggle.</term>, when the dark mother <note>Likely referring to the "mother of nature" or the material world, which tries to reclaim the soul from its spiritual state.</note> reaches for the image; and how it can rescue itself from this.
3. Priesthood of the New Covenant.

You do well that you open the door of your heart to **GOD**, so that His divine light may illuminate your darkness; you will now experience what a horror, monster, and **Behemoth** <note original="Behemoth">A biblical beast from the Book of Job, used here to represent the chaotic, animalistic state of human nature after the Fall.</note>, as a beast of all beasts, we have become in **Adam’s fall**. What deformity the holy name **JESUS**, as He enters the heart again, drives out and crushes. At which the soul itself is terrified, and falls into a deep humiliation and annihilation of itself, into a great repentance, and dares not lift its eyes before **GOD**, because it sees that it has become a dwelling place of devils and all unclean spirits; it sinks so deep into its nothingness that it would gladly become a "nothing": and with that, with its surrendered will, it falls out of the ground of nature into the eternal **Word of GOD**, in which it initially became a creature; and the same Word creates it anew, in senses, will, and desire: which is called the new rebirth. Then it becomes a completely foreign child in this corrupted natural world, of entirely different customs and virtues than it formerly was in its desolate animal life: in which the renewed soul greatly rejoices, seeing that it is now a poor, helpless little worm, and how its own ability and power have been lost; it therefore throws itself entirely into its mother’s

### To C. U., dated Sept. 4, 1696.

1. Departing from the **Love of GOD** plunges one into the utmost danger. 2. Constantly placing the <term>Imagination</term> <note>In this mystical context, "imagination" refers to the soul's power to focus its desire and "form" its internal reality, rather than mere fantasy.</note> into this love overcomes **Wrath**, and endures in all depths. 3. It is the true and only cure for our **Fall**. 4. How one can recover what has been neglected in this regard.

From this you see the danger in which we humans live in this world, standing right on the abyss of hell, such that as soon as we deviate from the **Love of GOD** with even a single thought, we fall prey to the **Wrath** in nature at that very moment.

2. Do not let your hands sink, thinking as if you were struck by **GOD** in the way our human reason supposes. No, it is only the **Wrath**, which is not **GOD**, but rather the <term>Center of Nature</term> <note>original: *Centrum Naturae*. A term from the philosophy of Jacob Böhme referring to the raw, conflicting forces of existence that lack the light of divine love.</note>. We must immediately take refuge in Love and depart with our will from the **abomination of sin**, so that Love may untie the bonds of **Wrath**. Read Luke 13:11–17. The devil would have swallowed us from the earth long ago if we had not taken refuge in Love (which is named **JESUS**). For we could not surrender ourselves to **Wrath**, nor worship it, although we had to feel its blows. And this you must diligently note, and constantly place your <term>Imagination</term> in the **Love of GOD**, so that you may endure in all depths,

### To C. U. on March 26, 1697.

1. After the crucifixion of the external man, and the killing of the body of sin, there follows the struggle with the dragon of <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; refers to the selfish ego or the state of being turned inward away from God.</note> in the human essence. 2. A description of this struggle of the principles in the <term>original source</term> <note>original: *Urkund*; in Böhme’s theosophy, this refers to the primal ground or foundational state of being.</note>. 3. The freedom of the soul’s will in this struggle: and how it can make of itself both a devil and an angel. 4. How necessary it is to immediately press into Love when tempted by the <term>wrath-fire</term> <note>original: *Zornfeuer*; the harsh, consuming aspect of existence that results from being separated from God's light.</note>, if one does not wish to remain a devil despite all outward piety. 5. What kind of fire of purification therefore awaits the half-renewed souls after death. 6. Love, the only spiritual and physical medicine: now the possibility is born to attain it.

Just as you have hitherto had to renounce the vanity and lust of the visible world in your external man, and nail the same to the cross with Christ so that the body of sin might cease: so you must now also go deeper in the spirit with Christ into Hell, and kill the red fiery dragon of <term>self-interest</term> <note>original: *Selbheit*; similar to *Eigenheit*, meaning the obsession with one's own desires and will.</note> and selfhood in the human essence, in your soul; which will now give you entirely new lessons, hidden from your understanding: for our creaturely soul has become, in Adam's Fall, a pure devil, which murders the <term>ground of light</term> <note>original: *Liechtsgrund*; the divine spark or the presence of God's light within the soul.</note>, as the Kingdom of Heaven, within us.

2. Now take note: in our <term>mind</term> <note>original: *Gemüth*; a term encompassing the disposition, soul, and emotional center of a person.</note> both eternal kingdoms, as Heaven and Hell, stand against one another; Heaven to the left (where the heart also has its seat in man) and Hell, together with **GOD's** wrath, to our right side. Now both of these lives are a fire, but qualifying and burning with a great difference. The heavenly fire in the heart burns in the very greatest gentleness, and is **GOD** and Love itself within us: and in the same

## of the late Mr. J. W. U.
### B 5

->To C. U. on Nov. 5, 1697.<-

1. Love is with us in the struggle; therefore we have no power to fear.
2. From where the soul’s rest or unrest [comes] after the death of the earthly body.
3. 4. Their state according to the degree of rebirth <note>original: *Wiedergeburt*; the central Pietist and mystical concept of being spiritually born anew through Christ</note> reached in [this] time; since after death there is no other process than during the body’s life.
5. The form of this anxious process, in which love, as the new body of power, transforms the hell within us into heaven.
6. Exactly which process Christ underwent in our humanity; which we must follow until reaching the age of manhood <note>original: *männlichen Alters*; referring to the "perfect man" or full spiritual maturity in the stature of Christ</note>.

Allow no other idea of **GOD** to enter but Love. This Love does not strike us: and however much your mind is covered by wrath in the struggle, fear no power; though the devil may threaten as he wishes, he cannot harm a single hair: for God, as Love, is with us in the struggle, even in the deepest hells, and helps us to break through the power of wrath and to overcome it. We must indeed suffer its blows in the flesh; but it has its goal, measure, and time, until **Christ** has gained a form within us. As soon as He is revealed, the wrath itself is terrified, because it sees that another is at the foundation <note>original: *im Grunde*; refers to the "Ground of the Soul," the deepest point of human existence where God dwells</note>: and thereby it lets its fierce claim drop, and may no longer inflict any damage upon us; because the divine light strikes it down, whereby a great torment and pain touches it. For the light is its pain and hell, and is just as when **God** grips an evil man’s conscience, whereby he falls into anxiety and unrest and ceases his murdering: so too is it to be understood with the creaturely wrath, as you will surely experience with **God**.

2. Concerning the soul's rest or unrest after the death of the earthly body: this knot <note>original: *Knopf*; metaphorically, a difficult riddle or core problem</note> lies in the deep ground of the knowledge of what **God** and Nature are. For "In the world you have anxiety, but in me you have peace; but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world," says *Christ*. Understand this: if the soul has not put on Christ's body here [in this life], then it stands in its original torment; for the soul in its root is a fire that consumes itself, and its worm cannot die. But when it attains Christ's body, as a heavenly essence, through rebirth, then all its fiery rays are transformed into a gentle light, and out of enmity comes pure love and Paradise.

3. Now, rebirth has its degrees <note>original: *Gradus*; stages of spiritual progression</note>. Those souls who have indeed attained a small beginning of rebirth during their time [on earth], but were snatched away by temporal death while the mind was still burdened with much earthliness—for them, this earthliness stands in the way and is a fiery wall to them, so that the will cannot soar above all creatures into **God**; and they can reach the essence of *Christ*, as eternal freedom, perhaps only with a single glance. There the poor soul stands in the wrestling fire-wheel of eternal nature <note>This refers to a concept from Jacob Böhme describing the soul's restless, driving hunger and internal conflict before it finds rest in the Divine Light</note>, where it has an indescribable torment within itself, until the earthly *Lucifer* <note>meaning the prideful, fallen self-will within the individual</note> has been burned away within it, and the tender spark of love, in which it is God’s image, has become substantial. Within that spark, the soul's will then finds its footing and is in **God**: even if it stood in Hell among all the devils, the location <note>original: *Locus*; the physical or spiritual place</note> could neither harm nor help it.

### To B. v. T. on the 8th of November 1697.

->Without the maintenance of a perpetual fire of light, there is<-
->no divine brotherly love; and without this, no com-<-
->munion with GOD.<-

Divine brotherly love has a quality similar to that in nature between husband and wife, excepting the animal lust of copulation <note>original: *Vermischung*; literally "mixing" or "mingling"</note>, which is an abomination before heavenly purity and chastity. These wedded spirits must carefully observe to always gather pure species <note>original: *Species*; here used in the philosophical sense of "images" or "forms"</note> of love into their imagination, and to fill the lamps of the heart with this oil, and thus maintain a perpetual fire of light. For this must not be extinguished for a single moment: then it is the heavenly tincture <term>tincture: in Böhmean mysticism, a spiritual essence or "dye" that transforms, illuminates, and gives life to matter</term>, and the body or garment of Wisdom—who is the eternally speaking, birthing Word—and the foundation of the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in the believer. From which we can see what a close communion there is between the Godhead and brotherly love; they cannot be separated, but rather mesh together like a clockwork: where brotherly love is the weight that must drive the whole mechanism <note>original: *Werck*</note> and all the wheels, and it is called, as John the Apostle says:
> He who loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how
> can he love God whom he hath not seen?

### To B. v. T. on the 23rd of Dec. 1697.

1. A central description of the process of the **New Birth** <note>original: *Wiedergeburt*; the spiritual process of regeneration or being "born again" in the Spirit</note>, how it begins with great earnestness.
2. What excuses **pious reason** <note>original: *fromme Vernunft*; the intellect that tries to justify itself through religious logic rather than true surrender</note> seeks within us during this process.
3. How **Christ**, the inner man, nevertheless proceeds with the slaughter of all animals <note>referring to the "animal" or "beastly" passions and instincts of the fallen human nature</note> and the sacrifice of the soul to the **Anathema** <note>original: *Anathema*; a Greek term for something "devoted to destruction" or a "curse," here meaning the complete surrender or "cutting off" of the old self</note>:
4. Which is indeed the first ground of self-denial, known as spiritual poverty;
5. But it is not yet the divine **body of power** <term>body of power: *Kraftleib*; in Böhmean mysticism, the spiritual, immortal body that replaces the mortal one as the soul is regenerated</term>, without which the soul is still in great danger of a "misstep in the fire," even for those with the noblest and gentlest temperament;
6. Because of the harsh forms within man himself: how one must pass through these unpleasantly <note>original: *unannehmlich*; meaning one must endure the painful aspects of purification</note> if one does not wish to get stuck in them and turn oneself into a devil.
7. At that first degree, the soul still stands in the **fire-ground** <note>original: *Feuergrund*; the source of the soul's energy and desire, which can be destructive if not tempered by divine light</note>, in the **Tincture of the Sun** <note>original: *Tinctura Solis*; an alchemical/mystical term for a specific level of spiritual illumination where the soul feels its own power</note>, where reason plays with knowledge and, lacking humility, rises above itself.
8. How one can escape such danger and reach the goal as a helpless child in the **heavenly Mother** <note>a mystical personification of Divine Wisdom, or Sophia</note>.
9. That one must not set out on this path merely out of good intentions;
10. Especially not **married people** <note>original: *getraute Leute*; literally "wedded people." Gichtelian circles often held specific views on the spiritual difficulties of the married state</note>. The nature of both wombs, the heavenly and the earthly.

Now God's light shines into our natural darkness; whereby the soul's fire becomes pregnant and eager for the freedom to give birth to God and the Kingdom of Heaven within itself. Thereupon the will of the **mind** <note>original: *Gemüth*; the inner disposition, heart, or seat of the soul's desires</note> arises and gathers itself, by the power of the light, out of all the essences of body and soul into One: in which mighty and great earnestness Christ destroys Hell with all earthly images and false idols within the soul.

->To B. v. T., February 12th, 1698.<-

1. The single point of all our practice is the total **surrender** of the will and of all creaturely self-interest:
2. Without which everything is merely a **fluttering about** <note>original: *Fladderey*; implies a lack of spiritual weight or constant shifting of opinions</note> in opinions.
3. It [this surrender] is tested by GOD to see if it is of the right kind.
4. How one may arrive at this, and thereby unlock a new world;
5. The description, powers, and glory of that world.

This is **proven**: <note>original: *probatum*</note> as soon as the creature does not depart from itself, the Creator does not move in; but the moment the creature departs, the Creator immediately enters and fills the place, etc. And this is the purpose of all our writing, as well as the single point of all our practice: for in our core <note>original: *Grund*; the "ground" or bottom of the soul where God dwells</note> everything must be pure GOD alone, so that not the slightest speck of what is from man remains hidden or left over within us. And nothing remains but for your dear self <note>original: *El.*; likely an abbreviation for *Euer Liebden*, a respectful and affectionate form of address used among German Pietists and mystics</note> to fall on your knees with us and call upon GOD for His Holy Spirit, so that it may be known what GOD has intended for you and wishes to do; whether GOD might ignite your **mind** <note>original: *Gemüth*; in this tradition, the *Gemüth* is more than the intellect; it is the center of the soul's inclinations and will</note> with His Holy Spirit and faith: for with this **priestly adornment** <note>referring back to the "priestly robe" of Sophia mentioned on the previous page</note> one must be clothed, or else it is nothing to subsist in <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Selbheit*; the state of being centered on one’s own ego rather than God</note>.

No <term>animal-man</term> <note>original: *Thier-Mensch*; a person living only according to their fallen, carnal instincts rather than their spiritual nature.</note> is capable of this deep peace and great stillness of the souls; rather, it belongs alone to the children who have led their <term>dragon-beast</term> <note>original: *Drachen-Thier*; a symbol for the selfish, egoistic desires and the "wrathful" nature of the soul.</note> of self-gratification through the sharp fire of God’s wrath in the death of Christ, and have swept it clean from the soul. 

Those others, however, who looked back in this struggle and fell prey to the fire of wrath, will only now find in what a miserable prison they are stuck, and they will have a hard time; and it might offer a sorrowful outlook, unless a little <term>divine spark</term> <note>original: *Füncklein*; the *Seelenfünklein* or "spark of the soul," the tiny remnant of divine light within a human that allows for potential salvation.</note> remains in the inner ground, which may extinguish the devil’s fire. We have drunk the cup and know how it tasted: but they will now have to drink the dregs. 

But we are innocent, because we have wrestled for them beyond our ability and have offered our love so redundantly. Therefore it is better to have stood in the struggle, although it is bitter and heavy, for then one has God with him in the <term>play</term> <note>original: *Spiel*; refers to the "Divine Play" (the *Göttliche Spiel*), the mystical concept of God's interaction with creation and the soul.</note>, who never leaves His own, and at the end rescues and crowns the soul out of all distress.

### To B. v. T., May 26, 1698.

1. Instructions, using the author’s own example, on when sin awakens and becomes sinful: and how the soul can reach eternal freedom outside of nature through this fire:
2. Where all the devil's fires and dark forms of nature are transformed into the light of love.
3. Few souls grasp this point: the reason being the two different <term>mothers</term> <note>original: *Mütter*; in theosophical terms, this refers to the sources of our being—the "earthly mother" of our physical nature and the "heavenly mother" of our spiritual nature.</note> within man.
4. The basis of external fasting, and how far its influence reaches.
5. What true fasting is and what it accomplishes.

You too have been baptized with the <term>baptism of fire</term> <note>original: *Feuertaufe*; a concept from Jacob Böhme’s theology describing a painful but necessary process where God's "fire" purifies the soul of its worldly desires.</note> in the Holy Spirit, and indeed with such a rich measure—like a sea of fire whose floods have constantly cast up all natural impurities and all the idols of false trust in the <term>creature</term> <note>original: *Creatur*; this refers to any created thing or worldly attachment that one relies on instead of God.</note>. It cut so sharply and pressed the heart together so much that the whole world became too narrow for the mind; the outer man felt such pain that I do not believe any torture could be devised that compares to it. Our <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the ego or the "own-will" that seeks to exist independently of God.</note>, however, did not struggle long against the fire of God's justice regarding the false images, but rather laid itself down in the will and itself **cursed** <note>original: *anathematisirte*; to declare something as anathema or spiritually rejected.</note> everything that separates God and the soul from one another. This was done with heartfelt pleading to God to spare nothing, but to thoroughly burn down the devil's entire **stronghold** <note>original: *Raubschloß*; literally a "robber's castle," a metaphor for the ego where the soul hides away from God's light.</note> with everything inside it—**note well** <note>original: *NB.* for *nota bene*.</note>, excepting nothing. This indeed occurred, but it pressed so hard upon the **spirit of the world** <note>original: *Spiritu mundi*; the carnal or worldly mind.</note> in flesh and blood that no counsel was available to us in heaven or on earth, except to surrender body, soul, and spirit into God’s most beloved will; and with that, the creaturely will fell back into the eternal Word of God once more;

# *To B. v. T., May 11, 1699.*
## Transformation of the animal man into an angel, through humble love, as our best medicine.

There is, *Elect* <note>original: *El.*; a common abbreviation in this circle for *Electus* (Chosen/Elect), used as a spiritual title for the recipient.</note>, no better medicine than humble love. This is a <term>tincture</term> <note>In alchemical mysticism, a "tincture" is a spiritual substance capable of penetrating and transforming lower, "base" qualities into higher, divine ones.</note> that can shatter hell: do not let yourself, *Elect*, be led astray or depart from it even by a single point, etc. If you break through in love with God, the Day shall show you in vision the great *Leviathan* <note>A biblical sea monster representing the prideful, untamed ego or the "animal" nature of fallen humanity.</note> as your own animal man—the Devil's fortress of plunder—so that you shall be terrified, and thank God eternally, who has overcome this *Goliath* within you through a power as weak as love. This [nature] must be <term>transmuted</term> <note>A term from alchemy meaning to change one substance into another, here used for the spiritual rebirth of the soul.</note> into an angel within the Light: for it made itself monstrous in the Fall of Adam. Where it was once the playmate and bridegroom of the eternal Wisdom of God, it has become a *Behemoth* <note>A biblical beast representing carnal strength and earthly desires.</note>, and is called the ground of fire or the <term>spirit of the world</term> <note>Latin: *spiritus mundi*; the animating spirit of the physical universe, which binds the soul to material concerns.</note> within us. Therefore, do not be terrified of it, nor spare it: it must be transmuted; otherwise it may not enter the gates of eternal life. What a mystery this is, hidden from many who would rather remain animals than wish to be made into angels. Therefore, seize the <term>full armor</term> <gloss>original Greek: πανοπλία [panoplia]</gloss> of God in prayer: you will surely soon attain victory.

->To S. O. P., July 9, 1699.<-

1. The new body, as the internal divine ground of love, alone is a match for the Cherub’s sword or the sting of sin. 2. And it always emerges from all the oppressions of Satan and wrath with profit. 3. The inevitability of the wrath-forms: and the soul's danger therein. 4. A central description of the state of souls before and after the Fall. 5. Its cure: the penetration of the will into the Mother of Love. 6. How this gate was barred by the apostasy of unfaithful brothers, but opened again through the persistent earnestness of the warriors of Christ. 7. The importance of this gate.

Until the soul has once again put on the heavenly new body, it cannot defend itself against the Cherub’s sword <note>A reference to the flaming sword of the Cherubim guarding the entrance to Eden (Genesis 3:24), which in this mystical context represents the barrier of sin and divine wrath.</note>, which is the sting of sin. And this is the precious victory of the Children of Sophia <note>Divine Wisdom, often personified as a feminine spiritual guide and bride of the soul in Behmenist mysticism.</note> in Christ—a sign of triumph and a knight’s banner—which extinguishes the <term>Turba</term> <note>original: *Turbam*; a Latin term used in Behmenist philosophy to describe a state of spiritual turmoil, disruption, or the destructive power of divine wrath.</note> in the mind and <term>tinges</term> <note>original: *tingiret*; an alchemical term for the process of "tincturing," or fundamentally transforming the quality of a substance—in this case, turning divine wrath into love.</note> the wrath of God. And even if the Devil assaults the noble mind ever so strongly with his hellish elements, and stokes his murderous fire so that the heart becomes anxious, fearful, and pained, not knowing which way to turn: yet the new body, as the essential inner divine ground, is of such power and virtue that it can endure in all fires—whatever they may be named, even in Hell—and nothing can shatter or destroy it anymore.

2. Indeed, Satan may well swallow it, for wrath hungers intensely for love; but love only crushes the dragon’s head within the essence. Therefore, wrath cannot hold it; for love shatters his hell, and henceforth everything for the mind is nothing but pure profit. For regardless of it being the battlefield,

->To S. O. P. on the 19th of Sept. 1699.<-

1. Wisdom in her power and high nobility is closed off from all <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; a central term in German mysticism referring to the ego-driven nature of the fallen human will.</note>. 2. What earnestness and faithfulness are required to become a partaker of her and to remain so.

I have seen with pleasure that you have grown fond of the Wisdom of God, and have a taste for her hidden power and friendliness. And she is also our lovely rose garden, and highest ornament, decoration, and crown of our mind. She is the light and the freedom of eternal Nature, and in herself free from all nature, so that nothing can touch her; and yet she is also firmly attached to the entire bond of eternity, and may not be separated from it, just as fire and light cannot be separated. And because she has such depths in her birth, she is the all-deepest hiddenness, such that no selfhood can ever find her: unless the creature surrenders its "natural right," and dies to its <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Selbheit*; the independent, selfish existence of the "I".</note> in the death of Jesus Christ; then the soul may receive a glimpse and a kiss.

2. But she does not easily surrender herself into the arms of desire; unless the soul has performed its schooling in fire, and has been found faithful and proven in love. God help us! how the soul must here allow itself to be scratched, whipped, and stung by the devil, and yet must by no means [take] in... <note>The text breaks off here; the catchword *nehm-* suggests the word *Annehmung* (acceptance/assumption) or *Anfechtung* (temptation) continues on the next page.</note>

Therein the deep fall of mankind, along with the medicine, is recognized.

What a treasure and wealth the life and the poverty of Christ is, is likely known to none except those to whom it has been entrusted. For as it is an exit from all created things, and a clinging to the <term>Word of the Lord</term> <note>original Latin: *Verbo Domini*</note>: likewise everything that has grown outside of God in selfhood separates itself from this life into its own; and it is a fleeing of the impure from the pure. Thus the <term>poverty of Christ</term> <note>original: *Armuth Christi*; a mystical concept referring to Christ’s total lack of worldly attachment and ego, which the believer must emulate.</note> is the true mirror and the image of the Godhead here in time on earth, as the self-subsistent Wisdom of God; by which everything must be marked and revealed.

Therefore it is called <term>SOPHIA</term> <note>Greek for Wisdom; in this context, it refers to the Divine Wisdom who acts as a teacher and mirror for the soul.</note>. ### To B. v. T. on Jan. 16, 1700.

**1.** How the <term>astral man</term> <note>original: *astralische Mensch*; in the mystical tradition of Jacob Böhme, this refers to the "star-governed" part of the human being—the psyche and instincts influenced by the natural world</note>, after the casting out of the dragon, becomes the bridegroom of <term>Sophia</term> <note>original: *Sophia*; the personification of Divine Wisdom and the spiritual counterpart to the soul</note>: the chasm between the children of **God** and the world. **2.** The cause of all unrest is within us, not outside of us. **3.** In the death of <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the state of being trapped in one's own ego, selfish will, and desires</note> the <term>paradisiacal man</term> <note>original: *paradeisische Mensch*; the redeemed, spiritual human being restored to the state of Adam before the Fall</note> is born: his inner nature and conduct under the pressure of wrath.

<image-desc>A small square woodcut illustration depicting a stone altar or plinth. In the center of the plinth, the letter 'I' is enclosed within a laurel wreath. Above the altar, a radiant sun or divine light shines with long, spreading rays.</image-desc>

You must set the knife to your astral man with great seriousness, and prepare him as a willing sacrificial offering, and cut the throat without any mercy: letting all the beasts howl and cry for their shepherd. And yet, in doing this, we do him no harm at all, but rather only help him away from his **dragon-beast**, who is an incarnate devil and our greatest enemy, whom we carry in our breast, and who is the true Lucifer. When this one is cast out, then our astral man—with the inward <term>light-power</term> <note>original: *Lichtkraft*</note>—is the inward man, and creates the essence in the spirit as the heavenly corporeality: yes, what is more, he is himself the holy <term>fire-tincture</term> <note>original: *Feuers-Tinctur*; the spiritual essence or life-force that purifies and transforms the soul</note>, and Sophia’s bridegroom and husband. And this is the chasm between us and the world, so that no one can come to us unless he dies to his selfhood in the death of Christ &c.

**2.** Regarding the mentioned **inconvenience** <note>original: *Incommodität*; referring to physical discomfort or unsuitable living conditions</note> of your lodgings, the same lesson applies as above. The **location** <note>original: *Locus*</note> does nothing to the matter; even if it were the most favorable opportunity, it should be one and the same to you, though perhaps involving different occurrences and circumstances. All difficulty shall vanish of its own accord as soon as you have truly arrived at the **death of selfhood** <term>Eigenheit</term> <note>the state of being trapped in one's own ego and selfish will</note>. The **obstacles** <note>original: *Obstacula*</note> are within us, not outside us; they are the children of whom **Jacob** had to be entirely deprived <note>a reference to Genesis 42, where Jacob fears the loss of his sons; here used as a metaphor for the soul being stripped of its worldly attachments</note>, a process for which the "old man" <note>the fallen, unregenerate nature of humanity</note> writhes and bends violently.

**3.** When he then renounces all natural rights, he enters into **equanimity** <note>original: *Gleichheit*; a mystical state of indifference to external worldly conditions</note>: love or suffering, sweet or sour, comfort or discomfort, etc., all is straight and even to him; he is content with all things and all people. But here follows the true lesson: henceforth he is a stumbling block and an offense to all people; all his works are led into the fiery **judgment of wrath**, and henceforth he can no longer satisfy the **Wrath** <note>original: *Zorn*; in the theology of Jacob Böhme, this is the "dark fire" or the first principle of nature that must be overcome by Light</note>. There, the sharp fire of wrath presses upon the mind and is a sword that passes through our soul over and over. In this anguish, we can do nothing else but pray for all our enemies and persecutors, and offer ourselves up for everyone as a curse and **anathema** <note>original: *Anathema*; a person or thing accursed or consigned to damnation; here meaning a total self-sacrifice</note> in the death of Christ. In this deep surrender of ourselves, the vision of **eternal freedom** rises within the soul’s mind, and the spirit, in this glimpse of life, breaks through nature into eternal freedom, leaving behind in the fire all selfhood and impurity; it has now become an entirely new creature, and is no longer called the **spirit of the world** <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the governing spirit of the physical, fallen universe</note>, but the **paradisiacal man**.

## To B. v. T., February 8, 1700.

1. Chastisements are a sign of **GOD'S** love: how through these the natural wrath is to be tinctured <note>original: *tingiren*; an alchemical term used here to mean "transformed" or "permeated" by a higher spiritual quality</note>. 2. The fire of love drives the false spirits from us and also kills selfhood <term>Eigenheit</term> <note>the ego-driven nature of the fallen man</note> within ourselves.

Accept this chastisement as a mark of **GOD’S** special love, and a sign that **SOPHIA** <note>Divine Wisdom, often personified as a celestial bride in this tradition</note> takes delight in your soul. As for the bastard children, let them run along without discipline <note>a reference to Hebrews 12:8, suggesting that those God ignores are not His true children</note>. Wait but a little while, and everything in your mind shall become pure sugar <note>a period expression for spiritual sweetness or consolation</note>; all bitterness and anxiety shall become a pure blessing, and wrath shall become a fire-flaming love: for the entire act <note>original: *Actus*</note> is nothing but love. **GOD** knows our weakness well, and occasionally grants an hour of refreshment so that the outer spirit receives a ray of light and can catch its breath; however, we must not remain resting upon that, but rather prepare ourselves for a new process. But in everything, keep **Jesus Christ** in your memory—that is, in your imagination <note>original: *Imagination*; in this context, it refers to the soul's power to inwardly visualize and form itself into the image of Christ</note>—as pure love. In this way, you will soon tincture your natural wrath with it, so that the entire depth of your mind becomes a pure essence of love; then the wrath of **GOD** must lose all its right and claim over you.

2. ### To B. v. T., April 2, 1700.

### The difficult state of souls in hours of temptation: and
### how they may happily emerge from them.

I rejoice in my spirit that you are beginning to understand the serpent-language <note>The "serpent-language" refers to the deceptive, rationalizing, or seductive thoughts that tempt the seeker away from spiritual purity.</note>: for although it sounds very pleasant, and in its outward breath seems neither good nor evil, it nevertheless carries deadly poison beneath its tongue. This Satan has often disguised himself among us as an angel of light and promised "golden mountains" <note>A common German idiom for promising great wealth or impossible things.</note>; but we have closed and plugged our eyes and ears against him, flatly rejecting everything. Even if you, beautiful god of filth <note>The author uses "Dreckgott" (muck-god) as a derogatory term for the devil or the false spirit of the material world.</note>, could give us the highest bliss and the very heaven (where God and the holy angels dwell), we would still not accept it from you, but would rather dwell in hell with our King of the Cross <note>Refers to Christ in His suffering.</note>. 1. The birth of Love and its great power in the internal and external. 2. How earnestness and serenity can stand together. 3. The process of becoming free from one’s own will, and the resulting blessedness.

Thus, whatever distress or danger I encountered, I merely stared with the eyes of the mind—that is, the eyes of the will—steadfastly into the revealed Wisdom and **Sophia** <note>In Böhmean mysticism, Sophia represents Divine Wisdom, the feminine counterpart to the Divine.</note> in the heart. ## To B. v. T., April 20, 1700.

1. The shortest way to become perfect and to be rid of the dragon of self-will. 2. Why GOD must come to the aid of the inner growth of the soul through the Cross. 3. The ease of becoming a child of GOD, and why so few nonetheless achieve it.

It is very comfortable for the soul when she allows the inner Spirit to govern and lead her, and she can attain great perfection in a short time. For she loses nothing of all her effort and labor, great or small, but rather everything she does, whether internally or externally, is pure gain; whereas, on the contrary, the person acting in self-will <term>Eigenheit</term> is a much greater martyr to themselves, and gains absolutely nothing with all their running and racing; instead, folly shines out of all their deeds before GOD and men, and they are an inconstant, confused wheel, running from one uncertainty into another, in pure delusion. ## To B. v. T. on May 22, 1700.

1. Love endures through the trial by fire <note>original: *Feuerprobe*; a common alchemical and mystical metaphor for the suffering or testing that purifies the soul.</note>, and rectifies the animalistic monstrosity of the *spirit of the world* <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the astral or worldly influence that governs the physical body and lower desires.</note> within us.
2. The state and danger of those who do not endure this trial:
3. Who, even with all outward piety, are—like Adam after the Fall—yet only slaves of the *spirit of the world*.

You could do no better than to close your eyes to sensuality <note>original: *Sinnlichkeit*; the focus on physical senses and worldly desires.</note> and to transform your senses with Love; thus you shall learn to dwell in the fire without pain and burning: and you shall perceive a truly noble fruit within you, which shall gladden you; for in this school one learns *essentially* <note>original: *essential*; meaning learning through the very essence of one's being rather than through external study.</note> what one will never experience from the outside. It is the salt which seasons the *spirit of the world* <note>original: *Spiritum mundi*</note> in us, so that it becomes an entirely different creature—no longer an animal which must be led by a bridle and tamed with whips, and yet remains only an animal born for beatings, which kicks out at its driver: in which animalistic monstrosity we all, for lack of the divine fire, would have had to remain standing outside the inner heavens and their inhabitants. Therefore, lift up your spirit by this word; you will in due time, when GOD shall unlock the closed *principles* <term>Principia</term> <note>The fundamental spiritual realms or dimensions of reality, often categorized into dark fire, light, and the physical world.</note> within you, experience more than we are permitted to put to pen: because it is the opened seal through which the devil's throne in man is entirely shattered, so that he knows not where to hide; but the divine light, as the Virgin of Wisdom <note>A central figure in mystical theology representing Divine Sophia, who guides the soul back to God.</note>, exposes him everywhere.

2. Therefore, everything that does not endure the trial by fire, and shrinks back before the Cherub <note>The guardian of Paradise; here representing the threshold the soul must pass through to enter the divine realm.</note>, attains the

1. The danger of the sensory ground: how the speaking of lies by Satan is to be overcome therein. 2. The intrusion of wrath carries a false tincture <note>original: *Tinctur*; in Boehme’s mysticism, this refers to a spiritual essence or transformative quality that "colors" the soul's state.</note>: the light of love reveals it immediately, from the slanderer’s own words. 3. ### To B. v. T., July 12, 1700.

1. Interaction with women is the very hardest trial for a beginner; 
2. Even the best **temperaments** <gloss>original: *Complexionen*; the physical and psychological makeup of a person</gloss> among women are no exception: it is an anxious and long-term process to burn away the **monster**. 
3. How one can become certain of the **will of God**.

---

It is one of the very hardest trials for a beginning student, the interaction with women, until our tincture <note>original: *Tinctur*; in Boehmian theosophy, this is the spiritual essence or "inner color" of the soul that must be transformed from a worldly to a divine state.</note> is sanctified and wedded by **God's Wisdom** <note>Referring to "Sophia," the personification of Divine Wisdom who acts as the spiritual bride for the seeking soul.</note>, and is found to withstand the tempter. For in social circles, the entire weight presses upon our minds from all sides, and things go difficultly until we accustom our neighbor’s "beast" <note>referring to the fallen, animalistic nature of human beings</note> to the proper harness. There, in particular, the **Matrix** <note>original: *Matrix*; here meaning the generative spiritual principle or "womb" of nature, which the author views as a site of intense spiritual danger and temptation.</note> of women is a cruel, monstrous creature, where all the cunning of the serpents cannot be recounted or expressed when Satan stirs the fire in the abyss. All of this then stands in the mirror of our mind, as if in the tincture, where one must then indeed sweat <note>meaning to undergo intense spiritual labor or agony.</note>.

2. A simple, good heart certainly has much of an advantage over a deceitful, false person who is a vessel in Satan's hand and can perform much evil with it. Nevertheless, all of Eve’s children, begotten of flesh and blood—whatever good mind or <term>temperament</term> <gloss>original: *Complexion*; the balance of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) that determines a person's character</gloss> they may have—possess a **monster** on and within themselves. This monster fights against holiness, purity, and chastity, and must be refined and purified only through divine fire. This does not happen without great temptation from Satan, which no one knows except he who has been in the **furnace of affliction** <note>A biblical reference to trials (Isaiah 48:10) that act like a blacksmith’s furnace to remove impurities from the soul.</note> himself. For no beast is able to enter the kingdom of heaven, and our conduct already here on earth [must be] in the heav-

### To C. B. K. on July 27, 1700.

->How difficult it is for the <term>fire-ground</term>, as the selfhood of nature, to surrender itself to God in the <term>light-ground</term>.<-
<note>original: *Feuergrund* and *Lichtsgrund*; terms from the mystic Jacob Boehme. The "fire-ground" represents the soul's raw, ego-driven energy and desire, while the "light-ground" represents divine peace and selfless love.</note>

IT is entirely certain and true: if we would only let ourselves be led by God in the inward ground with the simplicity of a child and surrender to Him, we would quickly find the trail and the right path of eternal life within us. But this sickness is a universal poison with which most are infected, even as they progress; when the sealed gates to the inner world open within the <term>mind</term> <note>original: *Gemüth*; the seat of the soul's will and spiritual perception.</note>, the soul always falls into a selfhood within the fire-ground and clings so firmly to these chains that it refuses to let itself go further toward God. Instead, it believes—as Boehme <note>Jacob Boehme (1575–1624), a German Christian mystic whose complex ideas about the nature of God and the soul heavily influenced this writer.</note> notes—that the divine light (which burns without such sharpness and fiery power, and works only in pure gentleness without strong sensations in the outer man) is a false light. This is caused by the rule of the *Spiritus mundi* <note>original Latin: "spirit of the world"; the force that governs the material, temporal universe and the physical body.</note> within us, as its life is nothing but pure selfhood; if it is to abandon this, it feels as if its very soul is being taken away, and yet it must hunger and waste away within its own selfhood. Therefore, God is sometimes forced to bring the soul into great distress and embarrassment and to cast down this dragon <note>A metaphor for the stubborn, grasping ego or the prideful nature of the fallen soul.</note>, so that the soul may finally surrender its dark <term>natural right</term> <note>original: *Natur-Recht*; here meaning the soul's claim to its own autonomous, selfish existence.</note> and give itself over to God.

### To I. C. P.

1. Total surrender of all self-will is the means to attain the little pearl of the love of GOD.
What a struggle this costs; and yet how easy it is. 2. Herein stands the <term>test</term> <note>original: *Proba*; a trial or proof, often used in alchemy and metallurgy to test the purity of a substance.</note> of all spirits.

Pay close attention, dear one, and mark it deep in your <term>mind</term> <note>original: *Gemüth*; the seat of the soul's will, desire, and spiritual perception.</note>: the little pearl of the love of GOD is precisely the prize for which there has been dancing and wrestling at all times. Everyone wants to kiss this bride gladly and embrace her in his arms; and she also gladly communicates herself to all creatures as long as the creature walks in humility. But she does not easily give herself into the marriage bed and the arms of desire with the soul, unless it first undergoes its <term>process</term> <note>original: *Proceß*; in this context, the mystical journey or "alchemical" transformation of the soul through suffering and refinement.</note>, which is exceedingly hidden and strange and wonderful to reason.

But if the soul can surrender its own will and let Love do with it what she wants—even let herself be cast into hell and dwell in the midst of devils—then the soul, through the fires of <term>purification</term> <note>original: *Leuterung*; a term for the purging of the soul's "selfhood" or ego.</note>, becomes as thin as a nothingness according to its own self-nature. Then it may pass in and out through all powers unhindered, into the inner gentle element to Christ, her helper.

But there lies the difficult knot: she must dwell in hell without anger or doubt. If she fails in this, the soul does not reach the <term>element</term> <note>The "Gentle Element" or "Fifth Element" in Böhmean thought, referring to the heavenly reality or the "Light-world" of God.</note>, but remains stuck in the birth as a raw, flying <term>fire-spirit</term> <note>original: *Feuergeist*; a soul that has been awakened in its own power but has not yet been softened by Divine Love, resulting in pride and bitterness.</note>, full of evil poison and blasphemy. For such a one, there is no counsel and no peace to be made; it must only return to the original birth, and the soul must die away to its dragon. For the <term>Virgin</term> <note>original: *Jungfrau*; referring to Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, who represents the pure, heavenly image that the soul lost at the Fall.</note> never gives herself to the <term>fire-worm</term> <note>original: *Feuerwurm*; a derogatory term for the selfish, prideful, and unrefined soul-fire.</note> as his property, even if the soul flies out over all thrones; there is no other counsel, it must simply be born anew. For

### To B. v. T. on the 7th of August, 1700.

->What the calling, work, and reward of the outer spirit are, regarding the inner economy of the Virgin with the soul.<-

Your practice until now has been to penetrate into the <term>heart</term> <note>original: *Gemüth*; in this mystical context, it refers to the seat of the soul's will, desire, and spiritual perception, rather than just the intellect.</note> to lay a firmer foundation, which is both good and right; yet it remains hidden from you that everything else—the entire outer man—is trying to force its way in to find rest there. God permits this for a time, until the heart has become so firm that it can no longer stray from Him. At that point, God will assign you a new practice and lesson: to completely wean your outer spirit and appoint it as a cattle herder over your animal senses, where it may perform its daily labor. Meanwhile, the <term>Virgin</term> <note>original: *Jungfrau*; a reference to "Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, who in Pietist mysticism acts as the celestial bride to the human soul.</note> shall first break through in the heart and, together with her bridegroom—the soul—manage their inner <term>economy</term> <note>original: *Oeconomie*; a term for the management or ordered arrangement of a household, here applied to the spiritual life.</note> and household within the heart. The outer man is to know nothing of this, but must instead dwell only in the cattle stall among the beasts; he shall, however, be illuminated by the rays of the Virgin from time to time, though not persistently. Because this discourse is still too deep for you at present, we wish to bring you into God and foster your growth through prayer.

the Virgin <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, a central figure in this mystical tradition representing the pure, heavenly mirror of God</note> is surrounded by Cherubim and Seraphim. We also help with all the strength of soul and spirit to wrestle against the <term>wrath</term> <note>original: *Zorn*; the spiritual force of judgment or the "dark world" that seeks to claim the soul</note>; indeed, if it were possible, we would gladly take our brothers' struggle upon ourselves, so that God’s wrath might seek its due upon our own souls. But it cannot help the soul [of the brother]; it must be dipped into the fire of wrath and leave behind everything that arose from <term>Adam’s Fall</term> <note>The biblical event of the first sin, which mystics believed introduced a "self-centered" desire into the human soul, separating it from the divine</note>. For Paradise is eternal freedom outside of nature, and it allows not a single speck of impurity within itself. Thus you may see, dear brother, what our work and play is within the wonders of God. All people could partake of this grace, if they would only abandon their <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the egoistic will or "me-centeredness" that creates a barrier between the individual and God</note> for a moment and hold still before the eternal Word. For nothing plagues us but our own will—that is our hell.

2. Therefore, test all spirits; you will find this sickness fundamentally throughout. And where one should fight this enemy within oneself, one turns outward against one's brother, [claiming] he is the one who did it. And we should be able to have peace, if we only (God forbid) did not also hold onto the sting in the foundation <note>original: *stich im Grund*; a lingering point of resentment or a hidden root of the "self-will" in the depths of the soul</note>. Therefore, we bear the <term>marks of Christ</term> <note>original: *Mahlzeichen Christi*; likely referring to spiritual stigmata or the visible signs of a life lived in "imitation of Christ," including suffering and humility</note> on our forehead of the natural man, so that many may be won and raised up from within. This is not difficult for us, because it is not the capacity of our selfhood, but the powers of Love that sustain and lead us on this path of life.

### To C. B. K. on Aug. 9, 1700.

<margin><unclear>Across the...</unclear></margin>
1. The second Principle is the true middle way: how it is to be attained.
2. In what manner the Author therein came to full mastery over the <term>spirit of the world</term> <note>original: *Spiritum mundi*; the astral and elemental force that governs the physical realm and human psychology</note> and to the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: *Mysterio magno*; the primal "chaos" or divine source from which all things were manifested</note>.
3. The first and third Principles, in their highest beauty, still only give birth to the <term>solar tincture</term> <note>original: *solarische Tinctur*; a high spiritual state of enlightenment that, while pure, can still be co-opted by the ego or "the devil"</note>, which the devil can well endure.
The reason for the discord among the godly of today.

When I look back, I also still remember the hours in which my mind was exactly as yours is now; that is, my soul was in love, but in a deep prison, such that an entire Principle stood between her and her love. If I could have shattered it with my <term>own-will</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the self-centered desire that separates the soul from God</note>, there would have been no fire so hot that I would not have willingly let my body be burned in it; everything else in this world was to me nothing but hellish fire. I also bravely cast off my self-will against this <term>cornerstone of stumbling</term> <note>A biblical reference to Christ or divine truth that causes the ego to trip and fall</note>. For everything the soul does—be it a fiery earnestness in the first Principle, or a <term>serenity</term> <note>original: *Gelassenheit*; a state of yieldedness or letting go of the self</note> in the third Principle—is all merely a work of the creaturely selfhood, and is called going too near or too far, wherein the <term>spirit of the world</term> <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*</note> stands with its governance. But until this outer shell is broken, and the soul is freed from this regent, the <term>spirit of the world</term>, she is unable to reach the middle way, which is the second Principle. In this Principle, the properties stand in equality, where the fire is Love, and the surrendered will is not a rest or standstill in the flesh, but is the burning wick with the flame or light of love. In as far as the soul now walks in the denial of the creaturely [self], according to that degree the second Principle becomes manifest, but only in the inward ground.

2. Yet, amidst such spiritual poverty and self-denial, in which I stood for many years with the deepest resignation, the soul is not able to completely rid itself of the **spirit of the world** <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the astral and elemental force that governs the physical realm and human psychology</note> during this [earthly] time. It retains its seat in the **sidereal reason** <note>original: *siderische Vernunft*; in Jacob Böhme’s philosophy, this is the intellect that belongs to the stars and the natural world, capable of worldly logic but blind to divine truth</note> and leads the soul into doubt and uncertainty. Therefore, I held fast to the inner ground or **Principle** <note>original: *Principio*</note> which is called the self-denial and poverty of Christ. Within this, my mind was also enlightened, so that I saw my salvation some years prior—and yet my **animal man** <note>original: *thierischer Mensch*; the physical, instinctual self driven by natural biological impulses</note> knew not how—until I brought to an end a cycle, as an **age** <note>original: *Seculum*</note> or eye of my life in **rebirth** <note>original: *Wiedergeburt*</note>. At that point, my free will had to choose or elect: either to establish itself firmly in the world, or to surrender itself entirely, body and soul, to the invisible God. After I successfully accomplished the latter, amid diligent wrestling and the subduing of the sensory man, the Wisdom of God—as **SOPHIA**—appeared to me personally and substantially in the mind (the radiance, power, and taste I cannot express). She unlocked for me the treasure chest of the **Great Mystery** <note>original: *Mysterii magni*; the primal source or "chaos" from which God manifests all of creation</note>, so that my faith was granted all its sustenance, completely substantial and more certain than if I had held it in my hand. She also imprinted upon my heart and revealed to me the spirit and conduct of dear Brother G. (whose condition was indeed known to me from afar, that it was poverty; but I did not know the **Mystery** <note>original: *Mysterium*</note> [behind it], but only what is called being poor through chance). And this **SOPHIA** has never departed from us, nor has she deceived us, but in all trials has been Yea and Amen, never Nay. She is also the bond of our spirit-

3. As for the two contrary Principles, insofar as the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the governing spirit of the physical and astral realms</note> rules within them; it should be noted that even if they manifest themselves in their extreme beauty within the mind through the **Tincture of the Sun** <note>original: *Tinctura Solis*; in theosophical alchemy, this is a high natural light of the intellect or soul which, while beautiful, is still part of the created world rather than the divine essence</note>, the mind cannot rest upon them. If it enters the fire, it is a false light that does not endure, but only brings the person into pure fickleness. We sense it immediately by the "taste," however artfully it may hide itself; it is instantly revealed before the inner holy Tincture. This is the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil** <note>referring to Genesis 2:9</note>, and the greatest poison, from which most people today eat their death. The inner Tincture, however, is **Paradise** <note>original: *Paradeis*</note>, in which Adam stood before the Fall, and where he should have desired nothing outside of himself. And this has been perfectly born again on earth through the **Process of Christ’s Humanity** <note>the mystical path of following Christ's life, death, and resurrection within one's own soul</note>. This also creates the greatest enmity and aversion among the "pious" of today—namely, the eating from these two different Tinctures. Therefore **Satan** cannot tolerate us at all, but proclaims us to be sorcerers and **false Magi** <note>original: *falsche Magos*; practitioners of deceptive spiritual arts</note>, and the greatest enemies of **Christendom**. This is caused by eating from the **Tree of Life**; the Devil cannot tolerate this at all here in his supposed kingdom. He will gladly permit everything else, and even praise a person for their piety, as long as they only

stuck in the **Tincture of the Sun**.

## To C. B. K., August 31, 1700.

1. How one can escape the mistakes of the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the governing spirit of the physical and planetary realm</note> within us. 2. The danger and damage to the soul if it does not return to the inward ground; 3. The excellence and depth of that ground. 4. It is not salvation to have God only for oneself; rather, one must ignite and refresh oneself in the brothers: without this, the powers of light remain hidden.

Simply hold your soul in the dearest will of God, and you will experience how God's growth proceeds from within, entirely hidden from the outer **astral man** <note>original: *astralischen Menschen*; the part of the human being influenced by the stars and the physical cosmos</note>: who meanwhile must deny his own will and learn, like the prodigal son, to consider himself unworthy to be called a child. For it is very dangerous in this state to play with the light, because the **Principles** <note>original: *Principia*; the three fundamental forces of reality in Behmenist philosophy: the dark fire, the divine light, and the outward world</note> manifest so strangely, as each one casts out its own light in the mixture of good and evil; and if a person does not have the **Separator** <note>original: *Separatorem*; an alchemical and mystical term for the power of discernment that divides the pure from the impure</note> within them, they can very easily make mistakes, just as these births [of error] lie open nowadays. Therefore, let your eye turn only inward, and you will be able to quiet your spirit until the hidden seed of the **Eternal Word** has become flesh and blood and pierced through the dark veil of the flesh. Then the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*</note> must follow behind and be subject to the virginal branch; for now he is master in the "wrath," and covers the mind with his arrogant realm in nothing but pain and **torment** <note>original: *Quaal*</note>, so that the mind must surely be afraid.

2. There is yet another lesson behind this, which is much deeper: namely, that our **fire-soul** <note>original: *Feuerseele*; the core of the soul which, without divine light, is a consuming fire</note>, once it has tasted the **little pearl of light** <note>original: *Lichtperlein*; a term for the first spark of divine wisdom or grace</note within itself, wants to use it to enter into lust and **spiritual adultery** <note>original: *geistliche Hurerey*; the misuse of spiritual gifts or "sweetness" for selfish emotional pleasure rather than for God's glory</note>; there-

### To B. v. T. on October 2, 1700.

->The heavenly fire burns only the creaturely self-will, without whose death no spirit can reach God.<-

It gladdens me to hear that God baptizes you **essentially** <note>original: *essentialiter*; meaning in the very substance of your being, not just symbolically</note> with His heavenly fire: without this, you would be dead and nothing according to the inward life. Therefore, take comfort in the great grace that befalls you; the painfulness is only the **creaturely self-will** <term>original: *creatürliche Eigenheit*; the egoistic nature of the created being that stands in the way of God</term>, which **putrefies** <note>original: *putreficiret*; a term from alchemy and mysticism referring to the "rotting" or breaking down of the old self to allow for new life</note> and must decay. Until this death has occurred, the soul’s spirit cannot ascend from the **fire-ground** <note>original: *Feuergrund*; the deep, energetic source of longing and power in the soul</note> and travel toward heaven; which happens through the **eighth form of fire** <note>referring to a stage of spiritual evolution beyond the seven natural properties</note> into the **Tincture** <term>original: *Tinctur*; a spiritualizing power or "dye" that transforms the soul's darkness into divine light</term> and the **paradisiacal world**. Therefore it is said: one must serve one's apprenticeship in the fire <note>original: *Schulrecht im Feuer thun*; to undergo the rigorous testing and purification of spiritual fire</note>, which proceeds **essentially** <note>actually and substantially</note>. Thus you can understand our heartfelt prayers, how they pass through all **three Principles** <term>original: *drey Principia*; the three realms of existence—the dark fire-source, the light-world of God, and the physical/outward world</term>, namely from the outer into the inner, where the **boundary mark** <note>original: *Scheideziel*; the point of separation or judgment</note> is in the first Principle, where impurity is consumed in the fire; before this, the spirit cannot reach the gates of the second Principle. Only wrap yourselves firmly in love, so that

->To *C. B. K.* on October 18, 1700.<-

### How wrath, as an **opposite** <note>original: *Contrarium*</note>, benefits our inward growth and reveals love.

To drive forth and ripen the inward growth, there is no better means than the **opposite** <note>original: *Contrarium*</note> and the foundation of hell: the dark and poisonous "No" of wrath. This is the revelation of all heavenly powers and virtues, wherein it becomes known what is good—namely, **GOD** and eternal love alone. For every **idea** <note>original: *Idea*; in the Platonic or Böhmean sense of an eternal archetype</note> in the light has its **opposite** in the darkness. As soon as that same opposite in the darkness is provoked by the adverse **creature** <term>original: *Creatur*; referring to the lower, self-willed nature of a human being</term>, immediately the **idea** in the light becomes manifest and is born out within us, which previously was unknown even to itself, like a nothingness. And these are the heavenly wonders from which the great song of praise arises, in which the holy angels rejoice.

## To R-t. on October 28, 1700.

1. Great importance of the struggle of the two eternal principles <term>original: *Principien*; in this mystical tradition, these refer to the two fundamental forces of God: Love/Light and Wrath/Darkness</term> within man.
2. Adam fell within this struggle; and we too must be tested in it.
3. The cause and purpose of all divine chastisement <term>original: *Kasteyung*; spiritual discipline or suffering intended to purify the soul through self-denial</term>.

I see with great joy how God has ignited your spirit in our heavenly little spark, in such a way that the two eternal principles <note>original: *Principia*</note>—of God's Love and Wrath—are truly active and in conflict within you. This is an exceedingly high grace, of which not one in a thousand becomes a partaker. These two central fires <note>original: *Centralfeuere*; the inward spiritual energies at the core of a person's being</note> are actually the creaturely divine breath, our essential soul <note>original: *essentiale Seele*</note>, the original eternal birth. From these, in the temperament <note>original: *Temperatur*; a state of perfect balance where opposing spiritual qualities no longer conflict</note>, the heavenly tincture <term>original: *Tinctur*; a term borrowed from alchemy referring to a spiritual essence that can transform and "color" the soul with divine properties</term>—as the true, holy, divine fire, SOPHIA <note>original: *SOPHIA*; the Greek word for Wisdom, often personified as the bride of the soul</note> and Paradise—rises up and is born. In whatever man this birth does not exist, he is but an animal. And it is easy to imagine, from the severe forms of the original source, what a powerful thing the new heavenly body must be; because Love, in opposition to Wrath, stands in equal balance, as she draws her essence from the severe forms to feed her fire-burning. Thus, pure powers and heavenly essence are revealed in the out-birth as our new body; which is then also unbreakable and firm, so that it can dwell in hell without burning, and transmutes <note>original: *transmutiret*</note> hell itself into nothing but Paradise and delight, also treading upon the head of the hellish dragon. And it means a great deal, to whom God entrusts this struggle. If the soul does not break through in Love, it becomes exceedingly hard and shackled in Wrath, where the soul stands in greater danger than an ignorant, natural man; for the soul stands right in the dark
