### To B. v. T., February 9, 1701.

1. The new **body of power** <note>original: *Kraftleib*; in Böhmean mysticism, this refers to the spiritual, celestial body that a believer develops within their earthly frame</note> must be a match for Satan in all **three principles** <note>original: *Principien*; these are the three realms of existence—the dark fire-world, the light world of God, and the external world of nature</note>, especially in those external things that seem insignificant; 2. Regarding the **essence** <note>original: *Wesenheit*</note> of the new body hidden within the external body; its opposite is the serpentine body of **selfhood** <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the state of being turned toward one's own selfish will rather than God</note>. Everything in the **new birth** <note>original: *Wiedergeburt*</note> depends upon the **tincturing** <note>original: *Tingirung*; an alchemical term for the spiritual transformation or "coloring" of a substance into a higher state</note> of this latter body.

You see upon which feet we stand, and from what essence our inward body has grown, such that it must be a match for Satan according to all three principles: otherwise, one thinks that everything external is a worthless, minor matter; and it is precisely there that Satan first takes advantage of people, as we have examples where, when we have given a good warning from a good heart, we were despised out of pride.

2. For this is a **mystery** <note>original: *Mysterium*</note>: although we must already die and decay according to the external man, there is nevertheless a hidden power in the external body which is the deepest mystery in the new birth, and for which the earthly **matrix** <note>original: *Matrix*; the formative or "womb-like" principle of nature that seeks to manifest spiritual reality</note> hungers so greatly. This power is immortal, and is the very substance of the new body. When this is lacking, the **paradisal man** cannot become manifest; instead, the soul draws to itself a false body from the **fire-ground** <note>original: *Feuergrund*; the fundamental, often wrathful or chaotic root of existence</note>, which is a **monster** <note>original: *Monstrum*</note> in comparison to the true likeness of God. And so stand most of the pious in our time; where, instead of this **paradisal idea** <note>original: *paradeisische Idea*; the original, perfect blueprint of humanity</note>, the evil beast of selfhood sits at the foundation. Therefore, understand: this pearl of which we report is the contrary of the earthly serpentine body. Whoever knows how to **transmute** <note>original: *transmutiren*</note> this, so that the first divine likeness is born from it, he has outside of himself

->To B. v. T., February 22, 1700.<-

### Comparison of the Works of the Surrendered Will and of Selfhood.

One must be amazed at what **selfhood** <term>original: *Eigenheit*; the state of being focused on one's own selfish desires rather than God's will</term> can endure and suffer; if a person, in a **surrendered will** <term>original: *gelassener Wille*; a central concept in German mysticism referring to "Gelassenheit" or the yielding of one's ego to God</term>, were to take but a tenth part of that burden upon themselves for Christ's sake, they would be found a brave warrior before God. But whatever selfhood does, there is no **constancy** <note>original: *Fixität*; an alchemical term used here to describe spiritual stability or a permanent state of being</note> in it; whereas what the surrendered will does is unbreakable and eternal—today, yesterday, and in the future the same, without change.

The basis for the distortion of Holy Scripture.

3. Thus there is a distinction: first, between lighting a fire from coarse and damp materials <note>original: *Speciebus*</note>, which must certainly be blown upon strongly; or second, maintaining a lamp with pure, clear oil, which latter may be called more a light than a fire; although it contains the root of the fire within itself, it is nevertheless entirely governed by the light. So God also dwells only in the light: but the fire is the strength and revelation of the light, and is called **Nature**; but the light is the freedom above and outside of Nature, in which **Paradise**, **Majesty**, and the **Kingdom of Heaven** stand.

## To B. v. T. on the 14th of June 1701.

->Without dying, the little pearl <note>original: *Perlein*; a common Pietist metaphor for the "Pearl of Great Price" or the divine spark within the soul</note> will not be born forth;<-

The fact that your soul <note>original: *Gemüth*</note> is beginning to fade away from writing is a sign that the grain of wheat <note>A biblical reference to John 12:24: a seed must die in the earth to bring forth fruit.</note> is beginning to decay, out of which a new life, better than the first, is born. For everything with and in us must pass through death, and in that dying, our little pearl is born forth.

The soul now stands in the eternal wonder, in Wisdom <note>Often referring to *Sophia*, the personification of Divine Wisdom</note>, to God's eternal praise, within the Mystery <note>original: *Mysterio*</note> of God. May God give the Holy Spirit to your heart as a ruler, so that you may take certain steps: you will experience God's wonders and, along with us, become a song of praise to God.

->To B. v. T. on the 7th of August 1701.<-

1. In the death of the sensual life <note>original: *sinnliches Leben*; the life governed by physical senses and worldly desires</note>, the true life is revealed as the pure, holy element. 2. Before the soul reaches the marriage to Sophia <note>Divine Wisdom, viewed in this mystical tradition as the celestial bride of the soul</note>, it must be freed from its dragon-beast and all disgust in the fire.

All the wells of the sensual life were stopped up, so that it could not speak or utter a single word more, and saw no other way before it but to surrender itself, inwardly and outwardly, to the sufferings of Christ: in which death the true life has been revealed; in which, even to this hour, we are a "death" to all [worldly] reason, etc. At first, I could not find my way in this myself, until God's light broke through within, in which we see that everything is pure grace of God, which thus keeps us standing: if this were to withdraw, it would be over for us, as it is with all flesh. It is the inner holy element in which we live and move <note>original: *wallen*; implies a pulsing or flowing spiritual movement</note> according to the inner man. Who can change God's will and purpose? Our outer man is dead for the sake of the inner man and has surrendered himself to the inner; for he is also a co-witness of grace, because he was also a beholder of the hidden wisdom.

2. The Virgin <note>Wisdom/Sophia</note> does not give herself to our souls for a matrimonial union <note>original: *eheliche Conjunction*; an alchemical and mystical term for the unification of the human spirit with the Divine</note> immediately, but only in the [initial] desire: for if the soul gets but one glimpse, it rises up in its fiery power and wants to overwhelm the Virgin with the dragon-beast <note>The "dragon" or "beast" represents the egoistic, aggressive nature of the fallen soul</note>; which then must be locked up anew as a Behemoth <note>A biblical beast from the Book of Job, used here to symbolize the untamed, monstrous animal nature of the self</note>, so that it does not rise outside and above its domain. Who can depict the inner form of the fallen souls with earthly words? It is a mystery <note>original: *Mysterium*</note>

### To D. O. S. on October 27, 1701.

1. Love is revealed through its opposite, the fire of wrath; in which the soul must perform its **school-discipline** <term>Schulrecht; in the mystical tradition, this refers to a period of spiritual testing or "schooling" where the soul must prove its legal standing or maturity through trial</term> and overcome. 2. The foundation of **predestination** <note>original: "Prädestination"</note> and the **election of grace** <note>original: "Gnadenwahl"</note>, which is recognizable only to the reborn: wherein lies the great power of both love and wrath.

Observe dearly and deeply that the hidden divine love, in its power and virtue, cannot be revealed except through its opposite: the greater the first is, the more poisonous and deadly is the latter. These two **central fires** <note>original: "Centralfeuere"</note> are the true dividing line, and they mark the end of nature; transforming a natural person into a divine, heavenly person. For nothing can enter into GOD unless it has performed its school-discipline in the fire, and has overcome the fiery dragon (which is our outer spirit) together with the **Cherub** <note>A reference to the angel with the flaming sword who guards the entrance to Paradise</note> of the creaturely wrath of GOD. Here the hidden poison and the abyss of our heart must be clearly brought to light: for in this conflict of principles, where love and wrath stand before us as creatures and entice us, there is a sympathy, where one likeness rebukes and awakens the other. And if a person understood it rightly, it is the greatest grace of GOD that can befall us; because the soul can, at one stroke, reach the hidden pearl as the foundation of perfection in **Christ** <note>original: "CHristo"</note>, and be rid of the outer spirit.

2. However, the **Great Mystery** <note>original Latin: "Mysterium magnum"</note> lies deeply locked away here, as does the tangled knot of predestination and the election of grace. Specifically, wherever the soul's will reaches—either toward the gentleness in the light, then it makes an angel of itself: or toward the sharpness in the fire, then it makes a devil of itself.

<summary>Überfeld explains that divine love is only revealed through the "fire of wrath," a spiritual trial the soul must endure to move from a natural to a divine state. He frames the choice between light and fire as the core of predestination, where the soul's own will determines whether it becomes an angel or a devil.</summary>

But since everything that is to endure in **God** must be fortified anew—which cannot happen without trial—it has been found that until this hour no one has been able to reach their former standing; not to mention that some have completely reignited themselves in the fire of wrath and spew such poison into other souls <note>original: "Gemüther"; refers to the inner disposition or seat of the emotions</note>. For what wrath once seizes, it does not easily let go: for it is the bond of eternity, and it requires great earnestness.

But we do better to break our own will here in this time, so that we may reach the gracious Virgin and bear fruit with her, and not depart from here empty.

### To J. C. P. on November 18, 1701.

1. The mighty difference between the external and internal <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctur"; in theosophical thought, this refers to a spiritual essence or transformative "dye" that colors and animates the soul</note>: how far both reach, and where they lead.
2. After overcoming one's own will, the external [tincture] becomes subject to the internal.
3. The great danger to souls in the <term>Solar Tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctura Solis"; a spiritual state associated with natural or solar power which, while impressive, can lead to pride or temptation if not balanced by divine grace</note>, as seen in Adam's and our own experience.

The solar <term>Tincture</term> shows us only the narrow gate of life: in such a way that my spirit was drawn upward for perhaps eight to ten days, standing in constant <term>contemplation</term> <note>original: "Contemplation"; deep, prayerful meditation</note> of the <term>magical birth</term> <note>original: "magischen Geburt"; the mystical process of being "born again" in a spiritual sense</note>. I found myself standing on the great broad way of this world, and before me was an exceedingly narrow gate or door; to enter which I still had to take a significant step: yet these [natural] forces could not bring me there, because they were not at all sufficient. I was, however, filled with great joy and songs of praise, and I fixed the envisioned gate of life as a goal in my mind, and surrendered myself to God’s guidance and <term>direction</term> <note>original: "Direction"</note> from within: I also <term>advanced</term> <note>original: "avancirte"</note> from day to day very perceptibly in the inner powers, and rejoiced in the approaching redemption from nature and the <term>Spirit of the World</term> <note>original: "Weltgeist"</note>. And although this external sun shone upon me, I was not at ease with it, and did not <term>reflect</term> <note>original: "reflectirte"; here meaning to focus or rely upon</note> upon it, regarding it as suspicious; since the spirit led me into great temptations with women, so that I had to use great earnestness and make a covenant with God, surrendering myself to Him in body, soul, and spirit, as His own property: on the other—

### To B. v. T., December 3, 1701.

Infinite blessing upon our growing into one another in faithful brotherly love; something that all self-centered growths must do without.

We can each best view ourselves in the mirror of the other according to our inward form, as one light ignites another, and nothing may remain hidden that is not awakened. And there is a growing into one another, and one spirit in many. However, everything that grows and runs in its own self-interest <note>original: "Eigenheit"; literally "own-ness," referring to the ego or the state of being focused on oneself rather than God</note> cannot save itself from the dark realm of <term>Fantasy</term> <note>original: "Phantasie"; in this mystical context, it refers to deceptive mental images or false spiritual imaginations that lead the soul astray</note>: and remains in its forming and making a foreign growth, which is not recognized in God's Eye of Light. And because God revealed the <term>Mystery</term> to me from the very beginning—that powers exist in the light alone—I have bound my spirit firmly to this fire of brotherly love: I have also found it steady and true in all trials, and experienced that all of Satan's art, however violently he attacks the <term>Mind</term> <note>original: "Gemüth"; a complex German term referring to the seat of emotions, soul, and disposition</note> with his poison and wrathful fire <note>original: "Grimmenfeuer"; the "fire of fury," a term for the harsh, judgmental aspect of nature or the divine when separated from love</note>, is unable to extinguish it; yet I have seen enough of how easily he has miserably overcome and scattered <note>The text ends mid-word with the catchword "streu-", likely for "zerstreuet" (scattered).</note> others who did not take heed of this bulwark—

For instead of Love using the fire-ground <term>fire-ground</term><note>original: "Feuergrund"; a term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the raw, energetic foundation of the soul which must be transformed by divine light into Love, or else it becomes a hellish fire.</note> to form its powerful, strong image—bringing forth its otherwise hidden powers within it as its tool and bringing them to light—the apostate creature lies in contradiction, entangled in the forms of darkness, where it can no longer reach the birth of the Light. From this arises envy and malice, which GOD will cut off and give to the fire to consume, because it is a foreign wood <note>Metaphorically, "foreign wood" refers to the worldly attachments or the "old self" that provides fuel for the wrong kind of fire.</note> which we have carried for nearly eighteen years, almost to death.

Thus, everything must penetrate through the sword of the *Cherub* <note>Referring to the flaming sword of the angel guarding the entrance to Eden (Genesis 3:24), representing the "cutting away" of the ego required for spiritual rebirth.</note>; otherwise, the doorkeeper lets no one in. Here, no scolding or animalistic contention helps; the door is firmly shut. May **GOD** assist us with His Holy Spirit!

### To B. v. T., April 28, 1703.
#### In what manner the inner man increases continually, until reaching full stature.

We can tangibly feel this growth, and how much we have increased each year in the grace and powers of the inner man <note>The "inner man" is a concept from Pauline theology, central to Pietism, referring to the spiritual self that is regenerated through Christ.</note>. Thus must your wood on the Tree of Life also become strong, and the wrath reveal the love <note>In theosophy, "wrath" (Zorn) is the raw, fiery energy of nature that, when yielded to God, becomes the foundation for "love" (Liebe).</note>: which is an essential growing of the powers; and this occurs when love beholds itself in the counter-image of wrath, and in joy eternally thanks **GOD**, who has rescued her [the soul] from the kingdom of hell and made her into an angel in heaven. This essential joy then permeates all forms of the soul’s inner and outer nature, so that they all may taste of it and have their nourishment from its fixed <term>fixed</term><note>original: "fixen"; in alchemy and mysticism, "fixed" refers to a state that is stable, permanent, and no longer volatile or easily lost.</note> sweetness. Thus, they can not only endure the devil's blows and assaults from within, but also become eternal enemies to all the falsehood of wrath: until the little tree, shaken by many storms, pain, and torment, becomes fruitful and brings forth fruits of eternal life, for which purpose we were planted.

---

->To B. v. T. on Jan. 22, 1704.<-

### Why one should not trust their own good intentions in external occurrences without consulting with the brothers.

I wish to suggest this much for your future notice: that, according to my humble feeling, you would have been fortunate if you had simply stood by the offered fifty <term>guilders</term> <note>original: *Gulden*; a common currency in early modern German territories.</note>, without letting a word of change be noticed. In that case, the <term>spirit of the world</term> <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; in this mystical tradition, it refers to the clever, transactional, and ego-driven mindset of secular society, as opposed to the Divine Spirit.</note> would have had to defeat itself, and in its <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the ego's attachment to its own will and desires.</note> would have cast you out of the <term>lodging</term> <note>original: *Logement*; refers to a rented room or apartment.</note> itself; then you would have emerged with a victory. Notwithstanding this, the entire course of events with the <term>landlady</term> <note>original: *Hospita*; the woman managing the house or lodging.</note> in the house would be excusable, provided you had only brought your encounter to Brother G.’s attention <note>Brother G. likely refers to Johann Georg Gichtel, the spiritual leader of this circle.</note>. Then the matter could still have been <term>remedied</term> <note>original: *remediren*; to fix or set right.</note>, because the brother would have advised you to wait until your lodging was actually rented out. There is no doubt about your good intention, and that you were without malice in not telling the brother; however, the spirit of the world makes use of our foolishness just as well, to make us <term>act precipitously</term> <note>original: *präcipitiren*; to rush headlong into a decision without reflection.</note>, and thus trip us up. None of our brothers have understood these steps; therefore, they have stumbled everywhere, whether out of good intention or in anger,

In this, diligently guard yourselves against even the slightest anger, so that you do not bring any foreign blemish into the Mother and spoil your birth: this is where wayward children have failed and plunged themselves into the wrath of GOD.

->To B. v. T. on the 26th of April, 1704.<-

> The best means to ripen one’s inner growth is to hold oneself to love and to embrace the new goal of the Virgin: her nature, law, and divine power. <note>The "Virgin" refers to Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, representing the pure spiritual mirror of God.</note>

You can best ripen <note>original: *maturiren*, from the Latin *maturare*.</note> your inner growth the closer you hold yourself to the light of the Sun, which is Love. Through this, the chamber of anguish <note>original: *Angstkammer*; in this mystical tradition, "anguish" refers to the initial, constricted state of the soul before it is illuminated by divine light.</note> in the mind becomes paradisiacal and gives off an exceedingly bright and powerful tincture <term>tincture</term> <note>In spiritual alchemy, a "tincture" is a transformative essence or spiritual force that changes the quality of whatever it touches.</note>; this preserves us from any collapse during all crosses and adversity, and in all trials, it brings forth God in Trinity and Wisdom within our spirit. 

And because the Virgin has set up a new goal and banner in the fire-ground <note>The "fire-ground" (*Feuergrund*) is the deep, energetic foundation of the human soul which must be transformed from a consuming fire into a light-flame.</note>, which bears the inscription that no self-will shall ever reach her again in eternity, and is now called a resigned will <note>original: *gelassener Wille*; a central concept meaning a will that has surrendered all personal desire and ego to God.</note>; so must the fire-soul renounce everything it has ever possessed, whether spiritually or physically. This goal or banner is the holy Cross of Christ in the fire-ground, upon which the self-will must die and become a humble, resigned will, which is recognized as a bridegroom of Sophia. 

This birth of the cross <note>original: *Creuzgeburt*.</note> is a truly noble sign and a fruit of our twenty-year-long, rigorous birth of anguish, granted to us poor worms in humanity out of undeserved grace—which the devil, by interrupting the first birth, was forced to advance in the divine counsel <note>original: *Raad*.</note>. This growth is now quite holy; only dig diligently in the spirit: when you find it, you will rejoice in it eternally, and [you will bind] all evil beasts—whether it be prestige before the "pious world" or whatever it may be—to this trunk of the cross...

Y 2

...been adopted into the divine marriage, and brought forth again with [labor] pains, as the Virgin <note>Referring to Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, who in this mystical tradition is the spiritual bride of the soul.</note> shuts out the [earthly] intellect from within; this is a crown of the inner man, which no one attains except those who have grown beyond the fire of Satan and are endowed with the heavenly fire, wherein you should understand us essentially <note>original: *essential*.</note>, etc.

3. We cannot let ourselves out of our Principle <term>Principle</term> <note>original: *Principio*; the foundational spiritual reality or "ground" in which the soul dwells.</note> to reach them (our blood relatives), because the chasm between the two is too great, until they, having become exhausted in the spirit of the world <note>original: *Spiritu mundi*; the temporal, external life governed by earthly desires and the senses.</note>, meet us from within; this requires a great length of time and a long period <note>original: *Periodus*.</note>. Thus twenty years passed with my brother-in-law before his spirit was recognized from within: despite the fact that he expressed himself quite well through charitable deeds, GOD nevertheless kept Himself closed off until he reached the point where GOD was moved. For the outer life in the spirit of the world is a very firm castle, which costs labor and strife until the soul unwinds itself from the constellations <note>original: *Gestirn*; in the mystical tradition of Jacob Boehme, this refers to the astral or planetary influences that bind the natural person to the physical world.</note>: these people never reach that point on their own, unless they are taken up by the children of Christ into the eternal dwellings <note>original: *ewige Hütten*; a biblical reference to the spiritual home of the righteous.</note>, and even then they do not know how it happens to them.

->Of the late Mr. I. W. U.<-

### To B. v. T. on April 26, 1704.

*The best means to ripen one's inner growth is to hold fast to Love and to embrace the new goal of the Virgin: its quality, law, and divine power.*

Your inner growth can be best ripened the closer you hold yourselves to the Sun’s light, which is Love: whereby the chamber of anguish <term>chamber of anguish</term> <note>original: *Angstkammer*; in Boehmian mysticism, this refers to the soul's internal state of tension and conflict that must be overcome to reach divine light.</note> in the mind becomes paradisiacal and gives off an exceedingly bright and powerful tincture <term>tincture</term> <note>original: *Tinctur*; a spiritual essence or transformative force that changes the quality of the soul.</note>; which protects us from any failing in all suffering and adversity, and in all trials births God in Trinity and Wisdom within our spirit. And because the Virgin <note>Referring to Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, who acts as the spiritual guide and bride of the soul.</note> has set up a new goal and banner in the ground of fire <term>ground of fire</term> <note>original: *Feuergrund*; the deep, energetic root of the soul's nature.</note>, which bears the inscription: that no self-will shall ever reach it in eternity, and is now called a "resigned will"; so must the fire-soul renounce everything it has ever possessed, whether spiritually or physically: this goal or banner is the holy Cross of Christ in the ground of fire, upon which the self-will must die, and become a humble, resigned will, which is recognized as a bridegroom of Sophia. This birth of the cross <note>original: *Creutzgeburt*.</note> is a most noble sign, and a fruit of our twenty years of severe birth of anguish <note>original: *Angstgeburt*; the painful process of spiritual transformation.</note>, given to us poor worms in humanity out of unmerited grace, which the devil was forced to promote in counsel <note>original: *Raad*; suggesting that even the devil's opposition served God's ultimate plan.</note> by breaking the first birth. The growth is now quite holy; dig diligently for it in the spirit: when you find it, you will rejoice over it eternally, and all evil beasts—whether it be the esteem of the "pious" world, or whatever it may be—at this stem of the cross...

->To B. v. T. on June 7, 1704.<-

1. How in the school of the heavenly Mother <note>Referring to Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, who in Gichtelian thought acts as the spiritual educator of the soul.</note>, after the first children’s A B C, the Book of the Three Principles is learned; and how this first truly helps us onto our feet.
2. What disaster is caused in this school by "flying" <note>A metaphor for spiritual pride or jumping ahead to advanced mystical states before one is ready.</note> and by seeking one's own comfort.

You have certainly had your childlike years of play until now: during which, as often as we think of it, we have always wished to receive your spirit with open arms into our school, to leaf through and recite with us the living, powerful A B C book of the spirit, which consists of three pages; then our joy shall be complete. Our dear Mother has indeed, as we see, made strong preparations <term>preparations</term> <note>original: *Präparatoria*; introductory exercises or spiritual disciplines.</note> for this, and had you diligently recite the A B C board <note>A "hornbook" or simple wooden tablet used to teach children the alphabet; here used metaphorically for the basics of faith.</note>, in which the very same letters are to be found as in the aforementioned book. There is, however, a difference: in the first, the spirits of the letters, such as consonants <term>consonants</term> <note>original: *Consonantes*; here representing the rigid, structural forces of nature.</note> and vowels <term>vowels</term> <note>original: *Vocales*; representing the divine breath or animating Spirit.</note>, run together. By the consonants, we understand the forms of eternal and temporal nature, as the spirit of the first and third principles <term>principles</term> <note>original: *Principii*; Jacob Boehme’s term for the three realms of reality: the dark fire-world, the light-world of God, and the visible world.</note>; but by the vowels, we understand the highly precious and noble key of the great mystery <term>great mystery</term> <note>original: *Mysterii magni*; the divine source or "chaos" from which all creation emerges.</note>, which is the Spirit of GOD Himself, according to the second principle. When this rises as a growth in the soul-fire <term>soul-fire</term> <note>original: *Seelenfeuer*; the energetic, burning core of the human soul which seeks the "light" to find peace.</note>, it distinguishes the forms of nature, so that every quality makes an eye or principle for itself, and there is no longer any confusion, and yet they dwell close by...

<summary>This letter uses the metaphor of a schoolroom to explain how a believer progresses from the "A B C" of faith to understanding the complex "Three Principles" of divine and natural reality. It warns against spiritual pride and explains the relationship between the structure of nature (consonants) and the Spirit of God (vowels).</summary>

...together, and in one another, and none exists without the other; the heavenly tincture <term>tincture</term> <note>original: *Tinctur*; in the alchemy of the soul, this is the transformative spiritual essence that turns the "lead" of dark nature into the "gold" of divine light.</note>, however, is the light that shines through the dark nature. Therefore, you will only then truly look back and see what your struggle has been from the beginning, and that you are nothing foreign or separated from God. This will truly help your spirit onto its feet in a righteous way, when you perceive, in your will and desire, the power of light as a guide toward the kindled divine fire of love, against all the grasping of Satan in dark nature. Into this fire, as into the divine fire, you can bring all your offerings and prayers, and they shall be received without rejection <term>rejection</term> <note>original: *Repuls*; a refusal or being pushed back.</note>.

2. Therefore, all this time, we have clung to the Spirit alone, apart from nature and the creaturely, yet we had to remain barren and could bring nothing to birth, because the Virgin <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, often depicted in this tradition as the spiritual bride of the soul.</note> no longer wished to smell or look upon the apostate nature of the soul, according to the first and third principles <term>principles</term> <note>original: *Principio*; referring to Jacob Boehme's system where the 1st principle is the dark fire of God's wrath, the 2nd is the light of love, and the 3rd is the material world.</note>; until, through all the degrees of birth, we finally came under God’s guidance, when after exceedingly great divine patience, the apostate branches were finally cast into the fire. 1. How one might most easily and safely pass through the external tribulations <term>tribulations</term> <note>original: *Tribulationen*; trials or great afflictions.</note> and temptations of the spirit of the world <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the collective consciousness and astrological influences of the material world that distract the soul from God.</note>: a secret <term>secret</term> <note>original: *Arcanum*; a hidden mystery or a spiritual remedy known only to initiates.</note> from the inner school of wisdom.

I have seen what has happened to you regarding the watch <note>This likely refers to a literal obligation for civic or military guard duty, which the recipient found spiritually distressing or conflicting.</note>. These are external exercises by which one beast bites the head off another; therefore, you cannot come away more free or light than if you desire to be nothing in spirit and nature in your selfhood <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Selbheit*.</note>, except what God, the eternal Word, wants to make of you. The spirit of the world, though stupid in itself, yet Satan is a cunning serpent within it, who understands our nativity <term>nativity</term> <note>original: *Nativität*; the specific astrological and elemental makeup a person is born with, which dictates their natural temperament and weaknesses.</note> and can mockingly read all the planets to us <note>A metaphor for how spiritual enemies use our own natural inclinations and "fate" to manipulate us.</note>, so that if we do not always keep the eye of our mind turned into Christ into the "Nothing" <note>original: *ins Nichts*; a central concept in Böhmean mysticism referring to the *Ungrund* or the divine void where the human self is extinguished to let God act.</note>, we always fall short and must "lose a feather" <note>original: *eine Feder lassen*; a German idiom meaning to suffer a loss, be damaged, or come out of a fight worse for wear.</note>. This is just as we observed in Freher <note>Dionysius Andreas Freher (1649–1728), a prominent German-British commentator on Jacob Böhme’s work and a contemporary of the author.</note>, who wanted to make himself strong in his self-centeredness during such external temptations, but always received such blows that he became confused and had to run away; and when he saw himself thus overcome, he conversely <note>original: *contrair*.</note> attacked our spirit with the spirit of the world <note>original: *Spiritu mundi*.</note> in anger, to suppress it through his perverse desire, so that it was much harder for me to balance this spirit with love from within than that external one

### To B. v. T. on August 19, 1704.

->The present throne of the Virgin, after leaving the fire-ground,<-
->and in what manner the Principles are thereby brought back<-
->into a divine harmony.<-

This temperament <note>original: *Temperatur*; in mystical thought, this refers to a state of perfect balance where no single quality dominates the others.</note> of the life-forms stood in the beginning in the fire-ground <term>fire-ground</term> <note>original: *Feuergrund*; the first principle of existence in Böhmean theosophy, representing the harsh, consuming, and energetic root of life and God’s "wrath" or strength.</note>, from which, however, the divine Virgin <note>original: *göttliche Jungfrau*; a reference to the Divine Sophia or Heavenly Wisdom, a central figure in Christian theosophy representing the mirror of God.</note> withdrew herself, turning the fire into a darkness after the first birth from the fire let in Satan. Through this, a confusion indeed arose, yet Satan could not achieve his purpose, even though he moved heaven and earth. Because of this, the formative powers of God in the external world stood still for a time; however, during that time, God generated for Himself a new growth in our internal ground, which has endured through all the storms of the Devil. 

And after the little boy <note>original: *Knäblein*; this refers to the "New Man" or the Christ-child born within the soul of the believer, a common Pietist and theosophical metaphor.</note> reached his years, the Virgin broke forth with him in the light-ground <term>light-ground</term> <note>original: *Lichtsgrund*; the second principle, representing God’s love, light, and the kingdom of heaven.</note>, where she now fashioned her throne and sent her son out to us into our nature of the first and third Principles <term>Principles</term> <note>original: *Principia*; the three "worlds" or levels of reality: 1. the dark fire-world (wrath), 2. the light-world (love), and 3. the external material world.</note>. There he now rules as a king in all three Principles, and with the lower principles as his strength and power, he powerfully ignites the light—acting as his mother—and there is a constant inclination of the lower forces toward the heart of God. That is to say: the Principles stand in a harmony, in which the divine Trinity <note>original: *Dreyheit*.</note> eternally rises.

<meta>This page continues the extracts of letters from I. W. U. (Johann Wilhelm Überfeld), an associate of the mystic Johann Georg Gichtel. Following the previous page’s discussion on the "Divine Virgin" (Sophia) and the inner "New Man," this extract focuses on the practical necessity of communal prayer to reclaim the divine spark from the "dragon" of the fallen nature.</meta>

header: of the late Mr. I. W. U.

### To B. v. T. on Sept. 30, 1704.

1. How one may obtain the Holy Spirit through united prayer: without which the overcoming of the dragon and the restoration of the divine image is impossible; 2. And without this, the dragon remains ruler, even with the most lovely and gentle outward appearance.

In response to your esteemed [letter], there is little to reply except what has dawned in my spirit, and what God Himself drives: namely, childlike prayer and entreaty for the gift of the Holy Spirit. For with this pledge <note>original: *Pfand*; referring to the Holy Spirit as a "guarantee" or "earnest" of salvation as per Ephesians 1:14.</note> you must be strengthened and sealed, should you march into the field against the dragon <note>The "dragon" represents the fallen, selfish nature of man and the influence of the Devil.</note> and stand firm in the battle against him. Therefore, take hold of your spirit in the word of promise in **Matthew 18**. *Whatever two or three agree upon, whatever it is they shall ask, shall be given to them.* This is the **divine tinder**, in which the **heavenly fire**—when we strike it with the steel of our desire upon the hard stone of our impressed and locked-up **center** <term>center</term> <note>original: *Centri*; in Böhmean theosophy, the *Centrum Naturae* is the inner core or "root" of a being where the divine or dark principles originate.</note>—immediately catches; as experience has brought to us, and as you also shall come to know.

2. ### To B. v. T., Jan. 8, 1705.

1. The divine **fire of love** <term>fire of love</term> <note>original: *Liebesfeuer*; in Böhme’s theosophy, this is the transformative power of God's grace that turns the soul's dark "fire" into light.</note> burns in the light and makes the path of the **dragon** <note>In this mystical tradition, the "dragon" symbolizes the fallen, selfish nature of man or the devilish influence within the soul.</note> completely pure; 2. Through whose rebellions in the darkness the fiery earnestness of souls is sharpened. 3. The author's experience with unfaithful suitors: how love bore itself during this and finally cast out the dragon. 4. How one can now attack him with fire, and what kind of **little wreath** <note>original: *Kränzlein*; a common metaphor for the spiritual reward or crown of victory given to those who persevere in faith.</note> follows the earnest struggle. 5. Some incidents with a **failed brother**; from which it can be seen what the dragon is in human nature, and how those who do not wish to let go of him do not belong to the **children of Wisdom** <note>Referring to "Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, a central figure in Christian theosophy representing the mirror of God.</note>. 6. This dragon has been worshipped as God from the world's beginning, but is now discovered and cast out; hence the separation and strife between brothers and brothers. 7. The more the inner man increases, the more circumscribed the outer interaction with other people becomes.

Whereby you, moved in the very deepest foundation of the **soul** <term>soul</term> <note>original: *Gemüth*; refers to the heart, mind, and deepest inner disposition.</note>, will burst all locks and seals: so that then the central divine fire, once struck, may henceforth no longer be extinguished, but can burn clearly through all its forms; whereby the **gates of the deep** <note>A metaphor for the profound spiritual dimensions or the "foundations" of existence.</note> are open, and a constant passage through the fire into the light has been prepared for your **will-spirit** <term>will-spirit</term> <note>original: *Willengeiste*; the faculty of the soul that directs one's desires and intentions toward God.</note>. Therefore you may now well use earnestness, and storm the dragon with fire; the **Turba** <term>Turba</term> <note>original Latin: *Turba*; in the mystical tradition of Jacob Böhme, this refers to the spirit of confusion, disorder, or the destructive wrath of God that breaks things apart.</note> is gone from the fire-forms: the Virgin shall now meet your will and, after earnest wrestling, set a little crown upon your head—namely, the gracious light of the **Confirmation** <note>original: *Confirmation*; here referring to a spiritual sealing or internal strengthening by the Holy Spirit rather than the church rite.</note> of the Holy Spirit, which shall set your calling fast and unlock your entire conduct, etc. etc.

5. He, **Freher**, had once laid a half-sheet of paper on my table, in which **Satan** revealed himself completely naked, as therein he declared war against me with fire and sword, with powder, hail, and bullet. Which letter, after I had read the top lines, I brought to his chamber and pointed out that he was stepping entirely outside of **Christ's** rule <note>original: *Christi Regel*</note>, who commanded us to give our lives for one another, and not to kill. Whereupon he fell to the ground in a faint, turning as pale as a sheet under my hands; and when he was helped into bed, I said: "See, my brother, you give birth to such poison that you yourself must faint from it; therefore consider how it must taste to me." Thereupon he broke out into these words: "May **GOD** take me away and join another soul to you in my place, who can walk like you, and with whom you can bring forth fruit." I replied that love desires no separation; he should only die to his self-will <term>Eigenheit</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; literally "own-ness." A central concept in this circle referring to the selfish ego or the "me and mine" that separates a person from God's will.</note>, then we would be equal to one another. Wanting to be "Something" and "Nothing" <note>original: *Ichts und Nichts*; mystical terms where "Ichts" is the created "Something" or self-identity, and "Nichts" is the divine "Nothing" or still eternity.</note> creates the inequality; for I am aware of nothing in my own self-will, but rather that **GOD** is the willing and doing of my spirit; why then should he cause himself so much torment in his self-will? Whereupon he uttered (in despair): "I seek death, and I cannot find it."

1. In fraternal communal living, it is not a matter of natural compatibility and yielding, but rather of surrendering one’s self-will to the ground of light. 2. Herein, an inexpressible wrestling between the qualities of Love and Wrath emerges, from which the basis of predestination becomes clear; 3. And how, for many, their knowledge serves only to increase their misfortune.

Thus I revealed and pointed out to him many times that if I were to surrender my inner ground into his <term>complexion <note>original: *Complexion*; the specific mixture of spiritual and physical temperaments.</note></term>, we would indeed be good natural brothers, but we would not withstand the struggle with the dragon; instead, we would have to return to the world, since it would only be the <term>spirit of the world <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*.</note></term>, which we—praise **GOD**!—have overcome, and such a life would be our death. # Of the Late Mr. J. W. U. <note>original: *des sel. Herrn I. W. U.*; "sel." is an abbreviation for *seligen*, meaning "blessed" or "of blessed memory," a traditional way to refer to the deceased. We are without guilt and warn you: if you are not truly in earnest, do not blame us afterward. We are soldiers <note>original: *Kriegesknechte*; literally "war-servants."</note> in God's outposts <note>original: *Vorlogen*; likely a variant of *Vorposten*, meaning front lines or advanced positions.</note> against the dark world and its inhabitants: we cannot do otherwise than be faithful to our army commander **Christ** <note>original: *Christo* (Latin dative/ablative form).</note>; even if no human being should follow us.

### To B. v. T. on March 26, 1705.

->One must not seek to make one’s affairs right with words from the outside, but inwardly with God and in the Light, which alone is a match for Satan.<-

You have extended yourselves almost too far outwardly into the **spirit of the world** <term>Spiritum mundi</term> <note>original: *Spiritum mundi*; the "spirit of the world" or the temporal, earthly influence that distracts the soul from its eternal source.</note>, which is not our **principle** <term>Principium</term>. NB.**—inwardly in God, wherein they are preserved, and no enemy can ever break them; in which our covenant with God also stands, and our foot is freed from being tripped by the enemy. The fire-ground <note>In this theology, the "fire-ground" is the raw, consuming energy of the soul. If not illuminated by God's Light, it becomes a hellish "darkness."</note> must be enlightened and softened by the Light; otherwise, it is a darkness and a pure **opposition** <term>Contrarietät</term> to the Light: what is "Yes" in the Light is "No" in the fire-ground, and **vice versa** <note>Latin: "and the other way around."</note>; it fails in everything. Therefore, let your practice be the **consecration** <term>Anathema</term> <note>original: *Anathema*; while often meaning a curse, in this mystical context it refers to the Greek sense of a "votive offering" or "sacrificing" the self-will to God.</note> and the offering up of the soul in the blood and death of Christ for all people, as we do: thus you will have the birth of Light within you, which will bind the dragon.

### To B. v. T. on August 9, 1705.

1. The outer tincture is fundamentally contrary to love and full of offense. 2. The love of God cannot be offended by anything. 3. Man is his own maker. 4. Comparison of the spiritual priesthood and the apostleship of our time.

My brother S., I hope that God shall also bless our work, so that He may prevail through the **spirit of the world** <note>original Latin: *Spiritum mundi*; the animating spirit of the physical, material universe.</note>, and may reach the **balanced temperament** <term>Temperatur</term> <note>In Böhmean mysticism, this refers to the "Temperamentum," the perfect harmony of the spiritual qualities where no single element dominates the others.</note> in the spirit: for the outer **tincture** <term>Tinctur</term> <note>An alchemical term meaning the essential quality or "color" of a substance; here it refers to the outward spiritual manifestation of a person's soul.</note> has never appeared more distasteful to me than precisely within his spirit. It is a powerfully rough nature, which resembles Esau in the Scriptures, upon whom the pious Isaac, his father, was mistakenly focused and remained stuck. <note>The author references the biblical story of Isaac and his sons Esau and Jacob to illustrate spiritual states; Esau often represents the "natural" or "earthly" man.</note> And it is the **ground of wrath** <term>Zorngrund</term>, and no love; it defends itself against love with all its might, and will not let it in, nor surrender itself to it. Outwardly, the outer tincture also burns in the **fire of wrath** <term>Zornfeuer</term>, and takes offense at external things, which are nevertheless outside of us: for instance, for twenty-one years we did not know that there was an evil or godless world in Holland, until Brother S. opened the **eye of wrath** <term>Zorn-Auge</term>, which became active on our way to Brother Adrian, where such people frequently go; but we withdraw ourselves from it, because it is painful to the **soul** <term>Gemüthe</term> <note>original: *Gemüthe*; the inner seat of a person's emotions, will, and spiritual disposition.</note>.

2. From which it appears that Brother S. has not yet fundamentally grasped love, which sees or admits no evil. Nature loves only its own likeness; but the love of God overcomes or transcends all wickedness, and can be seized or offended by nothing.

Regarding your eye or mirror, it would be good if you completely renounced yourself in it for the time being; for in the fire there is a false light, even if it is sharp and attractive: if you come to the light, you will find it repulsive to yourself. <note>original: "wirds euch selbst anstincken," literally "it will stink to you," meaning it will become disgusting or revealed as foul.</note> For it is a true poison to us, which infects soul and spirit from hell; therefore, at the risk of the heavenly image and the light-body, we cannot look into it: and they are only false **specters** <note>original: "Spectra [Gespenste]"; apparitions or ghostly illusions.</note> from the abyss, meant to plunge our spirit into pride and wrath. May **GOD** wish to protect you from all danger in grace, Amen.

### of the blessed Mr. *J. W. U.*

...mind fell into great sadness, and in great anxiety in solitude, in the field, I raised myself to **GOD**, speaking out of distress: 

> My **God**, how shall I alone get through this great wilderness, where no trace of the Kingdom of Heaven is to be found, and the path is hedged with such cruel, dark, fiery powers of hell! I almost despair, and I am afraid to begin the course. Has any living human in the world ever broken through this hell before me? If that were so, I would have courage and would confidently venture through need and death.

Whereupon the divine answer showed me a man in *Christ* <note>Original: *Christo*</note>, also the place in the world where he lived hidden. With this I went home with great joy and strengthened my *imagination* <note>In this context, "imagination" refers to the soul's power to form internal images and focus its will, a central concept in Boehmist spirituality.</note>, and could tell this vision to no one: but from that hour on I became estranged in mind from my parents and siblings, so that from this time forward they could never again enter into my heart's *tincture* <term>Tincture: The spiritual essence or "inner quality" of a person. To enter the tincture means to have a deep, soul-level connection or influence.</term>. As then my blessed mother, when I had come of age, once said to me: 

> Son, you are not as if you were our child, but a stranger; remember then, that I am your mother, who carried you beneath my heart!

**GOD** spared me, however, until my eighteenth year before He dared to begin the *effective* struggle with the spirit of this world in me. For once **God** has declared war on *Satan* in us, He never again retreats, nor makes a standstill or peace with the enemy, but carries out the struggle to victory through the whole of a person's life, even if the flesh should go to pieces; He spares nothing.

...became acquainted with companions and newly enlisted soldiers, whom I regarded with love. But I did not understand their sport or art of fencing <note>original: *Schirmkunst*, referring to the art of defense or fencing</note> [shadow-boxing] <note>original: *Spiegelfechten*, literally "mirror-fencing," often used metaphorically for mock-fighting or deceptive posturing</note>; therefore, when it came to the heart of the game, we always fell into disagreement. For the spirit of the world <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*</note> always wants to drift on top and be the supreme power in sacrifice and the kingdom. And so the game ran entirely into the spirit of the world, so that everyone fell clumsily and lost into the flesh: into which labyrinth my creaturely self <term>Creature: In this spiritual context, the "creature" or "creaturely self" refers to the human being as a biological, worldly entity, often seen as an obstacle to the divine spirit.</term> had unnoticeably wandered. 

Now I was cornered: I was expected to court <note>original: *freyen*, to woo or propose marriage</note> [a wife], but I could reach no state of pleasure or choice in the flesh, because my dear mother had taught me not to let myself feel lust. Therefore, at the risk of losing the inner man <term>Inner man: The spiritual or divine essence within a person, which Boehmists believed must be protected from worldly desires.</term>, I did not dare to test whether I preferred the eldest or youngest sister proposed to me. They advised me toward the youngest; but the children’s father wanted to give me the eldest: against whom **God**, at that very hour, awakened a revulsion within me, so that I answered that I would not be able to live with her. 

The anxiety with which my mind stood within during this, and how my soul labored day and night under this, praying that **GOD** might rescue me from danger, cannot be described. For I said: "My **God**! I do not understand this urge; it is foreign to my mind: therefore I do not trust myself. You know that my intention <note>original: *Intention*, used here to mean his spiritual aim or resolve</note> is that I seek to cling to you forever, to love and cling to you with spirit, soul, and body above all things at all times. Behold, here I am; whether you wish to have me in the world or out of the world: Take..."

### To F. F. S. on December 22, 1705.

1. Great danger at the first light or awakening, if one does not soon settle upon the **center of nature** <note>original: *Centrum naturæ*; in Jacob Böhme's philosophy, this is the fundamental point of origin where spiritual forces manifest</note> and die to all **selfhood** <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the ego-driven will that separates a person from God</note>. 2. Through this, the right fire is struck, without which the soul is an animal in the outward and a dragon in the inward. 3. With this fire, however, she returns to the first image of divine likeness, and in her outward works, she stands in **GOD** above nature. 4. How this image manifests throughout the whole person. 5. The essential difference between the **three wombs** <note>original: *Gebärmütter*; these are the three "Principles" or realms of existence: the dark fire-world, the light world, and the physical world</note> and their children: their signs and conduct toward one another. 6. Concerning the deep mystery of the holy poverty of Christ.

The mystery of **rebirth** (in which we wish to include all [elementary] questions as one) is great, because our heavenly image, **JESUS**, must be born through all **three principles** <note>original: *Principia*; the fundamental layers of reality</note>. (She—the soul—exists only as a **manifestation** <note>original: *Ausgeburt*</note> in the light) if she is to stand and triumph as a knight against Satan and the prince of this world. Therefore, you find that the first awakening and shattering of the **mind** <note>original: *Gemüth*; the seat of the will and the inner disposition</note> happens in the outer spirit; where the soul, through repentance and abstinence—depending on how faithfully she surrenders herself in her will to **GOD**—soon reaches the **outer tincture** <note>original: *Tinctur*; a spiritual essence or transformative power</note> in the mind. This, however, is very unstable, and it is not good for a person to remain in this state for long. As soon as Christ is born here, He must immediately be killed in us by Herod, or the **spirit of the world** <note>original: *Spiritu mundi*</note> (who devours his own children in the first form of eternal nature), because we are still innocent little children. And through this death, He must flee into the **first principle of the fire-birth** <note>original: *Feuersgeburt*</note>, as if into Egypt; and there, through earnest prayer and pressing into **GOD**, shatter the remaining locked forms of eternal nature. For where the soul does not soon [flee]—

Just as you already taste within yourselves what noble fruits love yields internally, and that she no longer keeps her sweet powers to herself—as she once did during her hard birth—but now mildly suckles her offspring, and has birthed herself into a more noble plant than she herself was: whose flesh has become our food, and his blood, the <term>Tincture</term>, our drink. This food and nourishment contains within it the victory over hell and the world, so that whoever eats of this bread has within him the life that takes eternal death captive. Therefore, we no longer think of the <term>anguish</term> <note>original: *Angst*; here referring to the labor pains of spiritual rebirth</note>, because the man is born into the world. We can now forgive everyone everything, if our "drivers" <note>Those who persecute or pressure the believers</note> can only forgive themselves. All sorrow is turned into joy: for this we thank GOD in eternity, who has not let the dragon <note>The "dragon" symbolizes the wrathful, ego-driven nature of the devil or the unredeemed self</note> be victorious. Hallelujah, Amen.

4. We now have no more conflict within us; rather, there is a constant ignition of the <term>desire for love</term> <note>original: *Liebebegierde*</note>, so that we put on <note>or "clothe ourselves in"</note> the <term>Stem of Christ</term> <note>original: *Stamm Christo*</note>, and also seize all foreign hungers from the abyss, or wherever they come from, and lead them into the unlocked point of life; there, the <term>imprinted forms of selfhood</term> <note>original: *impressete Gestalten der Eigenheit*; the rigid patterns of the ego</note> are soon dissolved, and the dragon becomes exceedingly supple and lets his venomous sting fall: whereby the fire of love [overcomes] the fire of hell...

It was quite different during the ongoing conflict of the <term>Principles</term> <note>original: *Principien*; referring to the three fundamental forces in Jacob Böhme’s cosmology: the Dark Fire-world, the Light Love-world, and the Outward World</note>, when one turned its back to the other, and each quality fled from the next, because the Dragon swallowed everything into his poisonous, murderous hunger. But this leaf has now turned, because the conflict of the Principles is concluded, and a flower has grown out of all three, whose scent is a plague to Satan; and we now boldly invite Satan himself—if indeed he has such a great hunger—that he may now be a guest, where he can satisfy himself just as we do. This growth was the goal; before this, the Principles could not come to a standstill within themselves; it was a constant birthing and consuming among one another. We had to follow this play until GOD finally brought our many martyrdoms, anxieties, and torments to their end, and set Himself as a Ruler upon the <term>Rainbow</term> <note>The rainbow is a frequent symbol in Christian mysticism for the synthesis of the dark and light principles into a unified harmony</note> between the Principles; there, Satan's pride was taken away. Yes, he must be drawn near by force to see our Helper, for which he is greatly ashamed, and for that reason he must be pulled close. Here his theft is broken; he stains his hands no more. He is a powerfully poor creature before the Light. He who previously wished to be a god in the outer <term>Star</term> <note>original: *Astro*; refers to the "Astrum," the celestial and psychological influences that govern the external world</note> and in the abyss of darkness is now a coarse donkey, as stupid as a beast. Woe to those who surrender themselves to this clumsy god; they shall have eternal shame because they allowed themselves to be so shamefully deceived.

### To B. v. T., January 16, 1706.

Good intentions originate from the outer light: wherein lies great danger, and such <term>dalliance</term> <note>original: *Buhlerey*; here referring to a superficial or misguided spiritual attraction to external phenomena rather than a true internal union with the Divine</note> is just as harmful as coarse dalliance in the flesh.

We wish that you were only for once as sensitive to our anguish as we are: you would not only see that good intentions are not sufficient in divine ways; but also that they are <term>Satan’s whip</term>, which we put into his hand so that he may strike us with it afterward. Certainly, we are terrified when we look upon the outer <term>tincture</term> <note>In this context, a spiritual essence or "coloring" that influences the soul</note> from the <term>stars</term> <note>original: *Gestirn*; referring to astrological or worldly influences that shape human personality and desires</note>, because Satan is hidden beneath it and seizes upon an inexperienced person with great force; therefore guard yourselves against it. Understand us in love, in what we tell you, because we take your spiritual growth to heart, as nothing is more harmful than outer dalliance. This contains within itself both the wrath of God and the <term>Turba</term> <note>A term used by Jacob Böhme to describe a state of terminal disturbance, chaos, or the "wrath-fire" that breaks things apart</note>, just as coarse whoredom in the flesh does; as you see in the conversation of our Mother Eve with the serpent, which is the very same ground—how Satan hides himself beneath it, as if under the <term>solar tincture</term> <note>A seemingly bright, golden, or "enlightened" influence that can be deceptive</note>, but soon thereafter reveals his claws: therefore it is not good to dally with the <term>Spirit of the world</term> <note>original: *Spiritu mundi*; the governing spirit of the physical, temporal universe</note>. Böhme <note>Jacob Böhme (1757–1624), the German mystic whose "theosophy" forms the basis of these letters</note> understood this deeply and writes: leave the outer spirit un-wedded, or he will reward you poorly or badly.

### To B. v. T., February 19, 1706.

1. Whatever a person holds fast and cannot surrender—even if it were a duty or an <term>Idea</term> <note>original: *Idea*; here referring to a mental construct or spiritual concept that one becomes attached to</note>—is the <term>Dragon of Selfhood</term> <note>original: *Drache der Eigenheit*; a Böhmean term for the egoistic nature that resists God</note>, and not Christ in us.
2. This [Christ], as the Bride of the Soul, is obtained only by means of the heavenly <term>Mother of Light</term> <note>original: *Lichtsmutter*; a personification of Divine Wisdom or the Sophia, who facilitates the birth of Christ in the soul</note>: whoever misses her remains stuck in the <term>fire-ground</term> <note>original: *Feuergrunde*; the harsh, consuming base of nature without the tempering of light</note> and perishes in dark selfhood.
3. Therefore, we must ignite this Mother without delay and blow upon the heavenly fire with her spirit of light: the power of which is to consume all <term>waste</term> <note>original: *Egest*; likely a variation of Latin *egesta*, meaning waste or dross, here referring to the impurities of the dark world</note> of the dark world,
4. And to unlock Heaven in all three <term>Principles</term> <note>Referring to the three realms of existence in Jacob Böhme’s cosmology: the dark fire-world, the light world, and the outer visible world</note>; where all conflict in the <term>Qualities</term> <note>The seven source-properties or "fountains" of nature</note> comes to an end.
5. How we gradually reach this high bliss through the transformation of the will with the divine Light of Love, as our true Mother, and in her draw from the <term>Word of the Lord</term> <note>original: *Verbo Domini*</note>.

If you wish for the newborn Christ-child to also move into your heart, then by no means stand firm in your own mind; rather, change all your exercises, spiritual and physical, and surrender to God with full <term>resignation</term> <note>original: *Resignation*; in the sense of *Gelassenheit* or total yielding to the Divine Will</note> what is His. That is: whatever spiritual concept your soul-spirit has entered into, do not build any <term>tabernacles</term> <note>A biblical reference to the Transfiguration (Matthew 17:4), where Peter wanted to stay in a moment of glory; here it means not clinging to spiritual experiences</note>; even if you have found the best practice, where you now think you should remain: it is only a dwelling of the Dragon (not of Christ); therefore he bites cruelly about him, like a fierce beast, to protect his nest. Simply throw away your selfhood: nothing shall be taken from you, but in the surrendered will everything shall be given to you; so that you may build a tabernacle of God within the human being and serve God in His holy temple. Selfhood has now brought its wonders to their goal; therefore you will have it much easier than we poor <term>little worms of Jacob</term> <note>original: *Würmlein Jacobs*; a humble self-reference based on Isaiah 41:14: "Fear not, thou worm Jacob"</note> had it in our days.

3. Therefore, we have written to you several times that you must not be a middle-man, and must make no *distinctions* <term>distinctions [separation] <note>original: *Discrimina*</note></term> between the inward and the outward, such as: "He believes he has found cause, through this or that external form, to censure you; yet inwardly, he does not despise the divine gift." That is the *spirit of the world* <term>spirit of the world <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the worldly or astral spirit that governs the physical and social realm, often contrasted with the pure divine spirit.</note></term>, dear brother; it has divided us in wrath. 4. The *spirit of the world* does not understand the Virgin’s <note>Refers to Divine Wisdom or Sophia, a central figure in Boehmian mysticism representing the pure, unfallen mirror of God.</note> way: she possesses all our three *principles* <term>principles <note>original: *Principia*; in theosophy, these are the three realms of existence: the dark fire-world, the light world of love, and the visible material world.</note></term>, and she regrets nothing; she knows what she does. She is not prone to outbursts like reason; she can watch many things until Satan peers out from man’s spirit and action—then she strikes and raps Satan on the knuckles. But her word is spirit and life, and has the renewing power within it, in which the soul can take hold and raise itself up, if it is from God. Whoever cannot bear this trial and brotherly chastisement is not worthy of our fellowship with the Father and the Son—God be praised in eternity. See, dear brother, that is our understanding. Therefore, withdraw your outward *tincture* <term>tincture <note>original: *Tinctur*; the spiritual essence or "coloring" that defines a being's nature or outward manifestation.</note></term>, which is full of good intentions, compassion, and goodwill; you will greatly benefit yourself and your playmate thereby. You must surrender him to God in spirit and nature, we say, as we recognize it in Christ.

->To B. v. T. on March 28, 1706.<-

Chastity and discipline in the spirit promote chastity in the flesh.

You will find it much easier to overcome Satan without such carnal company or fellowship in the house; he must fall of his own accord, provided you cast away all foreign suitors <note>original: *Buhler*; refers to worldly distractions or idols that "woo" the soul’s affection away from God.</note> together, so that the heavenly Virgin <note>Divine Wisdom or Sophia, the pure mirror of God’s glory.</note> may possess your mind alone. She will always indicate what you are to admit with discernment <note>original: *Discretion*</note> or not. If a suitor then approaches afterwards, he cannot move or poison your imagination <term>imagination <note>original: *Imagination*; in Boehmian theosophy, this is the creative power of the soul to "form" its internal reality through the will.</note></term>, much less the stimulus <note>original: *Stimulum*; a physical urge or provocation.</note>; rather, you will only feel snake-bites in the fire-ground <term>fire-ground <note>original: *Feuergrund*; the first "principle" or dark, energetic root of existence where the soul's desires burn.</note></term>, and you will be able to extinguish them by imagining into the Virgin.

->To B. v. T. on March 30, 1706.<-

How one can most easily overcome Satan in Venus <note>original: *Venere*; referring to the Roman goddess of love, used here to signify carnal lust or sexual temptation.</note>: who strengthens himself through the spirit of the world <note>original: *Spiritum mundi*; the elemental or astral spirit that governs the physical realm.</note> in the unconverted.

With God’s help, you shall soon be delivered from Satan in Venus. Only do not form yourself into any creature <note>original: *Creatur*; any created thing as opposed to the Creator.</note>, lest you go astray in the struggle and awaken a turmoil <term>turmoil <note>original: *Turbam*; a state of spiritual confusion or wrathful "uproar" in the soul’s elements.</note></term>; instead, imagine strongly into God's light, and you will experience that no power of the devil shall endure. This is especially true when you reach the Virgin of Wisdom with your desire; she casts the devil out immediately. Brother Adrian told me last year how Satan held him in this bond all that time,

### To B. v. T. on April 20, 1706.

1. The conclusion of the old and the beginning of a new goal with the start of this year: what the vision in this goal is, and how one should conduct oneself therein.
2. Contradictions in nature further God’s purpose in this goal: our duty and advantage therein.
3. With this, the holy testimony of God in humanity is now also raised up once more.

From yesterday’s letters to Brother G. you will see what a blessing the good God has granted to both you and Brother Adr. <note>likely Brother Andreas or Adrian, fellow members of the "Angelic Brethren" or a similar pietist circle.</note> from our struggle and victory, because He has perceived both of your spirits within the opened virginal mirror <term>virginal mirror <note>original: *jungfräulichen Spiegel*; refers to the "Mirror of Wisdom" or Sophia, the pure reflection of God’s glory in which the soul's true image is seen.</note></term>. This perceiving or beholding is a very powerful work—an attraction and an impregnation—from which the strong movement and pulling in the fire arose for you this past Saturday (when the end of the old goal was concluded and led by the Spirit of God into a new beginning). Take note, it is no natural spirit of wrath <term>spirit of wrath <note>original: *Grimmengeist*; the harsh, fierce, and consuming quality of nature when it is not tempered by God’s love.</note></term>, but rather the strong attraction of the Heavenly Father toward Christ, the virginal eye: and it contains within itself the hunger of all three principles <term>three principles <note>A foundational concept in Jakob Böhme’s thought: 1. The Dark World (fire/wrath), 2. The Light World (love/light), and 3. The Outward World (the physical universe).</note></term>. To this we must bring the food of love in earnest faith; otherwise, the strong hunger of the fierce abyss will rise up within it, which takes hold sharply and consumes us, skin and hair—

### To B. v. T., April 25, 1706.

> ->He who will not enter the world of light through the fire of anguish<-
> ->cannot endure.<-

Freher <note>Dionysius Andreas Freher (1649–1728), a prominent commentator on the works of Jakob Böhme.</note> complained constantly that my spirit was too strong for him, so that he could not keep pace with me; this happened because he did not want to go into the fire at all, while he was constantly impregnating me with his reason <note>original: *Vernunft*</note>, which our Virgin <note>Refers to the "Virgin Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, a central figure in this mystical tradition representing the pure, divine mirror of the soul.</note> gave birth to through the fire of anguish <term>fire of anguish <note>original: *Angstfeuer*; in Böhmean mysticism, the agonizing spiritual tension or "birth pangs" where the soul's dark nature is consumed to allow the divine light to emerge.</note></term>, for which he had no taste: he only wanted to rest in the impregnation of the first instance in the tincture <term>tincture <note>original: *Tinctur*; a spiritual essence or alchemical agent of transformation that infuses a substance with new life.</note></term> with his fire; in this I was to have had an honest German fellow-brother <note>original: *Confrater*</note> in him. This awakens faith powerfully, so that faith in the Invisible is a true eating of the heavenly manna, of Christ’s flesh and blood, the Virgin’s essence and corporeality, in which we—as in our <term>nutriment <note>original Latin: *Nutriment*; nourishment or sustenance</note></term>—grow and become strong in the inner man.

Of the late Mr. J. W. U.

## To J. F. S. on August 1, 1706.

1, 2. Why so many a young warrior has fallen into Venus <note>original: *in Venere*; a reference to carnal temptation or sexual lust</note>, and what he harvested as a result.
3. What such a captive soul must do to be born again and be rescued from misery.
4. The blessedness and conduct of the reborn and cleansed child.
5. The greater the earnestness the struggling soul demonstrates, the more it promotes this blessedness.
6. The failure of those who refuse to know such earnestness, hiding under a deceptive pretense of yieldedness <note>original: *Gelassenheit*; a key mystical term referring to the total surrender of the self-will to God</note>.
7. The gentleness and yieldedness of the outward spirit is merely an animalistic lack of understanding.
8. Why the true human must necessarily shatter the center of nature <term>Centrum naturæ</term> <note>A term from Boehmian theosophy referring to the restless, rotating core of natural properties that must be "broken through" to reach the divine light</note>.
9. The earnest process of this shattering of the "dark mother" <note>the source of raw, unrefined nature</note> in a beginner, until the attainment of true yieldedness in the light.
10. Which "light-growth" <note>original: *Lichts-Gewächs*; the spiritual fruit or plant of the soul</note> is then tested on the tree of temptation, involving both "mothers" <note>likely referring to the earthly and heavenly formative principles</note>.
11. How wretched those are who choose the external womb <term>Matrix</term> <note>original: *Matrix des Gestirns*; the formative influence of the stars and the physical world</note> of the stars during their supposed inward Sabbath: and how they may be advised.
12. The glorious lot of those who choose the heavenly Mother of Light, which is the final, complete marriage with her, after sufficiently proving their earnestness and faithfulness in the long process of rebirth.
13. Which people do not attain this; the blame is to be placed on themselves, not on God.
14. Whether God still speaks with humans as in ancient times. Two kinds of divine speaking: the first is common to all children of God without exception and is reliably certain;
15. The other, along with the great blessedness linked to it, happens only to some souls: who these are; when, how, and why it happens.
16. How these souls protect themselves from the interference of Satan; his judgment.
17. These matters are only for a hungry mind and are not to be offered for sale to others.
18. A thorough disclosure and instruction regarding prayer.

will, opened in our internal book of life, and in the light, the spirit or demon to which the conscious soul has surrendered itself has been found. There is something in the *knowledge* <note>original: *Scienz*; here referring to a specific, often misguided, inner knowing or self-awareness</note> within the spirit of the will, with which *Satan*, as if with a club, constantly strikes down the mind of our good friend. Afterwards, they learn with great heartache that the enemy has broken the *agreement* <note>original: *Accord*</note> and *terms of surrender* <note>original: *Capitulation*</note>, gouged out their eyes, and instead of the golden mountains in *Venus’s* heaven, plunged them into a great depth of wrath to bathe therein. 3. <meta>This page continues the spiritual counsel of Johann Wilhelm Ueberfeld, likely addressed to a "friend" or seeker experiencing a period of spiritual crisis or "labyrinth." ### of the blessed Mr. J. W. U.

For—take note—**GOD** is no acceptor of sins, but rather of the free will that inclines itself toward Him. He will experience what all earnest warriors have found. For **GOD** is the innermost center of His creature, as in the spirit of the will; therein He is near to us, to one as to the other: the Serpent-crusher <note>original: *Schlangentreter*; a title for Christ referring to Genesis 3:15, where the "seed of the woman" crushes the head of the serpent</note> with the Word of the Lord <note>original: *Verbo Domini*</note>, as the seed of rebirth, lies within; as is recognizable to us, and as the friend will also experience, no matter how much **Satan** lies: whose weapons are wrath and doubt, with which we are not to dispute; let him keep his "beautiful kingdom of heaven" for himself. And because it is found that the mind of the friend, in its confusion, would gladly see a trace upon which it might set and ground its foot, to be able to save itself from the labyrinth, he must diligently observe prayer, of which he has a good concept, and move the Word of the Lord <note>original: *Verbum Domini*</note> within himself. (And though the heart speaks nothing but **NO**, let the Word be more certain to you: **God** does not will the death of the sinner, but wants to give His Holy Spirit to those who ask Him for it.) So will he experience wonders: how the Serpent-crusher will storm **Satan’s** hell, and in all forms of fire crush the head of his power, and in the salnitrous terror <term>salnitrous terror: *salnitrischen Schrack*; a technical term in the theosophy of Jakob Böhme. It describes the sudden, explosive flash or "crack" (like ignited gunpowder/saltpeter) that occurs when the divine light breaks through the dark, fiery tensions of the soul, transforming anguish into joy.</term>, of which Ezekiel’s discourse speaks, entirely shatter and grind it to pieces.

4. Whereby the mind shall find another world rising within itself in a great, joy-filled, high-triumphing state, though in great humility like a newborn child, thus saved from the fire out of the very severe and great anguish of torment, and now made quite pure in the light; leaving to the devil the dregs <note>original: *Feces*; referring to the coarse, material, or "dark" remnants of the fallen nature</note> of the dark mother as his food, in which to wallow.
