The newborn child <note>original: *neugeborne Kind*; a central concept in theosophy referring to the soul that has undergone spiritual regeneration</note> now stands in another world, where it draws other nourishment into itself from the heavenly Mother’s breasts, namely Christ’s flesh and blood, and for all eternity no longer lusts to feed with the Devil’s fattened swine in the filth.

5. Christ’s warrior, Boehme <note>Jakob Boehme (1575–1624), the German mystic and shoemaker whose writings form the basis for this theology</note>, has pointed out another ready "handgrip" <note>a practical method or technique</note> to the friend, where he says: If your earnestness is great, then the earnestness in your Regenerator <note>the divine power, specifically Christ, who effects the rebirth within the soul</note> is also great; therefore, let nothing hold you back: **GOD** wants you, but He can do nothing without you.

6. What kind of leaders the friend has had, and whether they were masters of the weapons of their spiritual knighthood in Christ, I do not know; since the text concerning the overly strong driving and working of Selfhood <term>Selfhood: *Eigenheit*; the fallen, ego-driven nature of man that acts independently of God’s will</term> has a deeper ground and does not belong in this place: the friend cannot yet enter this class or school; he who is at the A-B-C, where the vowels and consonants <note>original: *Vocales und Consonantes*</note> stand mixed together, must begin there. When he has grasped this lesson well, **God** Himself will lead the spirits of both qualities <note>the opposing forces of light/dark or love/wrath within the soul</note> apart from one another within him, but will also immediately unite them into a wrestling play <note>original: *ringend Spiel*; the dynamic, creative tension between opposing forces that characterizes spiritual growth in Boehme's thought</note> with one another, the *a* with the *b*, *ab* etc. This is the Spirit’s wondrously beautiful school, of which those still have no understanding who cast down the wrestling mind and want one not to "work" in Selfhood, but only to be "resigned" <note>original: *gelassen*; referring to *Gelassenheit* or yieldedness, a mystical state of passivity</note>, saying: "**God** knows all." Such teachers, who know neither **God** nor the ground of nature, make a muddle and put forward the hypocritical long prayers of the Pharisees with many words; yet Christ persisted whole nights in prayer, and also wrestled even unto blood in the Garden of Olives <note>original: *Oelgarten*; Gethsemane</note>: just as the true worshippers of **God** in spirit and truth, as well as

### of the late Mr. J. W. U.

this poor warrior, for their part, must know that with powerless little arrow-prayers <note>original: *Stoßgebetlein*; short, spontaneous prayers often sent up in moments of need, here described as insufficient on their own</note> Satan is not to be overcome; a great earnestness must be present, which penetrates not only through the clouds of the vanity of this time, but through hell itself.

7. Every spirit reaches only as far as its mother; its **strivings** <term>strivings: *Conatus*; the innate inclination or effort of a thing to persist in its own being</term> go no further. Thus a man who lives gently and piously in the external spirit has his rest in the flesh and knows little of the struggle; Reason is his light, in which he clearly sees that all his work is in vain to change heaven: therefore he lets everything go as it goes, and thinks that this is **Yieldedness** <note>original: *Gelassenheit*; a key mystical term for the state of surrendering one's own will to God</note>, and lets the upper Ruler govern, who knows everything; but the poor man does not know that he is therein like all other animals, whose kingdom must break apart.

8. If he will not break it open by penetrating deep in prayer, then it is a worm that gnaws at him and burns even into the lowest hell, as in the abyss of souls.

9. But if the soul gives itself into the Father’s drawing <note>the magnetic-like pull of God's love attracting the soul back to Him</note>, and awakens its closed center with its fiery desire, then it will resolve itself in forms into fire, whereby the great **anguished life** <note>original: *Angstleben*; a technical term in Boehme’s theosophy referring to the spiritual "birth pangs" or the tension of the soul as it moves from darkness toward the Light</note> is born in the beginner, so that Reason does not know what is happening to it: it thinks, "you have given yourself into repentance and **GOD**, in hope of finding the soul's rest"; and behold, now you first truly enter into the anguish, which makes the whole world too narrow for you, so that you can no longer make use of it,

->To B. v. T. on August 16, 1706.<-

->The nature and varying outcome when the soul in the **chamber of anguish** goes inward or outward with its fire.<-

In the <term>chamber of anguish</term> <note>original: "Angstcammer"; a central term in the mysticism of Jacob Böhme, describing a state of spiritual contraction, "narrowness," or intense suffering that precedes the soul's "breakthrough" into divine light.</note> there is an exceedingly sharp trial, where it is tested whether the spirit wishes to go inward or outward with its fire; it falls prey to the <term>magic</term> <note>original: "Magie"; here used to mean the power of the will or the spiritual influence that shapes the soul’s reality.</note> of whichever direction it chooses. Inwardly, the soul-spirit is constantly ignited by the <term>Virgin</term> <note>original: "Jungfrau"; referring to Sophia or Divine Wisdom, who acts as the spiritual guide and "bride" to the soul.</note>; and the fire thereby becomes free from the **dross** <note>original: "Schlacken"; the metaphorical waste products or impurities of the material and dark worlds.</note> of the dark world, and never lets the mind grow faint or cold. Outwardly, the furnace may glow for a time, as long as the outer <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctur"; the spiritual life-force or essential quality that "colors" an individual's existence.</note> drives the soul-spirit: but because this soon completes its work, the furnace grows cold, and earnestness falls away; then the person indeed wishes to move heaven and earth, yet only reaches into the **abyss of selfhood**, which is darkness; there the wonders of the abyss emerge, as we have experienced with **Sucher** <note>Likely a reference to Georg Wilhelm Sucher, a figure involved in the radical pietist and Böhmean circles of the time.</note>.

1. A mystery of wisdom: to use the <term>wrath-fire</term> <note>original: "Zornfeuer"; in the thought of Jacob Böhme, this refers to the harsh, consuming quality of the divine fire that exists before it is tempered by light and love.</note> of a brother for one’s own and the brother's benefit; which is now easier than before in the revealed <term>Principle of Light</term> <note>original: "Lichts-Principio"; the realm of divine love and clarity that emerges after the spiritual fire is transformed.</note>.
2. Great earnestness and necessary caution in this conflict of principles among brothers.

The Spirit S. <note>likely an abbreviation for a specific individual's spirit or a "Spirit of Strife."</note> has taken hold in your mind because he is your playmate who wields the <term>Limbus</term> <note>original: "Limbum"; in Böhmean mysticism, the *Limbus* refers to the spiritual "soil" or primal matter from which the soul is formed.</note> in wrath to "impregnate" you—as I have long observed and reminded you several times. ### To B. v. T., October 26, 1706.

->What an earnest birth follows from the word of the men of GOD: and how one must struggle so as not to remain stuck in the fire.<-

Regarding your internal conflict, you must henceforth read our letters within all three principles <term>The Three Principles: A foundational concept in the mysticism of Jacob Böhme, referring to the Dark World (God's wrath/fire), the Light World (God's love/majesty), and the Outward World (our physical reality).</term>, since in the first instance the taste is sweet, but in the fire it is bitter; for within that fire is a sharp separation, where before it is pure love and "Yes," but behind it is pure wrath and "No." 

The will-spirit, however, stands in the middle and has the power to speak the word in or out; according to this, the word is signaled or transmuted <gloss>formed or transformed</gloss> <note>original: "transmutiret"</note>. Satan stirs the will exceedingly sharply and wishes to swallow the word into his hunger for wrath; but the Virgin in the light <note>The "Virgin" refers to Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, who represents the soul's spiritual counterpart and guide.</note> beholds the soul and also desires the word for her lovely food. Here, the will is its own true maker, and can transform itself within the word—which stands in the fire—into light and truth, or otherwise into darkness and lies. This is a school well known to us for a long time. 

For the fiery tablet <note>original: "Tabella"</note> is a wondrously sealed book, resembling a mirror or a globe <note>original: "Globo"</note> that is the dark world on one side and the flaming, fiery world of love on the other. The will, however, holds the hinge <note>original: "Angel." In this mystical context, it refers to the pivot-point or the "hook" upon which the soul hangs and turns between two states.</note> and can swing itself wherever it wishes. These earnest gates are unavoidable in every birth; and it is called "struggling" to pass through the distressing gates <note>original: "ängstliche Pforten." This refers to the "Angst" or contraction of the soul as it experiences the birth-pains of spiritual transformation.</note> and not to remain stuck in the fire. I hope you will find your own mind in this mirror and reflect more deeply on these matters: how in the darkness everything is wrath, and even GOD is called a consuming fire;

### To B. v. T., October 27, 1706.

1. The sensory ground brings accusation: how Satan is to be recognized therein and cast out with profit; 2. Also how to encounter **Asmodeus** <note>original: "Asmodi"; in this mystical context, he represents a spirit of discord or a specific trial of the passions.</note> gallantly, so that it may benefit the weak member. 3. This is now easier than in the previous stage, when the will had to sink into pure yieldedness <term>Gelassenheit: A central concept in German mysticism meaning a state of total surrender, letting go of self-will, and "yieldedness" to God.</term> <note>original: "Gelassenheit"</note> because of the accusation.

I find that Satan creates the greatest play for you in the sensory ground <note>The "sensory ground" refers to the lower part of the soul attached to physical feelings and earthly perceptions.</note> and **confounds** <note>original: "confundiret"</note> the wheel <note>The "Wheel of Nature" is a concept from Jacob Böhme describing the restless, circular motion of the soul's natural desires before they find rest in God.</note>, from which you cannot untangle yourself as quickly as through a complete birth, where the light swallows the darkness once again. We sense this struggle of yours in the **tincture** <term>Tincture: In spiritual alchemy, the "tincture" is the hidden spiritual essence or "dye" that can transform a base state into a divine one.</term> <note>original: "Tinctur"</note>, and we point to it in our letters and **recommend** love: not that you have failed in anything external; for we make no **reflection** upon the outer man, because we are dull and dead in the sensory life, and are departing from the animal <note>The "animal" refers to the lower, instinctual nature of man that must be overcome to reach the spiritual state.</note>, and forget while working what the outer stars effect, because the inner man has no involvement therein. The outer cannot touch the inner except through **imagination** through Satan’s **ascendants** <note>original: "Ascendenten"; referring to spiritual or astrological influences rising up to influence the soul's disposition.</note>: which, however, we must shatter in the will in an instant, so that we have no torment and **turba** <term>Turba: A Latin term used by Böhme to describe a state of "disturbance," "turmoil," or the awakened wrath of nature that disrupts spiritual peace.</term>. Therefore, if an accusation of oversights or **faults** <note>original: "Fauten," from the French "faute."</note> is spoken into your mind, know that it is Satan who wishes to mix himself into the external stars and strike fear and terror: and since he has forced himself in like a flash with a "quick now!", you [can]not [get rid] of the guest...

### To B. v. T., Nov. 3, 1706.

1. What the focus of the men of God is regarding their spiritual labor upon their weak fellow-branches <note>This imagery refers to the members of the spiritual community as "branches" on the vine of Christ.</note>.
2. In what manner many a soul falls behind in the spiritual race, and how they may be helped.

You become aware of your **spirit of prayer** in the **mind** <term>Gemüth: In 18th-century German mysticism, this refers to the deepest part of the soul, encompassing the will, emotions, and intellect.</term>; therefore, we take it by the hand with all the strength God gives, and lead it into the **depth** <note>The "Depth" (Tiefe) refers to the unmanifested ground of God or the "Ungrund" in Boehmist thought.</note> where God gives birth to Himself through the **fire** into the **light** in **heavenly essence** <note>original: "himmlische Wesenheit"; the spiritual substance of the divine realm.</note>, so that you may be grounded in the depth, standing firm in all trials, and at the same time outgrow the **outer spirit** <note>The "outer spirit" (äusserer Geist) is the part of the human soul directed toward the physical world and rational self-interest.</note>. This outer spirit, though full of good will, cannot reach the gates of the depth and does not understand the **Center of the Birth-giver** <note>original: "Centrum der Gebärerin"; in this mystical tradition, this refers to the generative source—the spiritual womb—from which divine light and wisdom are born.</note> through which a spirit must pass into the **eternal ground**. From this ground, the right understanding springs forth for the mind, namely the precious knowledge of God and of ourselves. Behold, there you have the ground toward which we reflect and look with your spirit; and it is by no means a misunderstanding, as if one suspected the other of something: for we do not enter into foreign images which are painful to our mind and which we cannot let into ourselves. Our seeing is only in the form of the spirit as it forms itself in the **essence** <term>Essenz: The spiritual "being" or fundamental quality of the soul.</term>, where we gladly show the weak mind the indispensable door of passage in the light, so that it may find and disentangle itself, etc.

In what manner many a soul falls behind in the spiritual course, and how to help them.

This [external spirit], though full of good will, cannot reach the gates of the depth, and does not understand the **center of the Mother** <note>original: "Centrum der Gebärerin"; refers to the generative source or the "womb" of the divine nature within the soul where spiritual rebirth occurs.</note>, through which a spirit must pass into the eternal **ground**, from which right understanding springs forth into the mind, namely the precious **knowledge** <note>original: "Erkentniß"; implies a direct, mystical experience of truth rather than just intellectual learning.</note> of God and of ourselves. ### To B. v. T. on Nov. 3, 1706.

1. What the aim of the men of God is in their spiritual labor upon their weak fellow-branches.
2. In what manner many a soul lags behind in the spiritual course, and how to help them.

You become aware of your spirit of prayer within your **mind** <term>Gemüth: The deep seat of the soul's disposition, will, and emotions; the core of the inner person.</term>; therefore, with all the strength that God provides, we take it by the hand and lead it into the **depth** <note>In Böhmean mysticism, the "depth" refers to the inner divine ground where the soul meets God.</note>, where God brings Himself forth through the fire into the light, into **heavenly being** <note>original: "himmlische Wesenheit"; refers to the spiritual substance of the divine realm.</note>, so that you, grounded in the depth, may stand firm in all trials and simultaneously outgrow the **outer spirit** <note>The "outer spirit" refers to the worldly, astral, or carnal mind that cannot perceive spiritual truths.</note>. This [outer spirit], though full of good will, cannot reach the gates of the depth and does not understand the **center of the mother** <term>Centrum der Gebärerin: A mystical term referring to the creative "matrix" or the birthing-place of nature and spirit through which the soul must pass to reach God.</term>, through which a spirit must go into the **eternal ground** <note>original: "ewigen Grund"; the absolute foundation or "Ungrund" of the Divine.</note>. From this ground, right understanding springs for the mind—namely, the precious knowledge of God and of ourselves.

See, there you have the ground toward which we reflect and look with your spirit; it is by no means a misunderstanding where one suspects something of the other. For we do not enter into foreign images, which are painful to our mind and which we cannot admit into ourselves. Our looking is only into the form of the spirit, as it takes shape in the **essence** <term>Essenz: The spiritual substance or "being-ness" of a soul.</term>, where we gladly show the weak mind the unavoidable door of passage in the light, so that it may find itself and unfold <note>original: "auswickeln"; to disentangle or develop itself out of its current state.</note> itself, etc.

->To B. v. T. on Dec. 4, 1706.<-

1. How the soul can press through from the outer to the inner realm in the death of Christ.
2. How he who is led by GOD from within out of the outer church may remain protected from erratic wandering <note>original: "fliegen" (flying); in this mystical context, it refers to "high-flying" spiritual instability or becoming a "fanatic" (Schwärmer) who loses their grounding after leaving organized religion.</note>.

May GOD take him into His own guidance. Regarding the church system <note>original: "Kirchenwesen"; refers to the formal, institutionalized structures of the state church.</note>, because it is a cruel loathing to the Spirit, one can only speak of it allegorically. Otherwise, as far as the gates of the outer principle (which are still closed to the man) are concerned, one can show the soul the **death of Christ**, where the **fire-turba** <note>The "Turba" is a term used by the mystic Jakob Böhme to describe a state of spiritual turmoil, wrath, or the chaotic disruption that occurs when the human will is not yet aligned with divine love.</note> powerfully drives the will until the **tiny spark of faith** is struck, which grows out of nature's craving like a flower out of the harsh and rigid earth. There, in that difficult bath <note>A metaphor for a period of intense spiritual purification, trial, or "baptism of fire."</note>, the gates of the depth are finally opened to the mind, where it eternally reaches the **center of nature** <term>Centrum Naturæ</term> <note>original Latin: "the center of nature." In Böhmean thought, this is the internal point of the soul where the spiritual and natural forces intersect and where the "new birth" begins.</note>, which contains the gates of shattering within itself. Then, in a joyful flash and breakthrough, the outer principle and the turmoil fall away, and the spirit can walk in the **light-world**, becoming poor in this world like Christ, and is unable to ever reach back into the old nature. These gates from the outer to the inner are very right and certain, etc.

2. We do not know from what impulse your brother-in-law departed from the outer church; whether it was from true insight and an inner drive of the mind? If so, GOD will appear to him in the **chamber of anguish** <note>original: "Angstcammer"; a metaphorical space of internal spiritual struggle where the soul feels trapped before finding divine relief.</note>, and take all terror and fear from him, and transform it into pure faith with great certainty and **boldness** <term>Parrhesia</term> <note>original Greek: "parrhesia"; meaning candid, fearless confidence and free speech, particularly the boldness a believer feels in the presence of God.</note>; although in great weakness, because the tiny spark of faith is in a great press <note>original: "Presse"; referring to a wine-press, a common metaphor for the soul being "squeezed" or tried by suffering to produce the "wine" of the spirit.</note>

Whence comes the adversity of the "pious" who remain in the <term>spirit of the world</term> [spiritu mundi] against the children of <term>Wisdom</term> [Sophia]. 9. What kind of earnestness is required to close the evil eye, emerge from all disharmony, and grow together fruitfully. 11. How one learns through this to find the right measure and manner in prayer: a thorough explanation of the same. 12. The Virgin of the Poverty of Christ, her chastity, exercises, trials, and final marriage to the soul: what results from this marriage. 13. Deep reason why **God** had to lead the Virgin through such <term>opposites</term> [contraria]. 14. Her economy and governance after the process of suffering has ended. 15. Concerning the <term>knowledge</term> [scienz] within the spirit of the will.

### Extracts of the Letters

...led into the wilderness, beyond all—even our own—reason and comprehension, where all reason must say: How shall this happen, since the **Virgin of the Poverty of Christ** <note>original: *Jungfrau der Armuth Christi*; a personification of Divine Wisdom or Sophia, who requires the soul to be stripped of worldly attachments and intellectual "selfhood"</note> recognizes no man to preside over her or provide for her? Dear Brother, in this wilderness of total abandonment by angels and men, she has wedded herself to our spirit in the midst of the deepest pressure, when **God’s wrath** struck from within and the world from without, leaving me with scarcely a shirt on my back. What rejoicing in the spirit this wedding brought about, no **beast** <note>original: *Thier*; in this mystical context, it refers to the "animal" or "natural" man who lives only by biological instinct and rational intellect without spiritual rebirth</note> is worthy to know, and even this hand is almost too timid to transcribe any of it for the external world. We hungered after this **manna** <note>spiritual food provided by God</note> alone, not after the offspring of earthly bread, which for five years back then we did not dare bring into our imagination—much less before God—due to the burning **murderous hunger of Satan**. From this you see through what great opposition the virginal growth must be forced out, since the greatest miracles of faith consist in enduring these temptations: though indeed it was not our own, but **God’s power** that kept our feet from stumbling, until we attained that for which we hungered. As a sign, the Virgin has imprinted herself upon our heart:

> I am yours, and you are mine, and the enemy shall not part us!

the echo of which refreshes us even to this hour. But the depth of the matter is this: The creaturely **Word of Life** in man had broken away from divine harmony and had imprinted itself into its own activity within the first three forms—<term>Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</term> <note>original: *Sal, Sulphur und Mercurius*; in the mystical chemistry of Jacob Böhme, these represent the fundamental forces of contraction, expansion, and circulation/rotation that make up all matter and spirit</note>—entirely contrary to the divine activity. Both these powers were combined, and the devil was master in both. But the building has once again succeeded for the Creator within us: no one can lay another foundation; let each one see how he builds upon it, and does not stare idly at the **Tree of Knowledge** <note>original: *Baum der Erkenntniß*; the author warns against seeking mere intellectual or worldly knowledge over spiritual life</note>. The **Tree of Life** stands, praise <term>God</term>!

->To T. S. on February 18, 1707.<-

#### The close, essential, and living union of love among the members of Christ with one another and with their Head.

We sense the Spirit of the Gospel living within our souls and minds with a spiritual savor; indeed, no longer as a foreign creature, but as something <term>essentially</term> <note>original: *essential*; referring to the fundamental substance or "essence" of a person's being</note> inborn in Christ. This is much closer than how a limb of the body is attached to the outer man, for we now stand joined together as members of one body in Christ—one spirit and one soul. Therefore, you can imagine that our dear Mother <note>In theosophical tradition, the "Mother" refers to Divine Sophia (Wisdom), viewed as the spiritual bride of the soul and the mother of the "new man" in Christ</note>, in our spiritual duties, can only look upon you and sparkle toward you within us with her most tender love, so that you may grow and increase in her power of light within the life of Jesus Christ. In the same way, she also looks kindly upon us with her eye of light within your spirit; from which your heartfelt blessings toward us also arise and are born. Because of this, we should no longer need to undertake long journeys across the land to come together, because "near" and "far" are one within our friendly, noble Mother. For God has enclosed everything within her, both the future and the present world <term>Principles</term> <note>original: *Principia*; a term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the different realms of existence (e.g., the dark fire-world, the light world, and the outer world)</note> into one eye and the eternal conclusion of Sophia. Where should we now turn away from one another, in our senses or thoughts? She bears our spirit out into pure essences of love; from which the rising spirits of thought from both you and all of us are a pure remembrance of love and a welcoming in the spirit, to the joy of all the holy angels.

### To J. F. S. on February 24, 1707.

1. Why the pearl of the Kingdom of GOD is not to be made common. 2. The true ground of both yieldedness and self-will: how one becomes a partaker of this pearl through the first alone, and what a poor end is met by the latter. 3. How one may attain the blessed knowledge of the divine depth.

One does not throw pearls onto the street, *etc.* <note>A reference to Matthew 7:6: "Do not throw your pearls before swine."</note>
Therefore, it is not within man’s power to deal with them according to his own whim. What is holy to the children of GOD in their <term>Principle</term> <note>original: *Principio*; refers to the essential spiritual realm or source from which a being operates</note>, the world profanes; for the <term>spirit of the world</term> <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the rational, earthly consciousness that governs physical existence but cannot grasp divine mysteries</note> is only a scout of the divine mysteries. It does not seek to enter through the narrow door, but only to break in, and afterward to gamble away the pearl with its paramour, Satan.

2. For in the eighth form, or the <term>fire-ground</term> <note>original: *Feuergrund*; in Böhmean theosophy, this is the raw, energetic foundation of the soul which must be transformed into light</note> of eternal nature (the first Principle of divine revelation in man), there is nearly great danger. Within it, the soul can make itself into either an angel or a devil. If the soul sinks down in <term>yieldedness</term> <note>original: *Gelassenheit*; a central mystical concept meaning the total surrender of the self-will to God</note> into GOD’s will, and into Christ’s suffering and death, then it has the gates of eternal life open, though it be very oppressed; and the Holy Spirit in the will leads the soul to the most gracious Virgin <note>referring to Divine Sophia or Wisdom</note>. There, a lovely <term>welcoming</term> <note>original: *beneveniren*; likely from the Latin *bene venire*, to come well or be welcomed</note> occurs in the spirit, and the flash of eternal triumphant joys bursts open the gates of eternal life in the deep. Through this, the spirit always has an open door, through which it may freely go out and in without any restraint from the devil, who can no longer <term>disturb</term> <note>original: *turbiren*; to agitate or throw into disorder</note> the soul with his snare of <term>self-will</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the state of being trapped in one's own ego or "selfhood"</note>. The other party, which also reaches the gates where death and life part, but—

<header>of the late Mr. J. W. U.</header>

->To J. S. St., February 24, 1707.<-

1. A recipe against the dark spirit of sickness, and all other trickery <note>original: *Gauckeley*; refers to illusions, prestidigitation, or the "juggling" acts of the devil to deceive the senses</note>, with which the high-flying Satan mocks the soul. 2. How humility, particularly in communities <note>original: *Societäten*; refers to the small, pietistic or theosophical prayer circles and communal households common among the followers of Jacob Böhme</note>, powerfully eases the struggle. 3. The cause of the restored angelic growing-together in the membered body of Jesus. 4. How this happens, and the true internal form of humility.

The enemy has no power except for that which we give him, and he is merely a <term>juggler</term> <note>original: *Gauckler*; a common mystical term for the devil, suggesting he cannot create real things, only deceptive phantasms and "magic" tricks to distract the soul</note>. Simply withdraw your <term>imagination</term> <note>original: *Imagination*; in this tradition, this is not just "make-believe," but the creative power of the soul to "form" its own reality or "clothe" itself in either light or darkness</note> from his dark images, and keep or impregnate your memory with God’s love and light (which is Jesus Christ); then he cannot harm you. If you simply remain without any <term>attachment</term> <note>original: *Annehmlichkeit*; here meaning an acceptance of or finding pleasure in the dark thoughts presented by the enemy</note>, and allow nothing of all this into your mind <note>original: *Gemüth*; the seat of emotions and will</note>, you will weaken Satan and become strong in Christ through faith. You will see wonderful leaps—how the enemy will behave in your mind in all sorts of ways—but he shall always come up short, because he is a defeated enemy; for love has triumphed over <term>wrath</term> <note>original: *Zorn*; refers to the "dark fire" or the first principle of nature which, without the light of love, becomes hell</note> and has overcome the hellish dragon.

2. It can greatly ease your struggle if, in your outward life, you submit yourself in love to another’s will, and always deny your own will in obedience. If you desire to be the least in the <term>form of a servant</term> <note>A biblical reference to Philippians 2:7, describing Christ’s humility</note> and serve your brother wherever you can: God has placed the opportunity for this into your hands because you live in a <term>community</term> <note>original: *Societate*</note>. You will eventually experience God’s purpose and why He—through revelation in our outer spirit—so particularly insists upon this (even though we know not the slightest thing about your <term>economy</term> <note>original: *Oeconomie*; refers to the practical management and daily lifestyle of the recipient’s communal household</note>). For this way...

# Extracts of the Letters

...nothing can sooner conquer rising haughty spirits than humility.

3. You will strike a mighty blow against Satan and hit the very pulse-vein of his torment—the reason why he could not endure among the angels in heaven. Our Monarch, Jesus Christ, has now led us into their order, where we, as members of His body, are now precisely joined together; so that we grow into one another and draw strength from one another, like one limb of the body from another, or, as you very well put it in your letter, like one branch on a tree from another. In this way, you can be sustained and grow without any of the pain and plague of <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Eigenheit*; in this mystical tradition, this refers to the selfish, ego-driven "own-will" that separates a person from God and others</note>.

4. For the <term>Magnet of Love</term> <note>original: *Liebe Magnet*; a term popularized by Jacob Böhme to describe the attractive spiritual force that pulls the soul toward divine unity</note> (the communion in Christ) now naturally draws all the powers of the entire tree of Christ through all its limbs and branches into itself. This life-sap then not only makes our wild wood—withered by God's wrath—green again, but also resists Satan's perverted sap, which tries to interfere from the outside (this perversion consists of wanting to be "something" in one's <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Selbheit*</note>). For the life-sap, which is Christ’s Spirit, is as a "Nothing" to the self-centered nature; therefore, our soul also wishes to be only a "Nothing," so that the "Divine Something" may take hold in its "Nothingness." In this divine <term>likeness</term> <note>original: *Gleichheit*; referring to the soul being in "equal form" or harmony with God's nature</note>, the inner man grows and increases in the midst of all of Satan’s power.

->To J. F. S., April 3, 1707.<-

1. The Virgin <note>In this mystical tradition, the "Virgin" represents Divine Wisdom (Sophia), the pure, creative mirror of God that the soul must reunite with to find peace.</note> is not reached through the external senses, but by means of the surrender of the will into her.
2. Whereby one then receives internal senses and life, but becomes dull and dead in the [human] reason;
3. Also learning to understand prayer, and the struggle between faith and doubt within it. Central instruction in this struggle, until reaching the gates of the breakthrough in the depths.
4. What lessons a beginner first receives in the fire <note>The "fire" refers to the first principle of the soul—the realm of longing, hunger, and sometimes spiritual trial or wrath—which must be transformed into light.</note> regarding surrendered and self-willed activity, until the gentle source-spirit of the second principle <term>Second Principle: In Behmenist cosmology, the "Second Principle" is the realm of Light, Love, and the Kingdom of God, which emerges from the "First Principle" of Fire/Father.</term>, acting as the key of the heavenly Mother, is born.
5. To which gentle spirit the author held fast for twenty-one years during the Devil's storms.
6. After their completion, God created something new, in which all principles now have one will of love in the light.
7. Earnest trials of poverty during this day's work, and the overcoming of the Tempter.
8. How the path is now made easier for followers, both internally and externally, and how one can hold the Lord's Supper with Christ daily.
9. The effect of the Theosophical Letters on the foundation of the soul: and how one can become "food for God" through these writings.
10. In contrast, the writings of Leade <note>Jane Leade (1623–1704) was an English mystic. Her followers, the Philadelphians, were often criticized by Überfeld's circle for focusing too much on visions and "outward" spiritual sensations.</note> merely amuse the senses and create only "fluttering spirits" <term>Fladdergeister: A derogatory term for "fickle spirits" or "unstable minds" who flit from one spiritual idea to another without deep, grounded transformation.</term> with their scattered opinions.
11. What is required to investigate the foundation of the restoration of humanity. The shallowness of the opinion regarding the restoration of devils <note>This refers to the doctrine of "Apokatastasis" or Universal Restoration. The author suggests that while humanity may be restored, the idea that even fallen angels (devils) will be saved is a "shallow" misunderstanding.</note>.

We see clearly that your spirit has glimpsed itself in the Virgin, and therefore has a great hunger for the light; however, the darkness cannot comprehend the light. The *spirit of the world* <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*</note> within us must also not try to grasp the Virgin, but rather only surrender itself into her; then she visits the external spirit many times and shoots her power and rays of light into its mirror: therein it must not [go] with

This is called the inverted eye of the soul, a contrary <note>original: *Contrarium*</note> to external reason; for what is "Yes" in the internal, is "No" in the external.

...bitter fire; they attack the worm of the soul <note>The "worm" often refers to the restless, self-consuming aspect of the human conscience or ego</note>, from which the serpent vomits a strange discharge into the mind: but as long as the spirit remains steadfastly unyielding within the fire, the worm must burst; then, in the light or spirit, a great, triumphant song of praise is born. This is a food in **God’s** mouth, as we know from our own taste and long experience, as we eat of one another’s spirit.

10. She expressed many things that also appeared to us in the magic mirror during our struggle; but we left them lying like unripe grain and did not want to scatter them into the *spirit of the world* <note>original: *Spiritu mundi* — the intermediary spirit between the physical and divine realms, often associated with human reason and astral influences</note>, because we know these times. The *spirit of the world* <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*</note> gathers it up readily, but has no understanding of the inner *mystery* <note>original: *Mysterio*</note>, and only produces "fluttering spirits" <note>unstable or superficial seekers who lack deep spiritual roots</note> who think they have "the bride in the bag" <note>a German idiom suggesting they believe they have already secured spiritual union or salvation</note> and are full of good things, believing heaven cannot fail them no matter how they live, as is sadly evident today. These writings are a true temptation of the *spirit of the world*.

11. **God** has indeed opened a door for humanity, leading us to the very innermost ground of embodied grace in the blood of **Jesus Christ** within our spirit, where eternal redemption was found, right out of the dragon's maw: but it is no work of speculation; rather, it requires "a pair of gloves" <note>an idiomatic way of saying one must handle the matter with vigorous, practical effort and protection</note> to tear the soul out of the devil's maw. ### To B. v. T., April 26, 1707.

1. Great blessing from brotherly harmony in the light of love.
2. Why rest and comfort in the flesh is the greatest cross for an inward Christian.

IT refreshes our soul that **GOD** has included and taken up your spirit into our **play of love** <note>original: *Liebespiel* — a mystical term for the harmonious interaction of divine forces and souls</note>; whereby our **dear Mother** <note>original: *liebe Mutter* — referring to Divine Wisdom or Sophia</note> will now sanctify your fire and set the **wheel of birth** <term>Rad der Geburt</term> <note>original: *Rad der Geburt* — a central concept in the mysticism of Jacob Böhme, referring to the cyclical process of spiritual and natural generation</note> into a lovely order: at which your spirit will greatly marvel, and in all conflict will be able to find and disentangle itself in **Christ**; because the **anointing or sanctification** <note>original: *Salb- oder Heiligung*</note> no longer looks upon anything as foreign, but knows how to lead everything back to **GOD**, its origin. This shall bring you pure powers instead of the previous torment in the darkness: for in the light, everything is recognized for **GOD**. If you were ever certain of your inward calling, you shall now truly become so. We can also grasp your spirit in the **harmony** <note>original: *Harmonia* (Latin)</note> in prayer much better than before, because the **Virgin’s sight** <note>original: *Jungfrauen Anblick* — the vision or presence of Sophia/Divine Wisdom</note> therein has become a sweet taste in the light. Thus there is now a hunger of **GOD** in our spirits for one another and in one another. May **GOD** now rightly establish you, so that the **dragon** <note>symbolizing the devil or the lower, egoistic nature</note>, both inwardly and outwardly, may fall, Amen.

---

2. If S. possessed some **inwardness** <term>Inwendigkeit</term> <note>the practice of focusing the soul entirely on the inner presence of God</note>, he should not first wait for Christ’s cross from without, but rest and comfort in the flesh should itself be the greatest cross to him, which should drive him to **GOD**, to cry out for rescue from the **world-spirit** <term>Weltgeist</term> <note>the superficial, material influence of the mundane world</note>; because nothing suppresses the spirit more.

His salvation and inner form when he chooses the light. 3. Why and for how long the jewel is not given to him as his own possession, but is held in reserve for him.

The **light of the virgins** <note>original: *Licht der Jungfrauen* — referring to the illumination provided by Divine Wisdom or Sophia</note> shall, in time, illuminate your foundation to such an extent, and also kindle your astral spirit, that you shall be able to maintain your spiritual balance even in the midst of the most severe fire-torment. For within us are two kinds of men: one is inward and one spirit with **GOD**, and **God’s** own; the other is outward and foreign. This outward one must carry the burden for the inward one; but he does so only by compulsion, for he has no further understanding, being an animal that knows nothing of the **mystery** <note>original: *Geheimniß* — the hidden spiritual reality of God's workings</note>: until he is led by the inward man to the **gracious Virgin** <note>Wisdom/Sophia</note>; where he then has the freedom to choose for himself: to be an angel in the light before him, or a devil in the dark torment behind him. And whichever party he joins here, he is confirmed in it by the **Fiat** <note>original: *Fiat* — Latin for "let it be done," referring to the creative word of God that fixes a soul's state</note>: then there is no revocation, and he cannot go back again.

2. In the light, he has the **Virgin of Wisdom** as his mirror (in which he knows that he too shall be **transfigured** <note>original: *verkläret* — glorified or made radiant with divine light</note>) and is now no longer foreign, but innate. Therefore, under the heaviest burden, he no longer sinks, and complains of no labor or toil; whatever **GOD** ever lays upon him, light or heavy, it is now his own burden: Heaven and Hell have become one to him. And though the light is covered from him in the torment of Hell, nothing can turn him away from his Virgin: he sees her in his

# Extracts of the Letters

->of the blessed <note>The term "selig" indicates the author was deceased at the time of publication.</note> Mr. I. W. U.<-

...become life. For the divine mysteries in the Bible, as well as the Book of Life **Jesus Christ**, are sealed in the spirit with seven seals: these locks lie upon the earthly mind <note>original: *Gemüth*—a central Pietist term referring to the seat of the soul's emotions, will, and thoughts.</note>, to such an extent that no reason, however learned or gifted, can ever grasp **God**, etc.

§ 3. Scripture mentions three kinds of heavens, in whose gates—which are very narrow and distressing—the great chamber of anguish stands; and in the spirit, these are called the Gates of the Depth of the Mind: where, between both central fires, the soul-spirit stands in a powerful press <note>original: *Quetsche*. This refers to the spiritual "crushing" or "squeezing" of the soul during its purification, similar to a winepress.</note>; which is why this passage in **Matthew 7** is called *the narrow way* <note>original Greek: *ὁδὸς τεθλιμμένη* (hodos tethlimmenē). Referring to Matthew 7:14: "strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life."</note>. Many seek this gate and do not find it: and it is the highest grace of **God** if **God** reveals Himself to the soul within these said gates. His, **God’s**, Spirit walks with His favorites and chosen companions (whose number is very small compared to the great multitude) in these gates.

4. Although He is a lover of all people, who would gladly make everyone blessed and offers His grace: a good beginning is made in many, and some even reach the first gate in the spirit, where several shrink back; others, who remain standing in the gate, become infatuated with the fire-glow of the souls; they think they now have heaven open to them, let their guide depart, reach into the forms of selfhood <term>Eigenheit: the state of being focused on one's own ego or will rather than being surrendered to God</term>, and destroy the divine **Essence** <note>original: *Ens*. > You shameful spirit, with all your art you still cannot form any divine powers; that betrays you, your false sugar is tasteless, so that your hidden poison is not covered from **God's** light in the heart.

1. How Christ still conducts His <term>walk <note>original: "Wandel." This refers to Christ’s way of life, conduct, and presence.</note></term> in His own people today, just as He did previously in the days of His flesh. 2. A central term in German mysticism referring to the ego-driven nature or the desire to possess things for oneself rather than being "resigned" to God.</note></term>.

Everyone is exceedingly fond of kissing this child in its first birth; its <term>tincture <note>original: "Tinctur." The animating force of the physical, temporal universe.</note></term> as her betrothed husband, who must provide nourishment for her and her child, which has its appointed time. Although the spirit of the world can do nothing on its own—it is merely the instrument in which Wisdom beholds herself—the Holy Spirit opens that which is beheld, and thus the "necessity" is born. This is the true blooming of Paradise through the **crystalline earth**: for the Virgin [Wisdom] makes the otherwise dark spirit of the world so clear with her mirror of light that the "earth" of the human being becomes crystalline from it. And in this manner, the angels in heaven form their bread: it is a very perceptible power in the <term>disposition <note>original: "Gemüth." ### Extracts from the Letters

...purification in faith. The soul <note>original: *Gemüth*; in this context, it refers to the seat of spiritual perception and emotion</note> was very attentive whenever it heard or read something, seeking to find whether a tiny spark of divine power resided in the word. This it received with great relish <note>original: *Schmack*; literally "taste," referring to the mystical ability to "savor" spiritual truth</note> and inward, heartfelt desire; the rest, like straw and chaff, it humbly allowed to pass by. Even if the text spoke of the physical heavens and the stars, it was nonetheless no food for faith. The spirit of testing and the "taste" upon the inner tongue finally became so pure that if I merely took a new author <term>author: *Auctorem* (Latin)</term> into my hand at my bookbinder's, I immediately perceived the spirit in the book—scenting it, as it were, in my soul—right from the title page. In this manner, all books fell away in the midst of the conflict, except for those of Jacob Böhme <note>Jakob Böhme (1575–1624) was a German mystic whose complex, visionary writings were central to this spiritual circle.</note>, who provided the right savor. This caused much jealousy among the pious of that time. I dared not open my mouth; the dragon gaped its jaws and cried: "Scripture, Scripture! You speak only of Bohemian villages <note>A pun on the German idiom *böhmische Dörfer*, meaning something incomprehensible ("It's Greek to me"). It also mocks the author's devotion to Jacob Böhme.</note>; these books are too obscure!"

6. And to confess the truth, I understood as little of what I read in a sensory way <note>referring to the rational, intellectual mind</note> as they might have; I could not even construct the words into a coherent sense <term>sense: *Sensu* (Latin)</term>. So completely had the spirit—due to the fiery conflict—withdrawn from the sensory ground and turned inward into faith. Regardless of this, I did not allow myself to be led astray; as much as time and the conflict allowed, I continued to take up the book. Although I could hardly read a single paragraph <term>paragraph: *Paragraphum* (Latin)</term> at once—often only two or three lines—the soul was filled by it. In that same moment, the mouth of faith opened to grasp the power of **GOD**, which awakened the spirit of prayer, so that I immediately had to fall upon my knees to [nourish] **GOD** with prayer...

## To B. v. T., August 31, 1707.

1. The requested Knight’s Wreath, or victory over the dark devil of the flesh, follows an earnest struggle in which the path has been cleared for us. 2. Motives for steadfastness when sensing satanic attacks.

You will now be truly called to arms, because **God** has exposed the enemy who has besieged you for so long; now the struggle must be for the noble Knight’s Wreath <note>The "Knight’s Wreath" (original: *Rittercränzlein*) is a metaphor for the spiritual reward or crown of victory given to those who overcome their lower nature.</note>. These harvests advance the soul splendidly; they are like our early days when there were palms or laurel branches, and they shall also bring a wreath to your spirit. We have already broken the path for you in the spirit, through hell and flesh: only follow after earnestly in humility, and you will find a trail that will lead you where your spirit has long desired to go, but from which you were held back by this dark devil of the flesh <note>original: *Fleischteufel*; a term used in radical Pietism to describe the personified carnal lusts and material desires of the human body.</note>. Therefore, **God** has hunted him into his own net, where he must now remain still, and the Principles <term>original: *Principia*<gloss>A reference to the "Three Principles" of Jacob Böhme’s cosmology: the dark fire-world, the light world of love, and the visible material world.</gloss></term> must now display their wonders.

2. Do not be terrified, however, by what kind of transformations <note>original: *Metamorphoses*</note> appear in your soul, but hold fast to love and faith. You will experience wonders—how **God** will storm hell from Satan, and how, with His love, He will lead Himself almighty through all the dross <note>original: *Egeß*; likely referring to the "outflow" or waste-matter of the dark world.</note> of darkness and wrath into the light: where a marriage with the Virgin <note>In this mystical tradition, the "Virgin" refers to Sophia (Divine Wisdom), the spiritual bride of the soul.</note> occurs, which has the crown of eternal life as its seal.

But as it is, we are without guilt, and have a good conscience before GOD toward her; for our heart truly bled because all love was scorned; for it is not at all a work of selfhood <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the state of being trapped in one's own ego or "will-to-self" rather than surrendered to God.</note> to withstand Satan on the evil day of temptation. Had she been able to rebuff the tempter, she would have received a little crown of light and been received with honor into the light-world; but because she fell, the <term>Turba<gloss>original: *Turba*; a Latin term used by Böhme to describe the "disturbance" or the awakening of God's wrath and the chaos of the elements when they fall out of divine harmony.</gloss></term> will search sharply in the wrath for the ground that checkmated the spirit of the will. Though nothing has been lost to GOD—for that which does not will to be in Love must stand still before the eternal Word in the wrath—for the <term>Word of the Lord<gloss>original: *Verbum Domini*</gloss></term> rules in both. The creature has caught itself in its own snare and must now allow itself to be worked upon by the eternal Word for the salvation of its spirit, which may yet require many tears of repentance in this life, etc.

5. Dear brother, you see the great kindness of GOD toward your soul. Do not be a mocker, and do not despise it. Cast off Satan, who climbs up before GOD along with the children of God (Job 1). The love of GOD is so humble that she lets the evil Ismael <note>In the Bible, Ishmael was the son of Abraham who "mocked" Isaac; in this mystical tradition, he represents the proud, rationalizing spirit that mocks true spiritual birth.</note> (who is Satan in the form of an angel) ride over her, and she does not bend: just as this rider in his grimness, right after I dispatched our previous message to you, rode up the back and spoke these very same words of mockery into the mind.

Why no one can be enticed or persuaded onto this narrow path of inwardness. 9. What an inward person must observe in interaction with weak brothers, if he and they are to remain without harm.

God sees our labor, how we—in our **heavenly virgin** <note>Sophia or Divine Wisdom, central to Gichtelian and Böhmic mysticism</note>, in spirit, soul, and body—give birth to ourselves into a seed or word of God; [we strive] in all our letters to impregnate your spirit with **Christ**; though until now without effect, because you do not let our word in or take it to heart, but hold it back in the external spirit. Yet that spirit is only the inner channel through which God, as through the sense of hearing, sows Himself into the mind and enters into our faith, which grasps the power of God in the word: wherein the powers of God then **coagulate** <note>original: *coaguliren*; an alchemical term used by mystics to describe the process of spirit becoming a solid "spiritual body" or "heavenly essence" within the believer</note>,

And so it is now with this final weaning, dear brothers: GOD has His wonders in it, so that we give birth with nothing but pain, and can rest neither in spirit nor in flesh.

### To J. F. S. on Nov. 15, 1707.

1. Fellowship with those who merely talk of piety and those who wander about <note>original: "Frommsprechern und Herumläufern." These terms refer to people who talk a great deal about religion or travel as itinerant preachers without true spiritual depth</note> leads to an outward focus and a foolish mania for converting others:
2. Instead, God strictly guides His beloved ones at home, even in the lowliest labor, toward their inner blessing.
3. Why the urge to run out and preach leaves them: and what God intends through this school of anguish <term>Angstschule: a period of intense spiritual trial or "narrowness" intended to purify the soul</term>, both inwardly and outwardly.
4. A child of God has God with them in the humblest tasks and now finds the way in the spirit made easier: yet they remain in their steady state and do not mingle with other "pious ones."

I see that your spirit has erred once more, whereby you are running in a foreign wheel <note>A metaphor, likely influenced by the mystic Jacob Böhme, describing a spiritual state or cycle that is out of alignment with God's center</note> outside of our spirit and mind: this stems from your practiced and quite unfortunate fellowship and brotherhood with K-g <note>Likely a reference to a specific individual in their circle, perhaps Krüger</note>; we could not emerge from this dream for a long time until God finally excluded that point from the soul, etc. Considering that you are pregnant with a great folly to convert many people, believing you have a faculty <term>faculty: a spiritual gift, capacity, or divinely granted authority</term> for it, as you erroneously inferred from our last letter.

2. But you will find the faculties of which we speak more fully explained in Brother Kr.’s letter: in which we became weak for the sake of you all and pointed out that no labor is so contemptible that God would not use it to sharpen our love for one another within our walls; wherein the bitter poverty of Christ has enclosed us, which has driven out all our itching <note>Refers to the "itching ears" mentioned in 2 Timothy 4:3, meaning a restless desire for novelty or public validation</note> and taught us to wrestle for the most holy faith—to be able to trust God even if the eyes do not see Him, and to learn to eat from the Word of the Lord <note>original: "Verbo Domini"</note> with Christ.

**Idleness** <term>original: *Müßiggang*; often considered a spiritual vice in Pietist circles</term> must grow silent when **GOD** enters into the **outer principle** <term>outer principle: (German: *äussere Principium*) the physical, material world as opposed to the inner spiritual world</term> with us, and **God** sets us to work, not the **spirit of the world** <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the natural force governing worldly life</note>. For then he, **Pharaoh** <note>a symbolic figure representing the worldly ego or the oppressive material nature that holds the soul captive</note>, along with all his creatures, is but a dull and stupid beast before divine **Wisdom**; just as we all were once such, and in great poverty had to be served according to the course of the world, like a beast in a stable that knows not how to help or save itself, where one animal is tended by another through the **Chief-Rector of Reason** <note>original: *Ober-Regenten der Vernunft*; the human intellect which governs natural life but lacks spiritual insight</note>, and must learn with great effort before it becomes fit for anything. Therefore, all those who come to us out of the spirit of the world look upon all their things as too frail and cast them away as soon as **God’s Wisdom** shines into their soul, and like children, they gladly learn from our dear **Mother** <note>a reference to Divine Sophia (Wisdom), often personified as a mother or bride in mystical tradition</note>. In this, there is initially a strange **metamorphosis** <note>original: *Metamorphosin*; a total transformation of the character</note>, because the wild animal makes strange leaps before it yields to the **inner man**; but as soon as it is tamed, the **Housemother** <note>original: *Hausmutter*; another title for Divine Wisdom, who manages the "household" of the soul</note> makes an angel out of the beast, who is capable of carrying out all her duties in nothing but blessing. To such a one, nothing in the whole world is closed or difficult; he knows how to help himself in everything: for all **faculties** in the eye of Wisdom are **ONE**; when **God** gives but a single glance, the creature is already taught. In this way, the strongest people, who have been accustomed to heavy labor from their youth, are only children or cattle in **God’s** household. Thus **Brother Adr.** <note>likely Brother Adrian, also known as Agabus (Friedrich Schlegel), a member of the Ephrata Cloister</note>, when he joined us, objected that he could do all work except for washing, as the soap would immediately bite through his hands. 21. ## To E. W. S. on Nov. 18, 1707.

### Why one must not admit Satan’s terrors of death.

Satan’s weapons of lies, with which he battles our weak <term>disposition</term> <note>original: *Gemüth*; in Pietist thought, this represents the inner core of a person where the mind, will, and emotions meet</note>, will fall away like filth before the divine radiance of light. <term>Death</term> <note>original: *Mors*</note> is his ultimate deadly dagger <note>original: *Mordpfriem*; literally a "murder-awl," a sharp piercing tool used here as a metaphor for a lethal weapon</note>, which he uses when his common weapons, wrath and doubt, no longer serve to harm us; then, right then, he shoots a cruel fear of death into the disposition and senses to cause us alarm and strike us with fear. Over our life, however, he has not a straw’s breadth of power; for the Word of God stands firm in humanity, where God says in <term>Job</term> <note>original: *Jobo*; referencing Job 2:6, where God limits Satan’s power over Job</note>: Satan, he, Job, is given into your hand except for his life; that you shall spare. We recognize Satan immediately when he comes dressed in this way, and our spirit will no more surrender itself to this messenger: not because we fear death, but because, just as we live for the Lord Jesus, so we also wish to die in him. And when this [death] arrives to bring us home, it is not terrifying to the spirit, but a welcome bridegroom; as one sees with the dying, where even the weakest children in Christ go with joy as if to a wedding.

<image-desc>A decorative typographic ornament (fleuron) with a central diamond motif flanked by symmetrical scrollwork and dot accents.</image-desc>

<meta>Catchword: To</meta>

<summary>This letter provides spiritual counsel on resisting the fear of death, characterizing it as an empty threat from Satan that cannot overcome the believer’s joy in Christ. The author frames death not as a terror, but as a welcome "bridegroom" leading the soul to a heavenly wedding.</summary>
<keywords>Death, Satan, Job, Christ, spiritual warfare, Bridegroom, Gemüth, fear of death, joy, Pietism</keywords>

### To T. S. on Nov. 18, 1707.

1. Theological <term>scholasticism</term> <note>original: *Schulgelahrtheit*; refers to the formal, academic study of divinity which the writer views as a hindrance to true faith</note> makes the <term>New Birth</term> <note>original: *Wiedergeburt*; the inner spiritual transformation or being "born again"</note> infinitely more difficult than does the simplicity of the laity, and even threatens those already reborn with the danger of self-complacency. 2. The difference between the mirror and the word in John and Paul based on this ground. 3. The latter held the heavenly womb in vision. Its holy birth of the cross. 4. And the dragon's wrath against it; which, however, is put to shame according to the inner and outer man. 5. How a warrior of Christ must behave in this deep struggle between the two eternal centers.

Many births have affected us, but none so sharp; from which you may gather that the theological school-system is merely a <term>brood of vipers</term> <note>original: *Schlangenbrut*; a biblical allusion to Matthew 3:7, suggesting a source of poison or deception</note>, in which the devil establishes himself and makes the rebirth in the Spirit of Christ impossible—a thousand times harder than among simple souls. Therefore, Paul also expresses his <term>spirit-resonance</term> <note>original: *Geist-Hall*; likely referring to the way the Holy Spirit echoes through human speech</note> only in a very veiled manner, as if in a riddle; exactly what the same Spirit in John recounts with an open mouth according to all the circumstances of the inner birth, fully unwrapping the <term>mystery</term> <note>original: *Mysterium*</note>.

2. And both, for that reason, also had two kinds of mirrors in their <term>disposition</term> <note>original: *Gemüth*; the center of human thought and emotion</note>. Paul looked into the outer, sensory mirror, in which he had to stand in constant fear of the "devil of scholarship"; he was therefore dejected in his disposition and was not permitted to look into the mirror of light with John, so that he might not become conceited by the high revelation: that is, he was not permitted to gaze at his <term>Little Child</term> <note>original: *Knäblein*; in this mystical tradition, this refers to the "New Man" or the Christ-child born within the soul</note> (in humility), so that Satan might not reflect himself with his own attractiveness in the reason, which was a great danger, by which the <term>creature</term> <note>original: *Creatur*; here meaning the human being as a created thing</note> might afterwards exalt itself.

<meta>catchword: Why</meta>

### To B. v. T., December 2, 1707.

1. An example from the Author: how a fatherly heart, through transformation and the overcoming of unpleasantness in the light of love, helps a soul to rise.

Herewith you have now become a womb in the spirit of your brothers; you will now carry this spirit in your heart and constantly give birth to it in GOD: where everything shall proceed better than all good admonitions, which make the spirit resentful and stubborn. Therefore, through the gift of the Holy Spirit, you should "look through your fingers" <note>An idiom meaning to overlook or tolerate something</note> at everything in their child’s play (since they must have a doll <note>Likely referring to external religious ceremonies or simpler spiritual practices that less mature believers still require</note>) and forbid nothing more: as adult people do in the world, who are the milder the older they are, but the younger they are, the more severe. From now on, you are weak in your inner dealings with one another, but they are strong. Therefore, in the fire of temptation <note>original: *Anfechtung*; spiritual trial or testing</note>, their reason will certainly...

->To J. F. S., Dec. 7, 1707.<-

->How one who holds the paternal quality among souls must be constituted, and how he should conduct himself toward them in both the inner and outer man.<-

Your childlike weakness pleases us much more than your previous manliness <note>The author distinguishes between human self-will ("manliness") and the spiritual humility ("weakness") required for divine transformation.</note>, which was not grounded in **GOD**. For this weakness is entirely proper to the divine child-state of **GOD**; which **God** transfigures in Himself, and makes the inner man known. Therefore, your letters are a very apt reply to our letters, because **God** has caused our spirit and mind to truly dawn within your soul; as the spirit now passes with the read word through the strict and rough gates of the outer spirit, into the fire or first *principle* <term>principle</term> <note>original: "Principium"; in the Böhmean tradition, this refers to the three foundational dimensions of reality: the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the outward world.</note>, and out of the fire into the light: in which manner you should now be able to digest strong food, and transform it into sap and strength, so that no word remains behind in the fire. 

Hereby you have now become a womb in the spirit of your brothers, which spirit you will now carry in your heart, and constantly bring to birth in **God**: where everything shall proceed better than all good exhortations, which make the spirit vexed and hesitant. This is why, through the gift of the Holy Spirit, you should turn a blind eye <note>original: "durch die Finger sehen"; literally "to look through the fingers," an idiom meaning to overlook or tolerate faults.</note> to everything in their child’s play—because they must have a doll <note>A metaphor for outward religious forms or rituals that less-mature believers still rely upon before reaching inner spiritual maturity.</note>—and forbid nothing more: just as grown people do in the world, who the older they are, the milder they become, but the younger they are, the stricter. From now on, in your inner walking with one another, you are weak: but they are strong. Therefore, in the fire of temptation, their reason will certainly [be...]

[...had] precedence, which the others had to follow; but now it is completely reversed, as the dark Nature in the fire runs ahead, while Love must follow after with its shepherd's staff, the holy life of the cross.

2. This cross initially stands only in a form of light and has only one nail with which Love is attached: with which nail Love, in its following after and surrendering into the Wrath, holds the Wrath by the heel, so that he must stand still in his course and cannot progress in his own will. Here, after the first child's play <note>original: "Kinderspiel"; referring to the initial, easy stage of spiritual devotion</note> of simple love which is pleasing to **God**, the soul is immediately snatched away from Satan out of the lusts of the ensuing youth, so that he does not spoil the tincture <term>tincture: a transformative spiritual essence or "alchemical" soul-quality</term> and turn it into a dalliance: for the Wrath feels the barb and defends itself against Love; and the more it defends itself, the more severely it gives birth to its bitter sting, and with it pierces or nails Love down: and thus there is an eternal bond of the qualities, where none can flee either forward or backward.

3. From which exercise a birth-wheel <term>birth-wheel: the cyclical struggle of spiritual qualities as they move toward rebirth</term> then brings itself forth, which passes through the first seven forms of fire into the eighth form, where in the life-flash <term>life-flash: the sudden, illuminating moment of spiritual breakthrough</term> another world opens up; wherein Love on the cross divides itself into three principles <note>original: "Principia"</note>, and now hangs on the cross in three distinctions and is stretched out: where the Virgin-child is henceforth roasted in hot love, because all fires flash back upon it, from below and above. Then every principle <note>original: "Principium"</note> gives birth to its own sting on the cross, and thus together three nails, with which the new man is fastened in **Christ**: with this he can now give himself over to be engulfed and swallowed by all; where then life always [emerges] again from death...

2. Thus our **Goel** <note>Hebrew: *Go’el*, meaning Redeemer or Kinsman-Redeemer; one who vindicates or recovers what was lost</note> and Helper has become for us the Way, the Truth, and the Life, positioned midway between this world-kingdom and the heavenly kingdom. Now that both are joined together in the Virgin <note>Sophia, the personification of Divine Wisdom</note>, we are able to turn this world into heaven within her; we can also bring heaven back and unlock it within the world, no matter how harsh the spirit may appear amidst external circumstances. The Virgin pierces through the veil in the spirit of desire: for she is the life within it, and without her, the spirit is but a dark stump. El. <note>likely a specific member of the spiritual circle, such as "Eleonora"</note> should experience these powers within themselves through God's earnestness of love, and by this, El.’s eye of the spirit and mind should also learn to look into the inner heavenly world, so as to find and steady themselves in all occurrences.

---

3. In the upbringing of children, it is exceedingly easy to err, and there is no better counsel than to pray to GOD. For however one goes about it, one either does too much or too little; on one side, one pulls the reins too short in "fire" <note>in this mystical context, "fire" refers to harshness, wrath, or legalistic severity</note>, or on the other side, one lets the bridle slip too far into the spirit of the world. Divine love is the middle ground <note>original Latin: "Medium"</note> between both; it grants the children the Spirit of God and grafts us into Christ. There, the growth can withstand more danger in the storms and winds of the devil and the world-spirit; and the divine, implanted love fights secretly against wrath, so that the inner person grows—hidden from the old nature—until love is strong enough to break out openly and take command of the person.

### To J. E. S. on January 2nd, 1708.

1. What weaknesses and harsh behaviors arise among beginners living together in brotherhood, within the **forms of wrath** <note>original: "Zorngestalten"; a term from Jacob Boehme's mysticism referring to the harsh, conflicting forces of nature before they are harmonized by light</note> toward one another. 2. And how, in childlike souls, true love grows in the light out of this evil root. 3. This birth of conflicting forms continues thereafter, and the light always rises anew out of the **fire of anguish** <note>original: "Angstfeuer"; the intense, purifying struggle of the soul as it moves from darkness to light</note>. 4. Why there is no standing still, and how the soul is finally led into the deepest ground of corruption within its own **spirit of will** in itself. 5. How she <note>The soul is traditionally referred to as "she" in German spiritual texts</note> sinks entirely into nothingness through this, and gives herself up as a curse for her brothers; but by this very act, she is born into the fatherly quality. 6. What this brings with it: and how such a person no longer births themselves in "fire" regarding the weaknesses of their brothers, but in tender love at the **Cross**. 7. These mysteries of **Wisdom** remain closed to the soul as long as it has fellowship with foreign spirits; 8. And they are food for divine understanding, not for the senses. 9. How one must deal with the Word in a soulful way if one does not wish to be chastised. 10. To which Wisdom is reluctant to go; but a person of understanding learns to love it. Example: S., how he was particularly burned by **women** <note>original: "Weibsleuten"; the text suggests he underwent spiritual trials or tribulations related to his interactions with women in the community</note> and became wiser.

---

# Extracts of Letters

...for you dear fellow brothers, the Kingdom of God shall now rise in the life of <term>JESUS Christ</term>, in the very midst of your weakness, and grow and flourish from it. For the dear Mother <note>A reference to Divine Wisdom (Sophia), often personified as a motherly figure who guides the soul in this tradition of mysticism.</note> has gained a heartfelt love for you, and precisely from your weaknesses toward one another, she will take a cause from which her divine love shall burn. This happens when the <term>Essences</term> <note>original: "Essentien"; the fundamental spiritual qualities or "life-forces" that constitute a person's inner being</note> of your spirit give birth to one another, and rub and strike against each other; where then a mirror rises in the fire, in which the <term>Essences</term> behold themselves, each one in the form of his brother—you in theirs, and they in your spirit and your life-constellation. This is an exceedingly terrifying sight, and yet it is not a foreign spirit, but our own spirit, which we see in the communal brotherly mirror.

2. This awakens the childlike spirit of prayer; just like a child who has fallen and hurt himself, or received some wrong or shame from other playmates, runs straight to his heart’s mother with mournful, crying eyes, and pours out his sorrow into his mother’s bosom. Then the mother wipes the child's cheeks, cleans and tends to him, and breathes her love into him, while also teaching him brotherly love; and she healthfully unites and sanctifies all three of her children into one love. By this, the <term>Wheel of Birth</term> <note>original: "Geburtsrad"; a term from Jacob Boehme describing the restless, circular motion of the natural soul's properties before they find rest in God</note> of these conflicting essences grows into pure <term>Paradise</term> and power in the heart. Thus, love grows directly out of the evil root—which in its abyss is called the <term>Wrath of God</term> <note>original: "Grimm GOttes"; the harsh, consuming quality of divine fire—the "dark" side of nature that lacks the "light" of love</note>—through the <term>Fire of Anguish</term> <note>original: "Angstfeuer"; the intense, purifying struggle where the soul is squeezed between its own darkness and the desire for light</note> into the light, where no more fierceness or wrath is recognized.

This is a certain precursor (and a warning strike, as we have here in this country when the clock is about to strike the hour), indicating that the joy-filled **Clock of Love** of the divine light of wisdom rises in the midst of the fire, and transforms all essences once more into pure power and light.

4. This is therefore an ever-driving and self-birthing growth; where the Spirit of **God** in the <term>Word of Creation</term> is the mover, and leaves our mind no rest in the flesh. He can well suffer that we kiss the sweet child of power and light of our inward man in the Mother’s <note>Divine Wisdom (Sophia).</note> womb, and thus respire and draw breath in our fire; but we may build no dwellings at all on **Mount Tabor** <note>A reference to the Transfiguration of Jesus (Matthew 17); a warning that one cannot stay forever in a state of high spiritual ecstasy.</note>: for **Moses**, (in the <term>third Principle</term> <note>original: "Principio"; in Böhmean theosophy, the third principle is the visible, material world.</note>) **Elijah**, (in the <term>first Principle</term> <note>The first principle is the world of the "dark fire" or the divine wrath/power.</note>) and **Christ** (in the <term>second Principle</term> <note>The second principle is the world of light and love.</note>) immediately converse once more about the <term>Process of the Cross</term> <note>original: "Creutz-Processu"; the necessary spiritual journey of suffering and death to the self.</note>, which **Christ** must undergo in Jerusalem.
