### To J. S. St. on January 27, 1708

1. Whoever wishes to enter the inner heavenly world must be free from the coarseness of the external spirit and possess a refined heavenly body: how one may attain this.
2. Without this body, which serves as the soul’s garment and the end-point of nature, no one can withstand the fire of testing; and there is a danger of becoming a "Satan" to the children of God.
3. How these souls (at the end of nature) are led through the forms of the two inner fires, until the completion of the Tabernacle of God <term>Hütte GOttes</term> <note>A reference to the biblical Tabernacle, used here as a metaphor for the soul becoming a dwelling place for the Divine.</note> within man.
4. Its three distinctions: the Outer Court, the Holy Place, and the Holy of Holies.

We are very pleased to see that your spirit is taking courage, along with the brothers, to enter with the Bridegroom into his wedding hall of the inner heavenly world, which has been opened in the spirit. We see that you are clearing everything away in the outer spirit so that you are not held back or left behind. In this you act very wisely, for it is much better and more blessed to sit at the table with Christ in the Kingdom of Heaven than to merely "snack" outside in the external spirit, enjoying the crumbs of the children without ever being able to be satisfied. Such a state makes the mind very desolate, and God must close Himself off from it; otherwise, the spirit of the world <note>original: "*Spiritus mundi*"; the temporal, worldly mindset that distracts from spiritual growth.</note> reaches in and seizes whatever it can grab. This is seen at weddings in the world: the door is locked against the beggars outside, yet for the guests within, nothing is locked away. Instead, there is a pure abundance of food and drink, as well as wedding joys, which are offered and given in great overflow. Therefore, it is well worth the effort to enter through the narrow gate and to accommodate oneself to God’s will, into whatever form He may reshape <note>original: "um-" leading to the catchword "schmel-" (schmelzen), meaning to melt down or recast in a mold.</note> us within the fire of trial—

melts [us]; so that we, changed from our coarse form, receive a heavenly body that is proportioned to the narrow gate of eternal life.

2. This body is also our soul’s **Wedding Garment** <term>Hochzeits-Kleid</term>, in which we are covered from the wrath of God and need no longer go out into the dark abyss. For once the soul has reached the inner gates, it cannot go back out into the external spirit; rather, it stands right upon the abyss, where one cannot play with the **Principles** <note>original: "Principien"; in theosophical terms, these are the fundamental spiritual realms or states of being.</note>. This is something most "brides" <note>Meaning seekers or souls aspiring to union with the Divine.</note> of our current time do not consider. Instead, they attempt to crowd in with their rough and naked **soul-worm** <term>Seelenwurm</term> <note>A humble or even disparaging term for the human soul in its raw, unregenerate state, stripped of divine glory.</note> through the door that was born, opened, and burst apart within our humanity out of God’s eternal grace. In that place, there is no turning back; this is why many arrive quite wrongly, because the **Virgin** <note>Likely a reference to Sophia or Divine Wisdom, who acts as the soul's guide and judge in this mystical tradition.</note> tests her guests with heavenly fire to see if they have reached the end of nature in the external spirit. This [attaining the end of nature] is the eternal divine will before the ignition of eternal Nature in the fire, and it is called our soul-garment. If the soul does not have this garment on, it cannot dwell in the fire; the Spirit spews it out. ...[divine] love in the fire, and the now fiery **desire of love** <note>original: *Liebebegierde*</note> rises directly upward into the **Heavenly Virgin of Substantiality** <note>original: *Jungfrau der Wesenheit*; in Böhmean thought, this is the pure, spiritual essence of Divine Wisdom (Sophia)</note>, and ignites the **heavenly womb** <note>original: *Gebärmutter*</note>—that is, it impregnates her with its strong flame of love and brings its own concerns and those of the brothers into the Mother.

4. And with this, **GOD** speaks the *Amen* into our **inner mind** <note>original: *Gemüth*; the seat of the soul’s will and disposition</note> through the *Creative Word* <note>original: *Verbo Fiat*; the Latin phrase for the 'Let there be' spoken at Creation</note> of His Son. Thus, the soul withdraws, and the creature is certain within itself of being heard by God; it rises from its knees with joy and takes its outward duties and tasks in hand. The *Turba* <note>original: *Turba*; a technical term in this tradition for the spirit of disruption, wrath, or chaos that breaks apart divine harmony</note> cannot force its way into the mind. Our spirit, however, must remain within the boundaries of **God** and take no liberty in the *spirit of the world* <note>original: *Spiritu mundi*</note>, for that is where the *Turba* is found, from which the Virgin flees. From this, you can conclude that prayer is not a work of the senses that burdens the head and the brain. This is why in all our letters we aim to wean your spirit away from the senses and apply all our words to your heart as food for your spirit. In this inward-turned, supersensible eye in the **ground of the mind** <note>original: *Gemüthsgrund*</note>, you will find the spirit in the deepest childlike simplicity—so much so that you will marvel at the simplicity in which **GOD** walks with us.

5. As for your desire to devote the entire morning to prayer and **devotion** <note>original: *Devotion*</note>, this has also been my own practice in all our undertakings here—

...[cho]sen; because in Frankfurt, amidst the business of trade, I could not secure or designate any certain time, but could only—as if by stealth and abruptly, here and there in a corner—give birth to my spirit in **GOD** through prayer, and therefore had to dedicate the nights to it. 6. I said with the greatest friendliness I could muster: "Brother Adrian, I see that you do not yet know our **house-custom** <note>original: *Hausweise*; the specific rules or spiritual rhythms governing their shared household</note>; we keep ourselves still in the morning as much as possible, but after the meal we do such things, and they are then a **physical exercise**." Because his spirit burned for work, however, my words fell wrongly into the fire, so that he replied in his zeal: "If you do not want to do it, then leave it be; I will do it alone then." ### Of the late Mr. J. W. U.
<page-num>449</page-num>

from that time on, I left him undisturbed in his way and sacrificed my own way for the sake of love, so as not to awaken any **sting** in the **essences** <term>original: *Essentien*; in Böhmean theosophy, these are the spiritual forces or "being-ness" that constitute the soul</term>; and in such a manner, I practiced with him for four years. I could immediately notice and feel in the **mirror of the mind** when his spirit was in motion: for then his intention immediately created a sting in the essences of the mind, as if one wanted to make him a servant. As soon as the spirit felt this sting, whether at a convenient or inconvenient time, I sprang up from my knees; and thereby we transformed the sting into a **cross**: I went out with him and saw what needed to be done, taking hold of the work with him, so that many times he himself was embarrassed by me and gave me freedom <note>Meaning Adrian felt bad for interrupting and allowed the author to return to his prayers.</note>.

But if I tried to withdraw myself, our gentle cross immediately turned back into a bitter sting, so that I could achieve nothing in the mind until Brother Adrian’s spirit had burned itself out and also went to rest: this often continued until four o'clock in the afternoon, because one thing led to another and they ran together. Yet I suffered no inner loss from this, but rather great gain, because in the **surrendered will-spirit** <term>original: *gelassenen Willengeist*; refers to a will that has given up its own desires to follow God's lead</term> **GOD** walked with us, and the **Virgin** <note>original: *Jungfrau*; refers to the Divine Sophia or Wisdom, a central figure in this mystical tradition</note> constantly gave me a glimpse from the **Sanctuary**, showing me how to act so that the essences might bring themselves forth lovely, without the grasp of **selfhood** <term>original: *Eigenheit*; the state of being focused on the ego rather than God</term>, and that we might become equal to all things in **Christ**, so that nothing should be unequal or wrong to the own-will. **GOD** has blessed it, thanks be to Him! And I now find that on the yoke or cross of Christ, the essences bring each other forth lovely and gently; but on the sting, they murder and choke each other to death. Thus, the essences in the Brother have also become gentle, so that he, without their agitation, remains in great gentleness and silence

### To J. G. K. on Jan. 29, 1708.

1. Why true prayer must be done kneeling.
2. What the heavenly Mother has brought forth in the **Author** <note>original: *Auctore*; referring to the writer</note> and his assistant, for the good of all humanity, in the goal of love.
3. How the **spirit of the world** <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; the astral or worldly spirit that governs material existence</note> has arbitrarily placed itself therein, and from it forged the opinion concerning the **restoration of the devils** <note>Refers to *Apokatastasis*, the controversial belief that all beings, including fallen angels, will eventually be saved.</note>.
4. The character of these **opinion-mongers** <term>original: *Meinungskrämer*; literally "merchants of opinions," those who peddle theological theories for their own ego</term>; and the danger of such "merchandising," of which the spirit of the world itself finally grows weary.
5. Whether and to what extent one can be assured of the salvation of a dying person: and what is required to enter into the heavenly world of light.
6. Jacob Boehme’s writings and the Bible are a sealed book to **Reason**, and both are only understandable to divine simplicity.
7. The lack of understanding of those who reject the church system and outward religions.

The spiritual birth or labor of prayer must be done kneeling, because of the **gates of the deep** in the **mind** <term>original: *Gemüth*; the inner disposition or soul-center</term>, because the spirit of the world bars our entrance with a cloud in the mind. And he who says that one can just as well pray while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, has as yet no understanding of the **depth**...

And he who says that one can just as well [pray] while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down has no understanding of the depths...

the **spirit of the world** <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*; in Böhmean thought, the astral or worldly influence that governs physical life but can distract the soul from God.</note> swallows up his inward powers and draws a veil over the mind, so that he can no longer grasp God with the **imagination** <term>Imagination: Not mere fantasy, but the soul's creative ability to "image" or focus itself into the divine light.</term>, but must instead feed himself only on sweet speculations, with the **waste** <note>original: *Egest*; a term for the byproduct or discharge of a process.</note> of the **principles** <term>Principles (original: *Principien*): The fundamental forces of reality—usually divided into Darkness/Fire, Light, and the Outward World.</term>, of which today this and tomorrow that floats to the surface. From this comes the instability in the human mind, and the spirit does not learn to distinguish between the speaking of God and Nature, nor between Love and Wrath, and is carried away by every temptation of the enemy. May God watch over us with His Holy Spirit! Amen.

3. **GOD**, by the unlocking of the **heavenly womb**, has unlocked the spirit in the depths and caused it to rise in the understanding. However, it immediately dawned in my mind: this undertaking is not from **GOD**, but only from human opinion; you should by no means release yourself into the spirit of the world, but let **GOD** shape you from within; He will lead you out of the world. Otherwise, nothing endures, but must fall apart again. This is also why we later gave our friendly thanks and declined their **courtship** <note>original: *Freyerey* — here meaning a persistent invitation or "wooing" to join a religious sect.</note> and invitation to **Wieuwerd** <note>Wieuwerd: A village in Friesland that became the center for the Labadists, a radical Pietist group known for their communal lifestyle and separation from the world.</note>; we likewise renounced other **sects**, including the Catholic Church with its monasteries and other Christian hearts who wanted to start a **community** and draw me in. We showed them that **God** does not work in this way: there must be a growth from within the spirit, which must have its time for ripening, and the creature must not outrun **God**.

And this Tree of Life, Jesus Christ in our humanity, is wonderful and stands firm in every storm of the Devil; and it grows green forever anew, no matter how often the Devil in his wrath tears off its limbs and branches: something no human-grown plant can do. And it gives the deepest lessons to the soul, because the soul must stand in every fire and bring forth all wonders—God’s love and wrath, in light and darkness; and it is impossible for the soul to break away from Christ, the Tree of Life, into which it is grafted and which the creature carries within itself. He is also the soul's strength, through which she gives birth, and therefore she cannot return back into her own selfhood <term>Eigenheit: The state of being self-centered or separated from God's will.</term> outside of God: even if she had to stand with Christ, who is Love, eternally in Hell, until the wonders of wrath are completed and Love swallows up the wrath.

5. There, then, the Tree of Life, Jesus Christ, is transfigured in the mind <term>Gemüth: The inner seat of the soul's will, emotions, and character.</term> with a new crown; in which heavenly Wisdom dwells with God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and brings forth her little child—as the angel—out of our animal nature <note>original: *Thier* — referring to the lower, carnal nature of man.</note> with a heavenly essence: and this second birth is recognized as much nobler than the first, because of this angelic birth <note>original: *englischen Geburt* — In 17th-century German, *englisch* usually means "angelic" (related to *Engel*), not "English."</note>. By this, we are now found in Christ, just as Christ is in us: which was not the case in the first birth; for then it was only said of the person, "Christ in you" or in us.

7. ### of the late Mr. J. W. U.

...if reason then willingly, without asserting its own selfhood <note>Selfhood (*Selbheit*) refers to the ego or the selfish, independent will that separates a person from God.</note>, in its own powers, in senses, will, and mind <term>Gemüth: A central concept in German mysticism referring to the seat of the soul, including the emotions, will, and deep-seated disposition.</term>, surrenders itself to its Creator for rebirth, like a child in the mother's womb who remains still for the mother until it has its growth: then the Holy Spirit rises within the wrestling essences <term>Essentien: In the mystical tradition of Jacob Boehme, these are the spiritual "substances" or active forces that make up the soul’s reality.</term> and moves within the will; this will then bursts open the womb, as if breaking the gates of the deep. By this, the soul enters into a new world, where Paradise blooms in the spirit of the essences, which also ignites the outer stars <note>In this context, the "outer stars" refers to the macrocosm or the astrological influences on the physical body, now transformed by the inner light.</note>: from which nothing but the pure praise of God arises, and our spirit can now dwell in hell without burning; because it must always, as before, be born and ignited in the lowermost parts of the soul, in the dark mind (which is called this great Deep).

This happens in all prayers, as often as the soul’s will seeks to introduce itself into God and awakens desire: which, by its attraction, creates the sting of darkness within the essences; because of this, the essences fall into such great unrest and want to force themselves out of this cruel depth into which they have fallen, and yet there is no escape, because Christ’s death stands within it, as mentioned. This is the great wheel of anguish <term>Angstrad: A term from Jacob Boehme describing the circular, agonizing movement of the soul's lower properties (contraction and friction) before they are transformed into the light of God.</term>, which gives birth to itself out of the darkness and is the igniter of eternal life in the midst of death; and it is now called the spirit of fiery desire, which unfolds <note>original: *ausschliesset* — In this mystical context, it likely means "to unlock" or "to blossom forth," though it can also mean "to exclude." Given the context of "opening" the heart to light, "unfolding" or "revealing" is the intended sense.</note> the divine light, and within it eternal wisdom and understanding, as God, before itself in the heart: NB. backwards is the eternal darkness, where God does not go: that is to say, God is in our forward-moving will, not backwards. In this, your spirit will be able to take hold of itself, confidently entrusting itself to God, wherever He goes with us.

# Extracts of the Letters

->To E. W. S. on April 2, 1708.<-

1. The nourishment and growth of the inner man under humility and patience, until the birth of the divine <term>light-essence <note>Original: *Lichtwesenheit*. In Böhmean thought, this is the substantial, spiritual body of light that forms within the believer.</note></term> in a new world.
2. The prefiguration of this mystery <note>original: *Mysterii*</note> through the altar in both the Old and New Testaments: the true form and glory of inner worship.
3. How the Heavenly Mother <note>A personification of Divine Wisdom (Sophia), who nurtures the soul in its early stages.</note> most graciously leads her little children toward this through the sugar of the **solar tincture**. <term>Solar tincture <note>Original: *solarischen Tinctur*. An alchemical metaphor for the purifying, golden life-force of Christ that heals the soul's "metallic" or base nature.</note></term>
4. Transfiguration of the divine "child's play" <note>The early, joyful stage of spiritual experience before the onset of trials.</note> through the united **will of love**, the opposite <note>original: *Contrarium*</note> of which is the outer spirit.
5. What a hellish game the same [outer spirit] staged for the **author** <note>original: *Auctori*</note>, and how he, through a life of the cross in the **Process of Christ** <note>original: *Proceß Christi*; the idea that a believer must personally undergo the stages of Christ’s life, suffering, and resurrection.</note>, was born out of it over twenty-one years in and with the Heavenly Mother.
6. His cautious conduct after the victory.
7. In the solar tincture, the conflict between Love and Wrath over the supreme rule still remains: the danger to souls therein, and their rescue through the rejection and denial of all things earthly.
8. After the years of "play" are set aside, the serious work begins, where one becomes, by one’s own choice, either a rogue or an angel.
9. Great danger at such a time, due to a mistake made in the fire, or a false rest in the first gift of childhood.
10. In the union of Fire and Light within the **will-spirit** <note>Original: *Willengeist*. The faculty of the soul that directs its desire and intent toward God.</note>, the divine essence is born, and therein the Kingdom of God stands in power.

The soul sees clearly that it cannot hold the Light-man, *Christ*, by its own power: He is only transformed within the soul's fire or hunger—much like natural food in a person is for the maintenance and growth of life; thus it is also to be understood regarding the Heavenly Food, *Christ*. He is born into a light within the soul’s fire-tincture, where He then enters back into His **source** <note>original: *Principium*</note> or most holy place, outside the reach <gloss>district</gloss> of the fire;

For the miracles in the Father's Nature <note>Refers to the manifestation of God’s power and majesty, as opposed to His humility in the "Life of the Cross."</note> were now at an end, in which Christ could have asked his heavenly Father for legions of angels, as he did at the raising of Lazarus: *Father, I know that you always hear me, glorify your name.* (This is why, when Christ asked the disciples in Luke 22 whether they had ever suffered any lack when he sent them out without purse or bag, he said to them: **NB.** <note>Latin: *Nota Bene*, meaning "Note Well."</note> *But now, whoever has a purse or bag, [let him take it]...*)

1. How the soul must become a "Nothing," emerging from the "Something" of nature.

A technical term for the harsh, dark, and consuming quality of existence that remains when God’s light is absent.</note></term> cannot take hold of it. Etc.
The soul is "something" in the fire—that is, nature—interpreted according to both fires of the first and third <term>principles <note>original: *Principii*. Jacob Böhme’s system of Three Principles: 1. The dark fire-world (Father/Wrath), 2. The light-world (Son/Love), and 3. The outward world of the elements.</note></term>. To both of these principles, the soul must die away until it becomes a "Nothing," no longer wishing to be anything in its <term>selfhood <note>original: *Selbheit*. The state of being driven by the ego or "I-ness" rather than being a vessel for the divine.</note></term> other than what God wills and is within it.

2. This form is entirely unaffected <note>original: *unaffectirt*. The internal transformation where the soul is "born again" from the dark fire of nature into the light of God.</note></term>, has himself received all three eyes (that is, when the soul can gather itself into an "eye" within each principle) and can distinguish between God and nature, light and darkness, within the <term>essence <note>original: *Essenz*. The fundamental spiritual substance or being.</note></term>. Because nature, both internally and externally, is capable of much, and in the model of the eternal will it [the soul]...

### To J. F. S. on April 9, 1708.

1. The deep birth and divine power of the Word of the men of God: and its various effects according to the threefold fire of the souls.
2. In which school the Author learned it, and how one may also come to understanding. A warning against the discipline-forgetting Satan of Reason.
3. Concerning the goal of human life.
4. The mystery of spiritual brotherhoods, and how such can be conducive to the growth of the inner person.
5. 6. The foundation therein, as in all societies, is humility in the fear of God;
7. Also doing nothing in external matters without God’s counsel among the brothers.

...so as not to be set on fire by it. When this is done, you must also do your duty in the school of the second fire, which is called the **fire of wrath** <note>original: *Zornfeuer*. In Böhmean mysticism, this represents the harsh, consuming, and judgmental quality of existence that must be transformed by divine love.</note>: because the devil pursues Christ there, but cannot spit him out or stir up an animalistic conflict; instead, he **macerates** <note>original: *maceriret*. From the Latin *macerare*, meaning to wear down, soften, or mortify the body/soul through suffering or discipline.</note> and crucifies Christ. A Greek term used here to describe a state of being "accursed" or "set apart for sacrifice" for the sake of one's spiritual siblings.</note> for our brothers: and in the third fire, which is **divine love**, burning in humility, he offers himself to his heavenly Father for reconciliation; and the great reconciliation of the primordial **source of fierceness and wrath** <note>original: *Grimm- und Zornquell*.</note> with love takes place. 2. This divine **Virgin** remains faithful to the soul, and nothing can overcome her: yet she gives herself up to be swallowed by the fierceness and wrath (as Christ says: *No one takes my life from me; I lay it down of myself*), and gives birth to herself through darkness and fire into the light; just as in all our prayers: in which you do not yet have a breakthrough, and remain standing in the gates. There you have—if you wish to read our word in its right understanding—what you must prepare yourselves for...

4. The **spirit of the world** <note>original: *Spiritus mundi*</note> is an offspring of the two inner worlds of fire and light, which in this manifestation are called wrath and love: and they lie as a chaos within the outer **tincture** <term>tincture</term> <note>A term from alchemy and mysticism referring to the spiritual essence or transformative "dye" that gives a thing its quality.</note> among one another; yet they stand in distinction within two hostile wills. But as soon as our **tincture** is sanctified in the heavenly **matrix** <note>original: *Matrice*; the spiritual womb or source of creation.</note>, **GOD** separates the mixed chaos with the **Word of Creation** <note>original: *Verbo Fiat*; the divine command "Let there be."</note>, placing each quality into a particular world, so that each has an eye in the **tincture**, and the third **principle** <note>original: *Principium*; refers to the third level of reality in this mystical system, the physical world.</note> also remains a world unto itself, and also has an eye: and thus there are three eyes that give birth to one another. The world of light, however, is the **primary** <note>original: *Primas*</note>, which leads the way with its eye of divine understanding, according to which the other eyes are directed; for without the light, they are a senseless <note>original: *dumme*; here meaning "mute," "dull," or "lacking understanding."</note> magic within themselves. In the mature age of **Christ**, **God**—through the movement of the Holy Spirit—leads all three into the Virgin of Wisdom <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, often personified as a celestial guide.</note>, and closes Himself—as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—into a divine mirror, which is called the **Holy Ternary** <note>original: *Ternarius sanctus*; the divine unity of the three principles.</note>, where the three worlds are **ONE**.

5. If we now wish to brew the **principles** <note>original: *Principia*</note> together before the proper time, and do not keep still before **God** in the fiery ground of our own grasping <note>original: *Faßlichkeit*; the ego's attempt to seize or comprehend spiritual truths through its own effort.</note>, and do not set our soul-eye in **God's** light so that this may be the ground of our movement, as well as our rest and stillness; then there arises a purely senseless sound, and an unruly pounding, as well as dark flashes: and yet we cannot reach the light; for there is a chasm between them, and it dwells in another **principle**.

6. Therefore, here is the wisdom and patience of the saints, where the soul denies itself in the **wrath-fire** <note>original: *Zornfeuer*; the harsh, consuming aspect of spiritual energy before it is transformed by light.</note>,

## To J. F. S. on May 2, 1708.

1. Engaging with fortune tellers conflicts with the **inner life**.
2. Where the heavenly Mother is to be reached, and where the Author’s word is born, and thus also where it is to be understood.

To answer the case regarding the <term>chiromancer</term> <note>original: *Chiromantico*; one who tells fortunes by reading palms.</note>, we cannot do so without giving you a sharp rebuke. It runs entirely contrary to <term>inwardness</term> <note>original: *Inwendigkeit*; the practice of seeking God within one's own soul rather than in external rituals or signs.</note> and the soul’s <term>serenity</term> <note>original: *Gelassenheit*; a central concept in German mysticism meaning a state of yieldedness, letting go of the self-will to be filled by God.</note>. We should not be able to stretch out our hand for such a thing, even upon pain of death. It is an intrusion into the **wrath**, which now disturbs your <term>disposition</term> <note>original: *Gemüth*; the seat of the soul’s emotions and spiritual will.</note>. We felt this sorcery in our own spirit, because we walk with you in spirit, and we found the work to be a genuine temptation from Satan; yet we did not know where it originated until you spoke it aloud.

2. Since you see then, dear Brother, that in all places—both inward and outward—matters have now become serious, then become soulful and turn within, so that you may find the countenance of God. With a single glance, our **dear Mother** <note>In this tradition, "the Mother" refers to Divine Sophia (Wisdom), viewed as the spiritual guide and "mother" of the regenerated soul.</note> will make the tempter known to you and protect you from harm. But you will find her nowhere else than—by the closing of the physical eye—within the **inward man**, which is her temple and dwelling, wherein she reveals herself to the soul. This is where we have directed you in all our letters, because our word is born here, and cannot be understood in any other place. There is an eternal lock and seal of **Reason** <note>original: *Vernunft*; often used by mystics to describe the limited, logical mind of man which cannot grasp divine mysteries.</note> placed before it, which can only conceive a mere shadow of it.

1. Whoever wishes to recognize **GOD** in His **creature** in **essence**, must himself have **GOD** in His **essence** within him: the difference between seeing in the spirit and seeing in the essence.

3. 6. The most difficult state is when the light is also swallowed up in the **outer man**: but upon this, the victory is all the more glorious.
7. The cause of this struggle in man; and the purpose: the bringing forth of **divine wonders**, and the **re-creation** of the whole man in the **heavenly mother of light**.
8. 9. 10. The nature of the struggle when the **little child** has reached **manly stature** in the heavenly mother: what kind of **salt** is necessary there, if she is to trust herself to her **bridegroom**, the outer spirit.

Until then, the disciples of the Savior had suffered no lack. But now Christ says: Sell bag and scrip, and he who has no sword, let him sell his garment and buy one <note>A reference to Luke 22:36. In this mystical interpretation, the "sword" is internal rather than physical.</note>. Things had never reached such an extremity before; and God would never wish for us, even in the greatest distress, to turn even a single thread into silver <note>To "silver" a thread means to sell one's meager belongings for money.</note>, because Christ no longer has any need for an outward sword, and the saying is fulfilled: *He was numbered among the transgressors* <note>original: *Er ist unter die Übelthäter gerechnet*; see Isaiah 53:12 and Luke 22:37.</note>. It was a matter of the inner sword of the Cherub <note>Referring to the flaming sword held by the Cherubim guarding the gates of Eden (Genesis 3:24) after the Fall.</note>, which the Hero <note>Christ is often referred to as the "Hero" or "Champion" in this tradition, battling the forces of darkness.</note> in the struggle wished to transform into a Sword of Love through his suffering.

We could not buy this at any price; the Prince of this World <note>Satan.</note> had to take from us as much as God’s justice within him demanded. After this exchange, the Cherub also lost all his power over humanity, both within us and outside of us; for the wrath of God was overtaken by love and has lost its legal claim. Since then, this Sword of Wrath has remained in Christ’s mouth <note>A reference to the vision in Revelation 1:16 of a sharp two-edged sword proceeding from the mouth of the Son of Man.</note> and is now a Sword of Love, with which He cuts away Satan and leads him into the light as a spectacle; He also uses this heavenly fire to sweep away the devil’s introduced shame from the creature out of the dark world, and now brings forth Paradise within the outer principle <term>In the mystical system of Jacob Boehme, a "Principle" is one of the three foundational realms of existence; the "outer principle" refers to our physical, visible world.</term> by means of the Tincture <term>The "Tincture" is a spiritual essence or "medicine" that can transform or "tinge" base, fallen nature back into a divine state.</term>. Such are the depths concerning the creation of this principle, which was infected by the devil, and which GOD brings to the test <note>original: *auf den Test*; an alchemical metaphor referring to the process of refining and proving metals in a cupel or crucible.</note> through the fire of holy poverty. &c.

->To Tr. on August 14, 1708.<-

**1.** To a follower of **JESUS**, blood relatives are dead until they also attain the life of Christ. **2.** The igniting, excellence, and purity of this life from all aspects of [corrupt] nature. **3.** How the Author <note>original: *Auctor*, referring to Johann Wilhelm Überfeld himself</note> fared with one of his biological brothers, and how that same brother, along with another relative, was granted back to him after death. **4.** Admonition to a godchild, with instruction on what the true water of Baptism is: **5.** And how through it he found heaven and finally came to an understanding of the election of grace <term>election of grace: *Gnadenwahl*, the theological concept of predestination regarding who is saved by God’s favor</term>: what a radiance of majesty he saw therein, and why he no longer desires to see such things here on earth. **6.** In what manner the initially terrifying sight of predestination is transformed into pure love: and what confidence it finally produces in the believing soul. **7.** Uncovering the source from which the confusion regarding the election of grace arises. **8.** Divine counsel against it. In what the torment of the damned consists; and how hell itself becomes heaven for the children of light. **9.** Where the ground of predestination to damnation is to be sought; and how the soul can nevertheless rescue itself from it. **10.** The inward condition of the children of love and the children of wrath, wherein the former find their salvation and the latter find their hell. **11.** How both begin already in the mother's womb: and through what process the soul can overcome the wrath <note>In the Böhmean tradition, "wrath" (Zorn) is the dark, consuming fire of God's power when separated from His light and love</note> in this time. **12.** How the wrath then promotes the inner soul-growth until it reaches manly stature: **13.** Wherein the sharp trial between the yielded <note>original: *gelassen*, referring to *Gelassenheit*, the mystical state of self-surrender or "letting go" of the self-will</note> and the self-centered will occurs: how Lucifer missed his chance <note>original: *die Schanze versehen*, meaning to fail or lose one's position through a poor choice</note> in this selection, and what became of him. **14.** Regarding the election of Esau, that it was not unto eternal damnation, and the reasons why. **15.** All difficulties regarding predestination are resolved in the rebirth <term>rebirth: *Wiedergeburt*, the spiritual process of being born again into Christ's life</term>, where one recognizes the difference between **GOD** in and outside of nature. **16.** How the Author shows both the Reformed <note>Calvinists, who generally held to strict double predestination</note> and the Lutherans their error in this matter, and how he can unite them. **17.** His victory over the wrath, and how the rift of Adam <note>The spiritual separation or "break" in human nature caused by the Fall of Adam</note> was thereby [repaired] in him again—

### To B. v. T., October 17, 1708.

1. Once the **fire-ground** <term>Feuergrund: in theosophical mysticism, the dark, foundational energetic core of the soul that must be transformed by light</term> is closed, faith consists only in the kindling of the divine fire of love through brotherly harmony.
2. How one enters a new world thereby, and can overcome all difficulty and powers of darkness in the heavenly Mother.
3. How the lives of the **Patriarchs** <term>Altväter: the biblical fathers, such as Abraham or Isaac, often interpreted by mystics as stages of spiritual development</term> should be read with caution.

Faith within us is nothing other than a pure kindling of the powers of love in the **tincture** <term>Tinctur: a spiritual quintessence or life-force that transforms and ennobles the soul</term>: the **Virgin** <note>Divine Wisdom, often called Sophia, the feminine personification of God's creative power</note> does not return at all to the harsh **agony** <term>Quaal: a term used by Jacob Boehme to describe the "quality" or "tormenting" tension of the foundational fire before it is illuminated by light</term> of the fire's kindling, because it obscures her beautiful radiance—which, with the kindling of the divine fire of love through brotherly harmony (Matthew 18 <note>original: "Matth. 18." likely referring to verse 20: "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them."</note>), flourishes in pure paradise and delight. Therefore, no other fire should nest in our spirit, for that makes the fire-ground into darkness, so that it can no longer move mountains from the **mind** <term>Gemüth: the seat of the soul's desires, thoughts, and will</term> into the sea of the heavenly tincture, but instead remains a rough, dark worm. etc.

2. Now, take heed of the **spark of love** <term>Liebefüncklein: the small seed of divine light within the soul</term> which the Virgin has struck in your **fire-limbus** <term>Feuers-Limbo: a transitional or formative state of the soul's energetic source</term>, and blow upon it diligently and earnestly within your mind; that is, kindle your spirit with all the powers of body, soul, and mind through virginal brotherly love. You will become aware of a new world within you, in which all divine powers in the...

### Great danger to the soul even from the most subtle angry thought.

You have herewith an essential lesson: that one should rather die than allow an angry thought to enter; just as our covenant in Christ lies between us and stands firm against the gates of hell.

## To F. W. S., November 24, 1708.

1. Stages of the spiritual soul-growth <term>Seelengewächs: a term describing the organic development or "maturation" of the soul as if it were a plant or living thing</term> in the sensory foundation, shown by the example of the various classes in an external school.
2. What the essential divine ground brings with it when the heavenly Mother is wedded to the male age <note>meaning: spiritual maturity or "manhood"</note>.
3. The process to reach this; and the difference between sensory and essential practice.

In our dear Mother Armelle’s school <note>The "Armellian school" refers to the teachings of Armelle Nicolas (1606–1671), a French mystic and maidservant known for her "school of love" where she found God in her daily household chores</note>, or the Kingdom of Heaven, Matthew 13:47, 48, where there are both good and bad children, there occur classes which inwardly resolve into principles <term>Principia: fundamental spiritual elements or planes of existence</term>, wherein all divine sciences can be learned: though not essentially <note>meaning: in their absolute essence</note>, but in a sensory way. Just as the table indicates how the good Armelle found her teaching in all things placed into her hands, as if they were so many books from which she had to memorize and learn her lesson from the outside in, and could study God from all of creation. 

There are seven of these classes, and they count backward from the Seventh <note>original: "Septima"</note> to the First <note>original: "Primam"</note>, just as in the world-spirit. The beginning in the Seventh class contains the first letters of repentance for dead works: these ABCs are difficult enough for the children of God, and they study them until sweat breaks out; but the first love makes all work easy for them, until they are rapped on the fingers by the pedagogue <note>original: "Pädagogo"</note>, or the spirit of nature, with the law of sin. This law consists of letters and teaches morals; through which they become so shy that they hardly dare to touch anything in the world; wrath follows right behind and strikes the tender conscience. From this class, one goes into

Without her, Sophia, **GOD** would be as nothing to the creature; for **GOD** beholds and brings Himself forth within her mirror, both in nature and in the creature, just as we also have no God outside of Christ. That which is above the mirror of Sophia is the eternal Unground <note>original: "Ungrund"; a term popularized by Jakob Böhme referring to the absolute, fathomless abyss of the Godhead that exists before any manifestation or "nature."</note>, which no spirit can reach. Furthermore, in the divine expanse, the Virgin <note>Referring to the "Virgin Sophia," the feminine personification of Divine Wisdom.</note> creates three mirrors according to the mystery of the three principles of divine being, in the revelation according to the eternal and temporal nature in the soul of man: this is why she is **God's** friend and playmate, and our soul’s helper and companion, who helps us bring forth the wonders of Christ’s cross. She does not leave the soul in its distress, but through the Holy Spirit intercedes <note>original: "vertrit"; an allusion to Romans 8:26, where the Spirit intercedes with "groanings which cannot be uttered."</note> for us before **GOD** with unspeakable sighs; she also clothes herself in our entire humanity and becomes what we are, so that we can see ourselves in her mirror within our own hearts. However, such seeing does not depend on the creaturely will; rather, the heavenly bride-leader, the Holy Spirit, opens the curtain Himself, as happens during her marriage with the soul. This wedding takes place secretly in all three principles <note>The Three Principles represent the dark fire-world (the Father's power), the light-world (the Son's love), and the outer world of manifestation.</note>, whereby the House of **GOD** is then built up in the spirit, with its three distinctions and wedding halls, where the virginal mirror or eye shines faithfully in each. These three mirrors are then finally gathered together under one head <note>original: "ἀνακεφαλαιῶται" (anakephalaiōtai); a Greek term from Ephesians 1:10 meaning "to bring all things together under one head" or "to sum up."</note> in the divine height in the <term>Holy Ternary: the "Ternarius Sanctus," or the substantial, heavenly realm where the Trinity is manifested</term>, once again in the unformed divine Wisdom outside of nature in **Jesus** Christ, according to Ephesians 1:10. For they are **God's** seal, an ornament of the Godhead in **JESUS** Christ: the divine Trinity in Unity within man.

1. Sorrowful consequences when one has opened the evil eye in the fire: the process of his rescue from Satan through a new birth in the goal of the Virgin, as a womb now in all three principles. 2. Böhme's "Three Principles" are the Dark World, the Light World, and the Outward/Physical World.</note>. ### To B. v. T. on December 26, 1708.

**1.** After the casting out of the <term>dragon of selfhood</term> <note>original: "Drachen der Eigenheit." In Böhmean mysticism, "Selfhood" refers to the ego-driven, selfish nature of the fallen man that must be overcome to reach God.</note>, the will can henceforth sink into the **Heavenly Mother**, who then rescues the spirit from the fire and the dark <term>impression</term> <note>original: "Impressung." This refers to a spiritual state where the soul is "pressed" or contracted into its own darkness or wrathful nature.</note>. **2.** An example of such an impression regarding **Brother S.** concerning **Abdias** <note>Likely referring to the biblical Prophet Obadiah or a specific commentary on his work.</note>.

You shall feel the powers rising within you, as all the selfhood of **Satan** is broken, and we can now work with a <term>resigned will</term> <note>original: "gelassenen Willen." Refers to *Gelassenheit*, a central concept of "letting go" or surrendering one's own will to the Divine Will.</note> within the **Heavenly Mother**: the likes of which will have been unknown to you before, because it did not exist as long as you were in our acquaintance, where the dragon of selfhood lay in the way, so that the will could not sink into the **Heavenly Womb** in **GOD’S** will. In this sinking, dear brother, into **GOD’S** will, **Sophia** will rise for you in the midst of the fire, and take your spirit out of the fire into herself. You see how **GOD** now leads everything out of the dark impression, to the vexation of **Satan**, who cannot withstand **GOD**, even if he sets hell on fire in body and mind. Etc.

**2.** Do not doubt, **Brother S.** shall surely come into divine humility and gentleness within himself, and obtain better senses, and join with us in one spirit, and handle **Abdias** more mildly. The paradoxes do not lie in the **author** <note>original: "Auctore"</note>, but in his own reason. **Brother S.** does not understand it. If he could only be pleased with our will, he should inherit a blessing for it. One certainly puts other things aside. What have we to criticize? We are indeed only beginners in **Christ** <note>original: "Christo"</note>: how then do we wish to censure the whole? Moreover, it is uncertain whether it shall ever be printed, and it may not come before the eyes of the learned; they are a particular world apart from us.

1. How from the killing letter and the life-giving spirit a divine harmony is born in **Sophia** <note>The personification of Divine Wisdom.</note>: and the resulting lessons of the spiritual priests.
2. Inseparability of the **figurative** and **unformed Word**: and how from the union of both, man receives divine essence.
3. Sincere souls can speak with one another without external words; though the latter still has its great use:
4. Likewise the biblical word, if it is not broken off from the inner [word].
5. How the children of **GOD** must learn their first **A b c** with the external word; and then are led further inward, until they come out of nature into **GOD**.

### To T. S., December 27, 1708.

1. In what manner the work of our rebirth and salvation rests solely upon the heavenly Mother.
2. Through this, the author affirms in all his letters the heavenly womb: from which its divine power and omnipotence originate.
3. How one must be composed in spirit if one wishes to save others within her as well.

We no longer bear the two sisters O. H. as frail, sinful humans, but as innocent, dear angels in heaven, in our tender love in the tincture <note>The "tincture" is a spiritual life-essence or "spiritual gold" that has the power to transform and purify the soul.</note>; just as they truly are such angel-humans in the eyes of our heavenly Mother <note>In this tradition, the "Heavenly Mother" refers to Divine Wisdom (Sophia), the spiritual matrix in which the new, Christ-like human is formed.</note>. ## To B. v. T., January 30, 1709.

1. Simply imitating the ways of a righteous member in outward things is the means to soon be rid of the selfhood <note>original: "Eigenheit." In this mystical context, it refers to the ego or the self-centered will that separates the soul from God.</note> of the dark nature;
2. The deception of this nature, as it hides itself under the appearance of self-denial, regarding food and other strict ways of living.
3. The Author's <note>original: "Auctor." Referring to the writer of the letter, likely Johann Georg Gichtel or a close associate.</note> example of how one should arrange one's meals soulfully <note>original: "gemüthlich." This suggests a state of inner peace and spiritual focus during physical nourishment.</note>; with an indication of how harmful the opposite is.
4. What is most important in this matter. The extreme danger of one's own self-will <note>original: "eigentlichen Impressung." Literally "own impression," referring to the soul's tendency to imprint its own desires onto spiritual practices.</note> in this and other self-chosen mortifications <note>original: "Kasteyungen." Acts of self-punishment or severe fasting intended to subdue the flesh.</note> of the flesh.
5. How the soul <note>original: "Gemüth."</note> is only mocked through false imagination without true essence; and that these foods are not a partaking of the divine power, unlike the meals of the true children of light <note>original: "Lichtskinder."</note>.
6. Which is illustrated by an example.
7. How to escape selfhood, and what a terrifying monster it is at its core.

> Only the yielded will <term>A central concept in German mysticism; "Gelassenheit" refers to a state of surrendered, peaceful resignation to God's will; original: "gelassene Wille"</term> is heard by God; self-will receives nothing, no matter how holy the thing it asks for.

In this state, the Holy Spirit itself places the prayer into the spiritual mouth within the will, and it is "Yes and Amen" as soon as we bring it into Christ, into the virginal mirror or altar; there, the "Amen" is born in the womb, and sensibly kisses both qualities <note>In Böhmean theosophy, "qualities" refers to the fundamental forces of nature (such as light and fire) that must be harmonized.</note> with it. Thus, self-will in heaven is nothing but the dragon <note>A reference to the dragon in Revelation, representing the grasping, rebellious ego</note>, no matter what it wishes to form with its desiring will, and no matter how sincere and holy it may truly seem; the Virgin <note>Referring to Divine Wisdom or Sophia</note> does not let him in, for she is a Virgin of heavenly discipline and purity.

**1.** What the reason of a child of God is tasked with before its enlightenment: and how it can reach the lost light and **angelic image** <note>the original, unfallen state of humanity</note> in no other way than through death. **2.** The danger and harm to those who occupy themselves with spiritual things through reason too soon: which is a false light and a casting off of the **brotherly yoke** <note>the shared discipline and mutual accountability within the spiritual community</note>, **3.** along with a perverted interpretation of their earnest and unappropriated word of love. **4.** The nature of the same in the **Author** <note>original: "Auctore"; referring to the writer of the letters</note>: and how one must conduct oneself in order to come into the light with it, and also to unite the **opposites** <note>original: "Contraria"</note> of reason. **5.** The various formations of the word of love of the **heavenly Mother** <note>Divine Sophia, or Heavenly Wisdom, often personified in this tradition as a motherly figure who nurtures the soul</note> according to the different strengths of her children, and how they should behave toward one another in this regard. **6.** What is to be done, according to the Author’s example, with rough temperaments, and when they misinterpret a brother's word and life, and judge them with an **evil eye**.

This worship is not to be sought in high places, nor is it necessary to travel far beyond the stars to seek the heavenly fire. Instead, I found that it is the intense burning of anguish itself within the lower parts of the soul, which seeks to consume [us], and into which we have thrown ourselves as an offering for all people. The divine sweetness is unspeakable, for it is the end of [fallen] nature and unlocks a new world in the spirit, even the **lost Paradise**. The **cherub** with the fiery sword stands before it and allows no fleshly beast to enter. Oh, if only people knew that they had heaven so near within them, they would not shy away from any anguish for Christ’s sake, but would give themselves over to the cherub; he only cuts away all impurity from us, so that we may walk in Paradise as innocent, pure angels. It was there that we encountered the dear children of GOD, and my **heavenly mother** <note>In the mystical tradition of Jakob Böhme and Gichtel, the "Heavenly Mother" refers to Divine Wisdom (Sophia), the spiritual feminine principle who guides the soul.</note> presented to me the dearest **Brother Gichtel** <note>Johann Georg Gichtel (1638–1710), a prominent German mystic and leader of the "Angelic Brothers," who emphasized the internal path to salvation.</note>.

This struggle of **faith** requires one to withdraw from the dark world [of sin] and simply snatch oneself out through the will, leaving the [earthly] essence behind until we reach the [gates] of eternal life in the fire, which stands at nature’s end. ### To M. and G., February 27, 1709.

1. Divine counsel for when brothers living together are tempted to separate again. What the tempter usually uses as a pretext, and how he is to be overcome.
2. A particular cause of instability and inability for inner worship is when one does not faithfully serve God in the *spirit of the world* <note>original: "Spiritu mundi"</note>, through the slaughtering of the beast of self-will <term>Eigenheit</term> <note>In this mystical context, "Eigenheit" refers to the egoistic attachment to one's own will, which must be "sacrificed" to reach God.</note>.
3. What kind of perversion and danger arises in the *tincture* <term>Tinctur</term> <note>In theosophical thought, the "tincture" is a subtle spiritual energy or life-force that can be corrupted by worldly desires.</note> as a result: how and why an inward Christian must keep himself pure within it.

It is difficult to advise or intercede in El.'s <note>Likely an abbreviation for "Elias," possibly referring to Friedrich Breckling or another member of the spiritual community.</note> matter, since both your wills have already diverged, and there is no one who should be able to bind them; they would break loose again anyway. The only good and best advice we know how to give is that you should return with your free will to the first ground that moved your will to live together, and see if the first love wishes to bloom again. There, you should diligently observe within yourselves whether it is God who wants to pair you or separate you; or whether it is nature, which has grown tired of one another. Though this trial shall be difficult for El., to be able to distinguish between God and nature: seeing as the growth of love has already let its blossoms fall, just as happens with all good souls <term>Gemüthern</term> <note>A term for the totality of the inner spiritual and emotional disposition.</note> who are truly planted together by God to bring forth fruit; since, as soon as the spring in the soul is over, and the well-

### To T. S., March 8, 1709.

1. Danger to the soul during the wonders of the outer spirit. The earnest process of purifying oneself again if one has become entangled in them.
2. How **God** comes to the aid of the outer spirit within us through the freedom of the will: by whose choice the Mother <note>The "Mother" refers to the creative, generative principle within the soul or nature.</note> is awakened who gives him birth.
3. The fate of those who choose the light: and their fruitful heavenly birth through the "brotherly word" <note>Refers to spiritual fellowship and the shared language of the community of believers.</note> with one another.
4. The wretchedness and blindness of those who fall back to the "dark mother" <note>The 'dark mother' represents the chaotic, unrefined source of nature before it is enlightened by God's love and light.</note>.
5. The cause and nature of such misery: and how the soul can be rescued from it.
6. Danger after this rescue, from a new and even worse dragon <note>A metaphor for spiritual pride or a more subtle form of temptation that arises after a person thinks they have achieved victory.</note>, if one looks at oneself in the reflection of the "outer mother."
7. In what manner one reaches the heavenly Mother and the inner essence <term>tincture</term> by means of the **Birth through the Cross** <term>Creutzgeburt</term> <note>A central Böhmean concept: the spiritual process where the self-will "dies" on the cross to be reborn in the divine light.</note>. How the outer spirit deceives itself in this regard: its character, and how it may be helped.
8. It all depends on the **Tincture**, which causes souls either to unite or to flee from one another: the birth of one with the other; and those in whom this does not take place.

1. Why dark dreams are not to be heeded. Signs of these and of divine visions.

The dreams you cited are partly from the darkness, and are not to be heeded; for **Love** can intervene in **Wrath** <note>In this theology, "Wrath" is the dark, fiery principle of God that must be tempered by the "Light" or "Love" principle.</note> and break its dark constellation. God also casts them out of your memory so that you do not speculate upon them, so that no **Turba** <note>A technical term in Böhmean mysticism meaning spiritual turmoil, disturbance, or the destructive "awakening" of the dark principle.</note> can be caused. By this you must distinguish divine visions from dark dreams: the first present nothing but love and goodness; the others express nothing but ideas of wrath and punishments, as well as other beastly monstrosities <note>German: *thierische Unbilder*—distorted, non-human images of the lower nature</note> which are painful to the soul.

And how to lay a firm divine foundation through prayer in the **fellowship of the members of Christ**. 9. How this fellowship is hidden and hateful to the **pious of the world** <note>German: *Weltfrommen*—those who are outwardly religious but still belong to the spirit of the world.</note>, but without it no one can come to God: 10. What the quality of a prayer pleasing to Him is, and its effect in the soul. 11. How one reaches the highest bliss and power in the light of love, and finally the **marriage with Christ**, through such unanimous prayer. 12. The difference between figurative words and prayer in spirit and in truth: in what manner one comes to the latter...

...does not want to enter through Christ, the narrow gate, into his own **soul-ground** <note>German: *Seelengrund*—a central term in German mysticism referring to the deepest, innermost part of the soul where the human meets the Divine.</note>, and be fruitful to GOD, but rather lives only by the sword; he becomes a completely corrupted nature, which must finally fall victim to its own **Turba** <note>original Latin: *Turbâ*—in Böhmean theology, this refers to the "disturber" or the chaotic, destructive wrath of nature that breaks apart any being that refuses to be transformed by Divine Love.</note>.

The **outer spirit** <note>The "outer spirit" refers to the worldly or sensory mind, as opposed to the inner, spiritual man.</note> must indeed have a little "child-like joy" after the first great **wedding** <note>Referring to the "Parable of the Great Banquet," symbolizing the initial call to a spiritual life.</note>, where GOD invites and compels both the good and the bad; GOD is not opposed to this pastime, provided one does not wish to remain children for long—children who are given sugar and remain clinging to the sugar. GOD completely overturns nature here, and slaughters the tender **little kid** <note>original: *Böcklein*—a metaphor for the stubborn, unruly animal-like nature of the human self-will.</note> of **self-will** and self-desire in the child, as food for the fire of His **righteousness**. The child may resist as long as it wishes; it must fundamentally surrender its will to GOD and sacrifice whatever He wishes to do with the creature in time and eternity. Otherwise, there is no crossing over the **narrow road**, which no **beast** <note>Meaning the "animal man" or the unrefined natural instincts.</note> can tread. There, **Satan** immediately attaches himself to the self-will and reproaches the soul, saying that it walks or prays in its own will, thereby driving it back; however, he cannot do this and has no hold on the soul if it has fundamentally sacrificed its will to God, becoming an **anathema** <note>original Greek: *Anathema*—here used not as a "curse" in the modern sense, but as a "votive offering" or something totally handed over to God's judgment and disposal for the sake of others.</note> for its brothers and all people. Then, GOD’s **righteousness** brings forth a completely different growth from the fire; in such a way that nothing is taken from the soul but its enemy. Instead of this **hideous dragon**, the soul receives an **angel** who, without any hindrance from wrath, anger, hell, or death, can follow the **slaughtered Lamb of GOD** wherever He goes.

<summary>This page describes the difficult spiritual transition from the "child-like" initial joy of faith to the "slaughtering" of the self-will, which allows the soul to transcend the reach of Satan and follow Christ.</summary>

3. We can say that it is a thousand times easier to serve GOD than to serve Satan in the **spirit of the world** <note>German: *Weltgeist*—the collective secular mindset or the driving force of worldly society.</note>, where one must learn everything through nothing but blows and shoves; whereas here, it flows from the divine nature itself: although it falls heavily upon **flesh and blood** <note>Referring to the unregenerate human nature and its physical desires.</note> and costs many a sweat and much anguish. No man knows of this, because GOD dwells between **Cherubim and Seraphim** <note>Traditional high-ranking angelic orders; a reference to God's dwelling in the Holy of Holies, hidden from the profane world.</note>, until the spirit of fire becomes accustomed to it and learns to dwell therein without burning.

4. We will therefore point El. <note>Likely an abbreviation for a recipient’s name, such as Eleonore or Elisabeth.</note> to the narrow door in her spirit, where two ways open up: one goes upward into the senses, out of the **impression** <note>German: *Impression*—in the school of Jakob Böhme, this refers to the "contraction" or hardening of the soul into its own dark, selfish existence.</note>; the other, however, goes into the depths through the anguish and turns inward: where the soul’s spirit can then gather itself in prayer, holding together all the powers of spirit, soul, and body in the will, and—with the hand of the will—constantly carrying and sinking them into Christ and the fiery sea of GOD’s love. There, the soul’s essence is then transformed from one glory to another, according to the image of Him who created her, as the Scripture speaks.

5. The sensory path upward deviates entirely from the **divine center** <note>Latin: *Centro*—the spiritual heart or origin point where God and the soul meet.</note> and leads the spirit into a wide field where the senses cannot grasp GOD at all, because He is incomprehensible to nature. Therefore, people on this path have only a shadow of GOD, of whom they form nothing but foreign ideas. They also know how to speak of **yieldedness** <term>Gelassenheit: a central term in German mysticism meaning the total surrender of the self-will and the "letting go" of one's own desires to make room for God.</term>, **will-lessness**, and all the virtues of the **inner man** (but all as something outside themselves); yet there is fundamentally no divine humility or yieldedness in it; rather, because they cannot reach GOD with their desire, they must **wipe their mouths** <note>A biblical idiom (derived from Proverbs 30:20) describing someone who acts with superficial innocence or makes excuses for their lack of spiritual depth.</note> and then say:

There then, in the depths of the disposition, the dark world of GOD's wrath occurs, with those four elements of darkness: Sin, Death, Devil, and Hell, which lie within one another as a **chaos**; and which the earnest seeker and digger, **David**, immediately discovered and found within himself, when he says: **The bonds of hell surrounded me, the torrents of Belial terrified me; I was overtaken by the snares of death.** <note>Quoting Psalm 18:4-5. In this, the dear God himself has provided for him and taken the roughest work away from Brother St., so that Brother Las. has others at his own station <note>original: *Geding*—a task or place of service</note> who test him and extinguish the fire within him. You must altogether enfold him in your heartfelt love, so his spirit will not desire to depart from you in Magdeburg, but will want to lay down his life with you and for you, and live and die with you. And when one submits to divine order, no one is a torment to the other, but the spirit of one is the medicine <note>original: *Arzney*</note> of the other; just as Brother St. will experience, and he will be rid of all his torment, not knowing how it happens to him: and Brother Las. shall be able to thrive and grow beside him.

### To M. F. R. on the 11th of April, 1709.

1. A true Christian is rare even among the pious: how they are to be found, and how they differ from one another. 2. What advantages the fellowship with inward Christians brings, especially in the battle against the dragon. 3. How this battle is to be conducted within the heavenly womb, Christ. 4. What kind of steadfastness and divine essence is born from it. 5. Its opposite, ideal knowledge, which is child's play but harmful to adults.

It is a great grace of God, as El. <note>likely a reference to a specific correspondent or spiritual source</note> reports, to find a true Christian, because Christ is completely hidden in this world, and one cannot know a Christian unless God Himself reveals them in the mind <note>original: *Gemüth*, referring to the soul's inner disposition, heart, or spiritual consciousness</note>; just as happened to us, for from the childhood age of five, the divine eye opened in the mind, so that I could see that God was nowhere to be found among thousands of people—even at the age of eighteen, not even among the pious with whom I became acquainted; yet my heart could rest in nothing until God brought me into acquaintance with a dear brother: where the Virgin <note>A reference to Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, a central figure in the mystical tradition of Jakob Böhme, which Überfeld followed.</note> opened herself in the mind and called this brother to us by name, in which the <term>essences</term> <note>original: *Essentien*. In this context, these are the spiritual substances or active energies that make up the inner person.</note> of the spirit could be strengthened, so that we have now pulled at one yoke of Christ for twenty-six years. In contrast, with all the other "pious" people, there was a constant disruption of the essences, full of conflict: because God blessed us from the beginning with His childlike spirit of prayer, I had no taste for sensory practice <note>external, ritualistic, or purely intellectual religious exercises</note>; the mind wanted only to have the powers of God, which are birthed through prayer and wrestling. This birth is understood by very few, and they see their minds in a <term>contrario</term> <note>original Latin: *contrario*, meaning a state of opposition or contradiction.</note>, where one wants to go in, and the other wants to go out.

### To H. N. B., May 12, 1709.

1. How the words of men of God should be received if one wishes to understand and benefit from them. 2. What the one hundred and forty-four thousand virgins (Revelation 14) represent. 3. How married people may also participate in their salvation, 4. And overcome Satan within the <term>tincture</term> <note>original: *Tinctur*; in the mystical tradition of Jacob Böhme, the "tincture" is the spiritual life-force or "medicine" that transforms and purifies the soul.</note>.

That God has brought you, together with your wife and child, into our <term>mind</term> <note>original: *Gemüth*, the inner seat of spiritual awareness and emotion</note>, consider this a pure grace of God. This speech has a simple, childlike meaning and needs no explanation. Only learn to distinguish the *speaking of love* from the *speaking of wrath* within you; thus our word will be spirit, power, and life to you, and not a judgment or a snare wherewith your spirit must choke itself; for wrath turns the "Yes" into a mere "No." And so you must always understand all our words in the Light, and grasp and keep them in your heart, so that the devil does not rob you of them and take them from the heart. May God grant you His grace and Holy Spirit for this!

What our dear friend writes of beloved Brother Gichtel, and what she has suffered regarding him, is fundamentally only a fairy tale, invented by the evil spirit to frighten souls away from us. ->To E. W. S. on January 18, 1709.<-

1. How external things become equal and light to an **inward Christian** <term>original: *inwendiger Christ*; a term used in Pietism to describe a believer who focuses on the internal transformation of the soul and a direct, personal relationship with God rather than outward ritual.</term>, and even promote **inward growth** <note>original: *inwendige Gewächs*</note>. 2. How they are thus minded in regard to work, and how one assists the other for their own inward advantage. 3. What it actually is that makes the work so light for them.

The dear Sister has also expressed herself regarding her toil at this same time, which God likewise lightens for us. May the dear God grant strength of body and **soul** <term>original: *Gemüth*; refers to the seat of emotions, will, and character—the "inner man."</term>, so that she is not exhausted under the great burden. It is pleasing to us that we know of it; it can serve us in prayer. For the external mirror clarifies the internal one, and the external and internal are closely linked: where God goes with us from the inner life into the outer life and action, all things become equal to us, and we equal to all things. Whether God goes in or out, we stand in God, and do all things in and with God, so that nothing feels heavy to us, but everything is as light as a feather. In this way, we have worked more in the external in **God’s vineyard** <note>A common biblical metaphor (cf. Matthew 20) for spiritual labor or service to the church community.</note> than we ever did in the world; to God’s praise, and our own growth in **grace** <note>original: *Gnade*</note> and powers, Amen.

2. Therefore our spirit shrinks from nothing, and looks at nothing [with dread], be it in small things or great, so long as God enters into it with us; although the courage is stronger than the strengths, which in the long—

She says that all things fly from her hand, so that she can now accomplish more work in two or three hours than she otherwise could in three or four days, because God is now in her spirit. This is brought about by the **gaze of the Virgin** <note>Refers to the "Virgin Sophia" or Divine Wisdom. In this theology, when the soul is "beheld" by Wisdom, it is transformed and empowered to perform its duties with supernatural ease.</note>; for with her gaze she divinizes our spirit, which is as if it were with the eternal word of divine power—which does not pass away, even though heaven and earth pass away. So it is also with the divine sight: when **Divine Wisdom** <note>original: *göttliche Weisheit*</note> beholds herself in the creature, then God stands in the creature from that moment on, and never leaves it again, and it is said: *Whom he has foreseen, them he also sanctifies.* <note>A paraphrase of Romans 8:30.</note>

### Thorough Instruction Regarding These Accusations.

Our word, which we draw from the **heavenly Mother** <note>Refers to Divine Wisdom or "Sophia," viewed in this tradition as a maternal spiritual principle that feeds and nurtures the soul.</note>, is El.’s <note>Likely referring to the recipient, Maria Elizabeth Richter.</note> mind, as we see: a lovely and pleasant food and a nourishment for the inner man, who transforms it into flesh and blood within himself, which is also called "giving birth"—just as God allows her [Wisdom] to look out from all the words of her pleasant writing, as can be clearly seen. Thus, it is in turn a food for our spirit, which God eats within us. So there is in the Kingdom of God a constant birthing of heavenly powers: the more they are born, the more excellent they become, until God harvests them in our spirit as food for His table or heavenly altar.

2. Of which birth the **world-spirit** <note>The *Weltgeist* represents the mundane, rationalistic, or superficial way of understanding the world, which lacks true spiritual insight.</note> knows nothing, except that the spirit only plays with the "figure" <note>Refers to the outward form or intellectual shell of religious ideas without the living substance.</note>: where the **tinctures** indeed merge into one another, but do not give birth to God; and therefore it is only a **spiritual dalliance** <term>original: *geistliche Buhlerey*; a strong term used to describe a superficial or selfish emotionalism in religion that lacks true commitment.</term> into which Satan finally weaves himself, and from it gives birth to the hellish dragon with hatred, bitterness, anger, and enmity etc., as the child of self-love.

6. We know, praise God! how to distinguish between the speaking of wrath and the speaking of love:

regarding questions which he might still have wished to put to me, had he been able to have the time, I answered that you brothers would explain such things to him, and that everything his soul <note>original: *Gemüth*; a central term in German mysticism referring to the seat of emotions, will, and spiritual disposition.</note> might desire and be able to ask already lay unlocked in what we had spoken to him that morning, provided he would only follow the Spirit within him.

It only costs a "small death" for the flesh, as the natural will must perish.

### To Is. M. on June 27, 1709.

1. The difference between a paternal correction and a chastisement in the fire; also the righteousness and inner life of the spirit that comes from both. 2. How one can partake of the former through a slight overcoming of one's self. 3. The danger in the sharpness of the fire and the necessary caution required, lest one becomes a murderer of souls.

The very same spiritual or divine blessing that has struck Brother Daniel here among us, also strikes El., and you are baptized in your heart with a spirit of divine childship <note>original: *Kindschaft*; the state of being a child of God.</note>: which is so much more blessed than if God had to use sharpness and—according to the Old Covenant—hand over your selfhood <note>original: *Eigenheit*; the stubborn, ego-driven nature of the human will.</note> to the angels or Cherubim <note>Celestial beings often depicted in this tradition as executors of divine justice or guardians of the fire.</note> in the fire to be strangled, and you had to be justified by the sword of God’s righteousness after a long struggle. This righteousness, however, is not as good as that of faith in Christ Jesus; because it does not reach the gates of the spirit in the light—which is deep divine humility, sunk away from the fire: outside of which gates no one can enter into Christ, and

and from which the powers of the inner or heavenly 
world are born. etc.

2. Therefore it is that we have written to you, that you 
should only let our letter <note>original: *Buchstaben*; refers to the "letter" of the word or law, which according to 2 Corinthians 3:6 "kills," while the Spirit gives life.</note> slay you, which is

which is in the Word, 2 Cor. 13:3, would make your spirit 
living again: which is a life of the Holy 
Spirit, far nobler than the first in the renewal of the 
mind; which birth the High Priest **JESUS** 
**Christ** circumcises <note>original: *beschneidet*; in this mystical context, it refers to both spiritual circumcision and the pruning of a vine.</note> with the two-edged sword, 
or knife, in the word of his mouth in the children 
of **God** (wherein **God's** love and wrath stand in 
equality, so that neither cuts sharper than the 
other), but not in the Jewish manner, but rather 
penetrates until it divides soul and spirit, 
also marrow and bone, Heb. 4:12, as the principles 
in the mind, which lie therein as a jumbled mixture. etc.

3. **Br. Dan.** <note>Likely referring to a member of the spiritual circle, "Brother Daniel."</note> has until now only been under sharp 
hands, which use the Father's single-edged knife, 
which according to John 15 takes away the unfruitful branches 
on the vine, Christ, and prunes and cleanses the 
fruitful ones, so that they bring even more fruit. 
Which sharp process a weak mind, that is 
not essentially grafted into Christ and 
cannot draw Christ’s spirit and sap into itself, 
cannot endure. Why it is necessary to handle this 
pruning knife very carefully: and unless he has 
Christ’s spirit and divine understanding, he can do 
more harm than good with it; because one can just 
as easily cut away the good wood as the bad on the vine.
